issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Knowledge tool results spend most of an agent's context on data it rarely uses. In the Knowledge trial (6,800 calls, 57.8M characters), connections alone were 49% of output: full summaries of linked pages, timestamps, paths, repeated metadata and fixed explanatory messages. The tools also carried many presentation options (`view`, `metadataView`, `includeCards`, `includeReferences`, …) that agents had to learn and that are sent with every turn.

## User Impact

User impact: agents get the same answers in about a third of the context, from tools with fewer parameters. Agent tool inputs now select *which* data to read, never how much of each record to show; there is no "full" mode. Lists return 16-character hash prefixes that fence writes directly, and write receipts carry the ontology fingerprint the next write needs. The Control UI, operator inspection and commands still receive complete responses.

**Breaking for agent prompts and skills:** `knowledge_record` drops `view`, `metadataView`, `includeMetadata`, `includeReferences`, `referenceOffset/Limit`, `evidenceLimit`, `maxEvidenceChars`; `knowledge_connections` drops `view`, `includeCards`, `includeEndpoints`; `knowledge_records` drops `includeCards`, `includeEndpoints`. Calls passing them fail input validation with a visible error. Bundled skills are updated.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Agent reads.** `knowledge_record` takes `id`, `offset`, `maxChars`, `includeEvidence`, `evidenceOffset` and returns identity, full hash, body or claim text, aliases, tags, dependencies, non-empty fields, linked pages, subject hint; `maxChars` bounds the whole response by shortening the text (identity and metadata are never cut). Non-high attribution confidence and its basis stay visible; claims carry an occurrence date only, never the ingestion time. Connections and records return shared list rows (`tool-rows.ts`): id, revision, 16-char hash; pages add title/type, claims add kind, day, comment-stripped text (`truncated` past 4,000), linked page titles and source; relationships add from/to.
- **Control UI keeps its options** through UI-only operations `record_detail`, `connections_detail` and `records_detail` (no tool). The agent tools call them with the data the agent asked for (`tool-results.ts`). Shared operations (grep, lookup, timeline, ontology, status, verify, writes) project for `context.source === "tool"` only.
- **Record budget** (`inspection.ts`): under the 24 KiB response budget the body shrinks first; compact domain fields are omitted only when no body text fits beside them (`omitted` lists `metadata.fields`, and the publish skill says to omit `fields` so they are preserved). Each attempt restarts from the whole window, so continuations always advance or end.
- **Receipts:** id, new revision, full hash, `ontologyFingerprint`; state/message only when not published; git only when not committed. `knowledge_mutation`/`knowledge_history` keep complete receipts. `expectedOntologyFingerprint` is unchanged.
- **Hash-prefix fences.** One `hashMatches` (`hash-fence.ts`) at every fence site (storage-edits, storage-lifecycle, storage-publication incl. batch edits, supersede, lifecycle, evidence-reconciliation, verification). Accepts the full hash or a lowercase hex prefix of ≥16 chars; revision must still match; `ExpectedHash` rejects shorter prefixes. **Reasoning:** the fence protects against concurrent and external edits to a record selected by ID, not against forged content; a 64-bit SHA-256 prefix makes an accidental match negligible.
- Link checks move to `knowledge_verify` `expectedLinks`; neighbors to `knowledge_connections`. Removed the old `search-detail.ts` compact-hit path. Docs and skills (regenerated with `sync-skill-references.mjs`) describe the new shapes.

Not changed: JSON serialization (separate core change), `expectedOntologyFingerprint` optionality (undecided), history/mutation/revision/diagnostics/attachment/attach/relink.

**Overlap:** unpushed skill changes on `openclaw-3c9/knowledge-page-curation` (516f9fb67ab6, 7241cff12d9b) edit the same skill files; expect conflicts.

## Evidence

This branch's projection re-run over the trial's real model-visible arm A results (sample averages scaled to arm totals; trial rows measured with the added 16-char hash; record calls measured as `includeEvidence` only, since the other options no longer exist):

| Tool | Calls | Avg now | Avg lean | Lean + compact JSON |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| connections | 1105 | 28358 | 5294 | 28.1M → 4.28M (85%) |
| record | 3141 | 8083 | 3832 | 19.6M → 8.77M (55%) |
| grep | 543 | 11874 | 6916 | 5.47M → 2.72M (50%) |
| annotate | 1211 | 950 | 344 | 66% |
| ontology | 132 | 8770 | 4418 | 62% |
| timeline | 52 | 20061 | 9140 | 61% |
| status | 126 | 1174 | 343 | 74% |
| verify | 125 | 796 | 193 | 79% |
| lookup | 15 | 1228 | 478 | 68% |
| receipts (save/withdraw/supersede/relationship) | — | 912–2142 | 344–660 | 65–82% |
| **Total** | | | | **57.3M → 19.6M lean (66%); 17.3M with compact JSON (70%)** |

Agent tool definitions (input schema + description, all Knowledge tools): 96.0k chars on main → 95.9k; `knowledge_record` 2,707 → 1,220, `knowledge_connections` 1,603 → 1,226, `knowledge_records` 1,932 → 1,618.

Tests: `tool-results.test.ts` drives the registered tools through the real plugin entry and `jsonResult`: default shapes for every read tool and receipt; removed options rejected; `*_detail` UI operations still return complete shapes; `maxChars` bounds page and claim responses with exact reconstruction; fences (16-char prefix accepted; 15-char, wrong, stale-revision and superseded-hash rejected; list-row prefixes fence annotate/withdraw); final page keeps its snapshot; merged IDs collapse; fields, attribution confidence and occurrence dates survive record reads; oversized fields are omitted with a terminating read; lean < 60% of complete.

Runs: full `extensions/knowledge` suite 65/68 files passed (3m33s); the three failing files were tests still calling the renamed operations, fixed and re-run with claim-cards (4/4 passed, 1m27s). At 3c1b046e: tool-results, inspection, records-continuation, retrieval and control-ui pass (5/5). `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test` clean; type-aware oxlint, oxfmt and the assertion-safety ratchet clean; skill sync check and `git diff --check` pass.

Review: the first Astra review found six P2 issues; all fixed with regression tests. A second review of c93786be found five P2s (attribution confidence dropped, `maxChars` described as a hard bound, compact domain fields dropped before the body shrank, stale `view` instructions in conventions and the `knowledge_edit_body` description, ingestion time shown as the claim date); all fixed, with tests red before and green after. A delta review found three continuation defects in the reworked budget; fixed and covered by a regression test. The final delta review found none.

CI repairs: type-aware oxlint (`require-array-sort-compare`, two `no-unnecessary-type-parameters`), two type assertions given `SAFETY` comments, three `as any` test casts removed, and a test-line allocation for this PR's net regression-test growth (`config/test-lines-allocations/196767-knowledge-lean-tool-results.txt`, 645). Head c93786be passed every CI check.

Not run: a live Gateway trial (the originating session reruns it on vault copies).

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Tool results built with core `jsonResult` / `payloadTextResult` reach the model as 2-space pretty-printed JSON, which spends model context on indentation for every tool call. Code Mode makes this worse: the `dispatch_action` envelope escapes the indented text a second time. About 116 non-test files call `jsonResult`. That includes core tools, about 28 bundled plugins, and every feature-plugin tool through `src/plugin-sdk/feature-plugin.ts` (for example, Knowledge).

## User Impact

User impact: agents spend roughly 20–25% fewer tokens on the JSON tool results this changes (about 2.5% of interactive and 8% of all transcript tokens in real sessions; see Evidence), with the same data. `details`, plugin APIs and config are unchanged. Control UI already renders JSON tool results with its own exact-lexeme JSON viewer, so its display is unchanged; Raw/Copy/Download keep the exact compact text. TUI renders JSON tool output literally instead of as Markdown.

## Why This Change Was Made

`jsonResult` and `payloadTextResult` in `src/agents/tools/tool-results.ts` now emit `JSON.stringify(payload)`. This is the single owner of the format. No flag or per-plugin opt-in was added, because no contract needed one: the SDK docs only named the helpers, and they now say the text is compact.

Siblings that copied that formatting, or measured budgets against it, now match the text that is actually sent:

- **Tool Search control results** are always compact. The `compact` option, which only Code Mode passed, is removed. Batch search fitting and the `tool_describe` instructions-hint size check measure compact text.
- **Budget checks** now measure the emitted text. Before, they measured pretty JSON and trimmed too early. This covers `sessions_list` fitting, the sessions patch `resolved` budget (its redundant pretty check is removed), the `plugins` tool result, the gateway `config.get` cap, `update.run` summary diagnostics trimming, and lobster `maxStdoutBytes`.
- **Other model-visible JSON** is compact as well: the raw `web_search` branch, `session_status` route and state-change fenced JSON, `ask_user` and secrets note payloads, bundle LSP and MCP results, and the feishu, github and llm-task plugin result helpers.
- **Display**: Control UI is unchanged; its existing JSON viewer already renders tool-result JSON with exact lexemes, so no display-only reformatting is added. The TUI treats JSON tool output as literal text, as it already did for Code Mode, so Markdown cannot alter values.

Deliberately left unchanged:

- Human-facing output: feature-plugin `registerCommand` text, CLI `--json` output, and files written to disk (manifests, evidence, configs).
- Codex and Agents API native transcript mirrors (`event-projector-tool-items`, `session-catalog-transcript-item`, `agentsapi-native-items`). They mirror another harness's items for display; they are not OpenClaw tool results sent to the model.
- Codex `context-engine-projection` `stableJson`. It feeds Codex's rendered-context budget, which has its own owner and tests and needs separate review against the Codex harness.
- `llm-task` `inputJson`, which is prompt input for a sub-model, not a tool result.
- qa-lab rendering and reports.
- `extensions/knowledge`, where result fields are being trimmed in a separate change.

## Evidence

Model-visible bytes, measured by running representative payloads through the real helpers (`jsonResult`, `feishuExternalToolResult`, `serializeToolSearchControlResult`):

| Result | Before | After | Saved |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Core `sessions_list` (12 rows, `jsonResult`) | 5,999 | 4,711 | 21.5% |
| Channel plugin: feishu doc read (`feishuExternalToolResult`, external-content wrapped) | 7,188 | 3,707 | 48.4% |
| Feature plugin: Knowledge-shaped search (10 hits, `jsonResult`) | 5,079 | 3,673 | 27.7% |
| Code Mode `dispatch_action` envelope around that result | 5,801 | 4,230 | 27.1% |

The payloads are synthetic, but their shapes match production results. Direct-call tools save the indentation only; nested and Code Mode results also lose the escaped indentation. Separately, re-rendering 6,800 real Knowledge results from a trial cut model-visible size from 57.8M to 44.7M chars (−23%).

### Token savings against real sessions

Measured by replaying 996 real local transcripts from the last 10 days (about 330M tokens: interactive dashboard sessions, cron automations and subagents) through current `main` formatting and through this PR. Tokens were counted with `o200k_base` as a proxy tokenizer. The baseline already includes `main`'s compact `dispatch_action` envelope. Shell output, file reads and Code Mode results are unchanged by this PR and count as unchanged.

| Sessions | Count | JSON share of tool tokens | Saving, % of tool tokens | Saving, % of all transcript tokens | Per-session median (p90) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Interactive (dashboard) | 110 | 17% | 3.3% | 2.5% | 2.2% (6.6%) |
| Subagents | 302 | 6.5% | 1.4% | 1.2% | 0.8% (3.6%) |
| Cron automations | 292 | 47% | 10.6% | 10.5% | 10.7% (16.5%) |
| Knowledge-heavy (any kind) | 100 | 82% | 17.4% | 16.1% | 15.9% (20.3%) |
| Code Mode sessions | 36 | 14% | 2.6% | 1.7% | 0.0% (2.8%) |
| All | 996 | 40% | 8.9% | 8.3% | 3.1% (15.0%) |

Results this PR changes lose about 22% of their tokens. The largest absolute savings come from `sessions_list` (−21%), `sessions_history` (−15%), `tool_describe` (−19%) and the `knowledge_*` tools (−15% to −28%). `github_read` is large but saves only about 5%, because its results are mostly file contents in a single string. These are transcript-token figures: compaction and prompt caching change billed tokens, but the relative savings should roughly carry over. A result that hits a size cap uses the same tokens and fits more content.

Tests run locally with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`:

- `src/plugin-sdk/tool-results.test.ts` covers the compact contract. It fails on the base and passes with this change.
- Sibling suites of every edited file pass: tool-search, code-mode, `ask_user`, gateway tool, plugins, secrets, sessions, `session_status`, `web_search`, LSP/MCP bundle, feishu, github, llm-task, TUI tool execution and Control UI tool output.
- Updated exact-text expectations pass: task suggestion, computer refusal, `sessions_list` query, plugins tool, tool-search runtime, scheduled widget, sessions self-archive, browser, feishu docx table, MCP HTTP question authority, worker gateway tool runtime, and the code-mode-json budget.
- A TUI test checks that compact JSON renders literally.
- Final-head rerun of every updated-expectation file plus the MCP/LSP/gateway tool tests (20 files): all pass except `extensions/voice-call/index.test.ts` (EXIT=1, 370s wall). That failure is inherited from `main`: the same file fails the same way on `b21829a4c85f` in a clean worktree ("Voice call service is not running…", service runtime never starts, mock config unset). It does not touch JSON formatting.
- Earlier batches: sibling suites 15 + 3 files pass (225s wall; infra shard re-run after a mid-run source edit, 17 files pass); review-fix batch passes.
- `pnpm check:changed` on the final head (1304s): every lane passes except two that are not caused by this PR. The Plugin SDK surface budget fails the same way on `main`. The dead-export scan reports only files this PR does not touch.

No visual change: Control UI display code is untouched.




CI repair on the final head: the first CI run's failures were all caused by this PR (stale pretty-JSON expectations in `tool-search`, `mcp-http` and `llm-task` tests, a Control UI display reformat that broke the existing exact-lexeme JSON viewer, now reverted, and +4 test lines over the test-lines ratchet, now offset). Focused reruns of every failing file pass locally.

issue.body:
Related: #196138 (design), #196380 and #196402 (landed prerequisites), #196456 (stacked Control UI).

Current head: `3087c8051a103cb117060f80321048b193832c5c`. Targets `main`. **No merge or production deployment is authorized or claimed.** Discovery and loader rollout remain separately gated.

## What Problem This Solves

A claw whose endpoint or Gateway key was lost or may have leaked needs a supported recovery without losing its people, owner devices, nodes, invitations or membership history. A restored backup must also move above the binding Discovery already knows.

## User Impact

On the computer running the claw, the owner runs `openclaw id rebind`, provides an owner-account link code and supplies the recovery kit through a hidden prompt or stdin, never argv. Both keys move together; the owner root and membership remain. The Control UI action follows in #196456. Remote callers are refused. `openclaw id status` reports access and publication; `openclaw id publish --code` can finish publication with a fresh code.

Once the binding commits, a later activation or status-read failure must not look like an uncommitted rotation. The CLI reports the committed binding, warning exit code **2**, and `openclaw id status` as the next step. It explicitly warns against repeating rebind, which would rotate again. No automatic commit retry was introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Prepare stages both keys; repeated preparation reuses them. The CLI verifies Discovery's descriptor under the recovery root and signs above both local and verified published sequences. `--binding-seq` is available when Discovery cannot be read, never below an observed verified binding.
- Authority commits only a root-signed binding naming exactly the staged replacement keys and a higher sequence. Live service/Labs authority is rechecked immediately before persistence. Registration must first be settled under the key Discovery knows.
- Restart promotes the staged keys. A crash after commit completes promotion at the next start. Publication sends descriptor and snapshot together and retains the owner code in memory for retries; missing/expired codes remain visible.
- A root-verified newer Discovery binding reports `binding_superseded`; unverifiable refusal data reports `discovery_integrity`. Pins and followers use the existing signed-binding protocol.
- The settlement repair removes a redundant postcommit pending-state write: binding-sequence lag already owns that fact. Recorded startup failures and thrown follow-up errors now retain `moved:true`, with `published:null`, `followUpError`, and a safe next step. Both CLI and companion UI consume that outcome.

Design decisions preserved: both keys move, an owner-account code authorizes publication, verified published sequence is respected, and the ceremony is local-only. Discovery must support atomic descriptor/snapshot publication before Gateway rollout. Owner-account notification remains outside this PR.

## Evidence

### Current repair

- Regression-first: postcommit bookkeeping/restart and CLI warning cases fail before the repair. Independent Astra review found that normal tunnel-start failures were caught into service status rather than thrown; a real-service-composition regression reproduced that missing warning before it was fixed.
- Settlement repair at `2434f64e61c8`: **40/40** focused service, publication-retry, actual local-Gateway rebind/crash, and registered CLI tests passed in **101.03s**. Command: `pnpm test src/gateway/openclaw-id/service.rebind.test.ts src/cli/id-cli.commands.test.ts src/gateway/server.openclaw-id-rebind.test.ts src/gateway/openclaw-id/publication-retry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Core and affected test-shard typechecks, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, diff checks and exact test-line allocation pass. The settlement allocation is **149**, matching net test growth without added slack. The earlier CLI mock/type repair allocation is **192**.
- Fresh independent Astra P0–P2 source reassessment found no verified findings. The committed patch exactly matches the reviewed and locally tested snapshot. This was a narrative independent review, not independent test execution or live acceptance.
- Existing protocol/authority proofs cover signature, sequence, staged-key and lifetime refusal boundaries. The server rebind test's positive and crash cases launch a real local Gateway; its relayed-client denial assertion invokes the handler directly with a fixture. **That assertion is not an actual relayed request through the running Gateway.**
- A final-head staging attempt was performed and stopped during browser owner enrollment, before the requested denial/lifetime proofs. The exact fresh fixture was retired, an independent authenticated descriptor read returned 404, private state was removed, and the canonical lock was released. This is cleanup success, not acceptance success. Historical integrated receipts below retain their original execution revisions.

### Type-only CI follow-up

At `2434f64e61c8`, [CI run 42877734773](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42877734773) completed with a Madge import-cycle failure: `service-rebind-owner → service-rebind → service`. The final head moves the unchanged status union into a leaf type contract and updates its two consumers. It changes no runtime statements or authorization behavior.

- The actual failing Madge gate now reports **0 cycles**.
- Production and owning Gateway-test types, three-file type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks pass.
- Focused service, publication-retry and registered CLI checks: **38/38 passed**, two shards in **88.00s**. The earlier invocation hit its outer command deadline and is not credited as a pass; its owned processes were confirmed stopped before the completed run.
- The same independent Astra reviewer verified the frozen three-file delta and unchanged status union: **no verified P0–P2 findings**. Review did not independently execute tests.
- Final-head real-relayed refusal and ended-lifetime persistence acceptance remain blocked by the owner-enrollment timeout described below. No passing final-head staging acceptance is claimed.

### Final-head staging attempt: enrollment blocked, cleanup verified

The exact `3087c8051a103cb117060f80321048b193832c5c` Gateway ran against the verified staging deployment window under one canonical lock. Dedicated owner sign-in succeeded. Before requesting a link code, account-authenticated `GET /v1/access` returned HTTP 200 with the exact selected email and `preview_access: true`. Initial publication and an authenticated descriptor read succeeded at binding 1.

The browser reached the new claw origin and the loader's `enrolling` phase. Opening recovery-kit entry succeeded, but filling `#kit-input` timed out. The retained safe error identifies that exact operation; it does not establish why the input was unavailable. The deployed loader's source provenance remains unknown. No extra fixture, retry, product fix or deployment was performed to work around this failure.

**Not reached:** successful remote owner enrollment, actual relayed rebind refusal, ended-lifetime refusal, and the new authorized rebind positive control. Their acceptance gates remain open; final hosted re-review is held.

After the failure, the Gateway exited with code 0 and the private browser closed. Only then was the exact new fixture retired through the supported service path. Read-only service verification found zero claw/member/relay rows and the exact hostname marked retired. The proof independently fetched the descriptor with its account session and received 404, removed its private state, and released the canonical lock. Parent verification confirmed the owned processes/listener and private directory were absent and the lock was available. Redacted final fields:

```json
{
  "proofPassed": false,
  "failureStage": "real-relay-owner-enrollment",
  "failureName": "TimeoutError",
  "authenticatedDescriptorStatus": 404,
  "processCleanupConfirmed": true,
  "privateCleanupConfirmed": true,
  "localCleanupConfirmed": true
}
```

Cleanup completed on 2026-11-10 at 21:04:07 UTC. Service/image metadata is not a loaded-binary attestation. No merge or production deployment is claimed.

### Exact-head CI

The final `3087c8051a10` push uses normal PR CI, not a broad manual dispatch. These are observed states, not a claim that queued/running checks passed. Merge/deployment holds remain.

- [CodeQL](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42882708607): in_progress
- [macOS Periphery Dead Code [report]](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42882708839): in_progress
- [OpenGrep — PR Diff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42882708781): in_progress
- [Workflow Sanity](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42882708882): in_progress
- [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42882709491): in_progress
- [CodeQL Critical Quality](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42882708673): in_progress
- [PR context and evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42882704819): completed / success
- [Auto response](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42882704845): in_progress
- [Labeler](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42882704815): completed / success
- [ClawSweeper Dispatch](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42882704840): completed / success
- [Security Review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42882704714): in_progress

## Redacted integrated acceptance evidence (2026-11-10)

The excerpts below retain original result-field names and values, with identity, endpoint, credential and operator-path fields omitted. They show bounded outcomes, not a claim that every authority-denial case passed.

**Executed revisions:** the Gateway build, restart runs and restored-state publisher used `f864514d93a08efda68c14eabc42768f081af854`. The repaired CLI and native snapshot-ahead run used `f08fea43c6979223ebf44f8b05020dd3033414ea`. These are historical execution revisions, not the final heads of PR #196388 or #196456. Later source repairs and restacks require their own qualification.

### Wrong recovery kit: observed binding did not change

The actual registered CLI rejected an unrelated recovery kit at binding 2. A subsequent authenticated read compared the **complete binding object** with its pre-attempt value. Supported cancellation then succeeded. This establishes the wrong-kit case's bounded binding outcome; preparation can stage keys, so it does not mean that no temporary state was created.

```json
{
  "bindingBefore": 2,
  "wrongKit": {
    "case": "wrong_kit",
    "ok": false,
    "category": "wrong-kit",
    "exit": 1,
    "movedOutput": false,
    "publishedOutput": false
  },
  "wrongKitBindingUnchanged": true,
  "stagedCancellationAccepted": true,
  "cancel": {"ok": true, "exit": 0}
}
```

The encompassing run has `passed: false`: a **later, separate** correct-kit CLI invocation returned an error after committing binding 2→3. That later error is not denial evidence. The chronology attributes this pre-repair CLI run to `f864514d93a08efda68c14eabc42768f081af854`; the outer receipt pins that Gateway revision, but the wrong-kit subresult contains no independent CLI-source SHA.

The missing-code receipt contains only this CLI input-validation result:

```json
{"case":"missing_code","ok":false,"category":"missing-link-code","errorClass":"Error"}
```

It contains no binding readback, RPC count, retained exit field or embedded source revision. It is not independent final-effect denial evidence and does not prove a server-side authority check.

A claw whose endpoint or Gateway key was lost or may have leaked needs a supported recovery without losing its people, owner devices, nodes, invitations or membership history. A restored backup must also move above the binding Discovery already knows.

## User Impact

On the computer running the claw, the owner runs `openclaw id rebind`, provides an owner-account link code and supplies the recovery kit through a hidden prompt or stdin, never argv. Both keys move together; the owner root and membership remain. The Control UI action follows in #196456. Remote callers are refused. `openclaw id status` reports access and publication; `openclaw id publish --code` can finish publication with a fresh code.

Once the binding commits, a later activation or status-read failure must not look like an uncommitted rotation. issue.body:
Related: #196138 (re-bind design, "Key files at every start")

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a linked claw silently creates a new endpoint key or Gateway key when its key file is lost (disk loss, a restore that skipped `openclaw-id/`, an accidental delete), then publishes and signs under keys its owner-signed server binding does not name, which strands every device.

## User Impact

User impact: when a linked claw's key file is missing or holds a different key, OpenClaw ID remote access stays off with status `keys_refused` (`key: endpoint | gateway`, `reason: keys_missing | key_mismatch`). Nothing is created, published, signed or dialed with another key. The Gateway itself keeps running, so everything on the machine works as before. Restoring the original key file brings remote access back. The way to move a claw to new keys (`openclaw id rebind`) follows in a stacked PR. Unlinked Gateways create keys exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Once a claw is linked, its stored binding is the only record of which K_srv and K_gw are current. At every start the Gateway (for K_gw) and the tunnel child (for K_srv, via `expectedEndpointKey` in its start message) use the key file only when its seed derives the bound public key. Otherwise they promote a staged `<file>.next` only if *its* seed derives the bound key, so a planted file is never used, and if neither matches they refuse. The re-bind uses that `.next` promotion to finish an interrupted commit. The child exits with new codes 76/75, which the supervisor does not retry. The Gateway never reads the K_srv file.

Owner decision for this fix: the Gateway is not blocked from starting, and nothing in startup or Doctor treats this state as fatal.

<details><summary>Notes for reviewers</summary>

- `claw-name-check.ts` and `service-gateway-key.ts` are extracted from `service.ts` (max-lines). Name-check behavior is unchanged, and the lifetime signal is still captured on admission.
- The tunnel child's K_srv requirement survives authority withdrawn after an uncertain store write. It keeps the last bound K_srv rather than falling back to the unlinked "create" start (from the independent review).
- Test fixtures: `linkedClaw()` now writes its K_gw seed into a per-claw state dir. Several existing tests relied on the bug, because the Gateway minted a key for a linked claw.

</details>

## Evidence

- Real Gateway (`src/gateway/server.openclaw-id-keys.test.ts`). A linked claw with `gateway.key` gone returns `keys_refused/gateway/keys_missing`, with no key files created and `health` still answering. With `endpoint.key` gone, the real tunnel child returns `keys_refused/endpoint/keys_missing` and creates no key. **Both fail on `main`** (status `on`, keys minted).
- Real tunnel child: it serves on the bound key and promotes a staged key the binding names. This shows the Ed25519 seed→pubkey derivation equals iroh's endpoint id.
- Service: K_gw missing or mismatched means no `fetch`, no file, and `publish()` → `failed keys_missing`. A local membership change is still accepted and stays pending for publication. Red on `main`.
- Key rule matrix (`keyfile.test.ts`): match, staged match, missing, mismatch, and a planted staged key that is not promoted. Supervisor: 76/75 are not retried.
- Withdrawn-authority restart regression: red without the fix, green with it.
- Link-commit regression: a Gateway that starts unlinked and links, then has its authority withdrawn by an uncertain write before any child restart reads the binding. The restart getter still returns the committed K_srv. Red without the fix, green with it (ClawSweeper P2/security).
- Recovery copy (log lines and docs/concepts/experimental-features.md): restore the original key files, **then restart the Gateway**. After a refusal the supervisor does not retry, so restoring the file alone does not bring remote access back (ClawSweeper P2).
- `linkedClaw` key directories are tracked and removed after each test file (ClawSweeper P3).
- Still open: runtime proof with an isolated Gateway and a stable-upgrade check. These run with the staging live proof.
- `src/gateway/openclaw-id` suite green, plus `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:ui`, oxlint and format. Inherited failure: `server.auth.openclaw-id-node-host.test.ts` "both streaming transfer routes use the same private bridge" fails identically on `main` in this environment.



## Initial-link uncertain settlement correction

`a71dce7` addresses the new current-head P2: the initial link may be durable even when its acknowledgement and reconciliation read both fail. The service now retains the supervisor-reported running K_srv before awaiting link settlement, rather than only after a successful return. It does not trust caller-supplied binding data or restore withdrawn authority. A readable binding still wins; a refused link attempt conservatively retains the already-running endpoint constraint for that process. Fresh unlinked startups remain unchanged.

The existing withdrawn-authority regression now covers both the initial-link and later-write cases. The initial case verifies the persisted binding, withdrawn authority and endpoint constraint delivered to the next child start. It fails on `3c40bfb` (getter returns undefined) and passes with this change. Focused service/keyfile/name/real-Gateway lost-key suites: 5 files, 20/20 tests. Core typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, format, diff check and the test-lines ratchet pass. Fresh independent source review found no P0–P2 findings. The test matrix reuses the existing fixture; production repair moves one assignment before settlement without introducing another owner or state field.

This regression reads the real service's restart-key getter with the native child mocked. <summary>New exact-head local run: real child refuses mismatched current/staged keys before IP I/O</summary>

{"mode":"staged","result":"passed","exitCode":76,"readyMessages":0}

Only persistence was fault-injected through the authority's store interface: write the JSON record to the throwaway profile, then throw the acknowledgement error; the reconciliation read also throws. This is a real on-disk write with injected acknowledgement/read failure, **not a SQLite crash/durability qualification or full Gateway-process restart**. Unrelated membership side effects were inert fixture callbacks.

Procedure: start genuinely unlinked; let the native child bind and report its running endpoint; create valid owner-signed initial-link statements for that endpoint; call production `service.commitLink`; observe the persisted binding and withdrawn authority; place nonmatching current and staged seeds in the isolated profile; kill only the owned native child; let the unchanged production supervisor restart it.

Owned service/children were stopped at run end; product source and historical proof refs were not changed.

## Current qualification — November 10

Current head: `829e19d639a00337ea755797d4ef731f439a0525`, stacked on #196388 at `3087c8051a103cb117060f80321048b193832c5c` (`feat/ocid-owner-rebind`). **Readiness is authorized solely to start normal PR CI. ### Normal CI — current head

Attempt 1 of normal run [42885829576](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42885829576) ended in **failure** at this head. At 2026-11-10T20:30:13Z, one explicitly authorized **rerun of failed jobs** was accepted as a flake check—not retry-until-green. Both exact cases passed on attempt 2: [attachment focus, 4195 ms](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42885829576/job/130108897118) and [Fast/Ultrafast persistence, 3782 ms](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42885829576/job/130108896958). Both newly executed jobs finished successfully; the original failures and their unresolved attribution remain recorded below. No second rerun was requested. The requested audit of 20 terminal main runs and 10 recent other-PR runs is complete. No matching failure was found in that bounded sample, but only one main run actually executed each case: both passed in [main run 42885152368](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42885152368) at `0c5c4754c33dd9a9e7f4eb4493d4472d458a4609` ([attachment: 2347 ms, shard 6/7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42885152368/job/130072036378); [quick-thinking: 3798 ms, shard 2/7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42885152368/job/130072036380)). The other 19 main runs had skipped UI matrices or no jobs. Only one other-PR run executed both cases; both passed before that run was cancelled. No log retrieval remains pending. This is not proof of branch-wide absence or PR causality. With no matching main-failure evidence, these remain PR-owned for the requested full-shard/worker comparison against main, even if the single rerun passes. Both rerun cases must pass and matching main-history failures must exist before calling them pre-existing flakes. Otherwise they remain owned by this PR for CI-like concurrent reproduction and repair; no assertions will be weakened.

The original failing test jobs are:

- [UI E2E 6/7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42885829576/job/130074852343): `config-quick-thinking-persistence.e2e.test.ts:116`, Fast checked-state expected `true`, received `false` after the patch request was observed (634 cases passed, one failed).

Final hosted re-review remains held pending disposition; the stack and landing hold remain unchanged.

- Owner People events refresh the open menu. A rejected refresh retains an established warning and remedy within its owner scope; client/revision replacement retires that scope without leaking old warnings or late replies.

Historical integrated acceptance below keeps its original revisions and limitations. Final-head real-relayed/lifetime proof is being coordinated in the parent ceremony lane, not claimed here.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on the computer that runs a claw, the Control UI had no way to move it to new keys, and it never said why remote access stopped when a key file was lost or newer keys were published elsewhere. Only `openclaw id rebind` and `openclaw id status` could tell or fix that.

## User Impact

User impact: the owner can recover a claw with lost or leaked keys from the browser, with the recovery code and their signed-in account. The account menu and system Inbox show each key problem with its fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Account menu, this computer only:** offers **Move to new keys** while signed in with OpenClaw ID.
- **Dialog flow:**
  - the link code comes from the signed-in account (`account_link_code`), with nothing to paste;
  - the recovery code typed in the browser derives R, which signs the staged keys' binding;
  - the J7 check of Discovery's published binding runs in the browser;
  - the owner confirms the owner, endpoint and Gateway key fingerprints, then `rebind_commit` stores the binding and publishes it.
- **Signing owner:** `signRebind` moves from `src/cli` into the protocol package, so the CLI and the browser share one implementation.
- **Warnings with fixes:**
  - `keys_refused`: a key file is missing or doesn't match;
  - `binding_superseded`: Discovery lists newer keys;
  - `needs_link_code`: new keys aren't published yet, with **Publish new keys**, which also uses the account's code.

Stacked on #196388 (`feat/ocid-owner-rebind`).

## Changes
- `packages/openclaw-id-protocol/src/enrollment/rebind.ts`: `signRebind`, moved from `src/cli/id-cli-rebind.ts` together with its tests.
- `ui/src/lib/openclaw-id/rebind.ts`: prepare/sign, commit, cancel and publish-with-code. A non-kit string is refused before anything is staged.
- `ui/src/components/openclaw-id/move-keys-dialog.tsx`: the dialog.
- `account-menu.tsx` and `identity-menu.tsx`: warning rows and actions. The publication state is read from `openclawId.people`, owner-only, on this computer.
- `docs/cli/id.md`: describes the Control UI path.

All data is synthetic, from the mocked Gateway.

**Tests:**
- `ui/src/e2e/openclaw-id-move-keys.e2e.test.ts` (mocked Gateway, real Chromium), 2/2:
  - the three warnings each show their action;
  - the dialog sends exactly `account_link_code`, `rebind_prepare`, `rebind_commit`, and the committed binding is signed by the kit's root with the account's code.
- `ui/src/lib/openclaw-id/rebind.test.ts`: real kit signing that verifies under R, a non-kit refused before any request, and another claw's kit refused.
- `account-menu.test.tsx`: the warnings appear only on this computer, and Publish uses the account's code.
- Results:
  - Earlier-head UI unit suites for OpenClaw ID: 79/79;
  - protocol `rebind.test.ts`: 5/5, moved from the CLI;
  - the existing account-menu e2e test still passes;
  - `tsgo:ui`, oxlint, stylelint, the controller guard and the i18n baseline are clean.

**Review fixes:**
- **Dismissal during a running step (P2):** Escape or the backdrop during a running check or commit is refused, so a move that completes is never reported as cancelled. `move-keys-dialog.test.tsx` fails on the previous head and passes now.
- **Signing before confirmation (P2), not changed:** the binding is still signed at **Check**, as in `openclaw id rebind`. The signature stays in browser memory and is sent only by **Move to new keys**; Cancel discards it. Signing later would mean keeping the recovery code in memory until confirmation, which is worse custody for no protection gained.
- **Secret handling on close:**
  - The kit secret S and the derived seed are byte arrays, zeroed inside `signRebind`.
  - R is a non-extractable CryptoKey, dropped after signing.
  - The typed recovery code and the signed binding are JS strings, which can't be overwritten. Cancel, close and a finished move release them and scrub the input field.

**Not covered:**
- Historical integrated staging evidence appears below; final-head real-relayed and lifetime proof remains outstanding.
- The new Inbox screenshots have been inspected locally; the images above show the earlier account-menu/dialog surfaces, not the Inbox.




## Earlier account-lifetime repair

A checked plan now retains its original account/sign-out custody, rechecked against the account owner's live storage immediately before `rebind_commit`, including before another tab's storage event. Sign-out/account replacement retires the confirmation and releases the recovery text, code and signed plan. Late Check results cannot republish into a disposed dialog. Fresh-code publication also rechecks custody before sending. The account guard is shared with link-code retrieval rather than duplicating account authority in the dialog.

Retirement after a commit has already been dispatched keeps its settlement visible: success resolves true, and a failure after retirement produces an error notice before resolving false. Labs-off no longer silently disposes a pending commit.

Proof: the re-bind tests now use the real account owner, not a mocked account-code provider. Both cross-tab commit regressions fail before the repair and pass afterward. The focused real-account/menu/dialog suites pass 34/34; the Chromium J7/move-keys e2e passes 2/2. Typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, controller guard and allocation checks pass. Fresh independent review: the feature-disposal finding was repaired and rechecked, with no remaining P0–P2 findings. Existing publication-code retry/persistence is independently covered by Gateway service tests; the menu's forwarding assertion is not claimed as publication behavior proof.

No layout or copy changes in this repair. Existing sanitized dialog/banner screenshots remain applicable. Staging account/Discovery proof and stable-upgrade qualification remain outstanding.

## Inbox recovery and asynchronous publication

At `d8bbb616302b`, missing, mismatched, and superseded keys also appear in the system Inbox on this computer, with recovery guidance and the Move to new keys action. Owner, connection, scope, and Labs changes fence stale reads. Publication settlement refreshes the warning through the existing owner-authorized People event, including refusals without an owner account ID. A successful delayed publication clears the warning; a later superseded binding creates it.

Validation on the reviewed source tree:
- Gateway publication suite: 10 passed. The deferred-refusal notification regression failed before the repair and passed afterward.
- Focused sidebar/attention/account-menu suites: 51 passed; account-menu 17 passed again after the final error-wrapper correction.
- Real Chromium with mocked Gateway: 2 passed, now retaining the warning after commit until delayed publication emits its event.
- UI typecheck and scoped core/UI type-aware lint passed; the full affected-UI lint retained four existing Solid warnings.
- Review evidence correction resolved by a fresh independent Astra review of exact commit `d8bbb616302b` against `a6663b26ecc1`: no verified P0–P2 findings across the complete 40-file diff. The reviewer confirmed both sides of publication-settlement invalidation, account custody and signer extraction. Report SHA-256 `bae89ccb89e9f00ae0a7e61273a831c00397cc288c5070d0171c529f7818c95b`; reviewed binary-diff SHA-256 `683e43427c2dbd8077e796181c0365da6e3d1f64387ffa385221ee0dff7584f0`, independently matched after delivery. This narrative review used instruction-enforced read-only access, not helper sandbox certification. It ran signing smoke assertions and diff checks, not full suites or live proof. It replaces reliance on the earlier unretrievable follow-up report.
- Exact PR test-line allocation: 767; no allocation added for inherited baseline debt.

The committed tree was verified byte-for-byte against the reviewed patch. These checks do not establish current-head hosted CI or live Discovery proof. The PR remains draft. A separate combined proof branch includes the per-key freshness changes without changing this PR's base. Live staging, replacement-tunnel, and stable-upgrade proof remain outstanding.


## Historical same-host bundle budget attribution

Reviewed candidate `5ba2144b8c9d` is now published; local, remote branch and PR head match. Independent Astra delta review found no verified P0–P2 issues and confirmed the cold-menu repair. The earlier full review covers `93a5336cbc05`; the final review covers its four-file delta, not a rerun of the full review. Review of the first reduction (`93a5336cbc05`) found a missing stylesheet on cold account-menu recovery; this candidate explicitly imports the shared stylesheet from the lazy dialog. It does not rely on opening Inbox first.

Measurements use separate Studio checkouts, Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, frozen dependency installs and `pnpm build:runtime`. Base and pinned-main builds reproduced their prior measurements. The final repaired candidate was rebuilt. Bytes below are normalized gzip unless marked raw.

| Startup JS | 91,884 | 91,884 | 91,884 | 91,888 | 0 |

| New boot JS | 803,821 | 806,370 | 806,343 | 803,766 | +2,522 |
| All CSS gzip | 326,469 | 326,673 | 326,488 | 326,509 | +19 |
| All CSS raw | 1,681,996 | 1,682,398 | 1,682,080 | 1,682,167 | +84 |

On November 10, Josh approved the remaining JavaScript cost for owner warnings that remote access is off or keys have moved, as relayed by the coordinator. Only the measured increase over the actual PR base is added to each exceeded JS cap:

| JS cap | Before | Approved increase | After | Remaining inherited overage |

The largest ordinary chunk measures 564,758 bytes on base and 567,285 on the candidate. No inherited overage is absorbed. No CSS, startup, request-count or dependency limit changes. Both fixed CSS ceilings pass: 326,575 gzip and 1,682,231 raw bytes. Pinned main has a different chat cap and is not the PR baseline.

The reduction removes the custom dialog stylesheet and reuses metadata-row styles, with an explicit lazy import for cold-menu access. It also consolidates warning construction. Signing, recovery-kit derivation and dialog copy were already lazy; they were not the source of boot growth. The remaining increase supplies missing/mismatched/superseded key warnings, recovery actions, and owner/connection-scoped refresh after publication settles.

Validation: the new cold-menu regression first reproduced four unstyled block rows, then passed with the repair. All three Chromium cases pass, covering cold account menu, Inbox recovery and delayed publication refresh against a mocked Gateway. UI typecheck, focused type-aware lint, all 50 performance-checker tests and the exact-base test-lines ratchet pass. Test allocation increases by the regression's 16 net lines; inherited allocation debt is not absorbed. Prior reduction unit coverage was 20/20.

The fresh synthetic cold-menu confirmation screenshot was visually inspected: labels, old/new fingerprints, binding sequence and trailing confirmation action are visible. Evidence: `/tmp/ocid-rollout-evidence/cold-menu-green/dialog-confirm-account-menu.png` (local, not an uploaded attachment or live Gateway proof). Studio and Linux dialog source SHA-256 match: `dda4ea65e0cd27669aa567a452df413876fe0b10be6e980e444f943fbad59750`. Hosted exact-head CI and live staging proof remain outstanding. The PR remains draft; passing performance-checker tests do not mean the strict bundle budget passes—the three inherited JS overages remain as disclosed.

## Integrated staging acceptance and final cleanup — November 10

This closes the earlier pending same-claw staging run, not exact-head hosted CI or every PR-specific test gap. The isolated Gateway used combined source `f864514d93a08efda68c14eabc42768f081af854`; the repaired registered CLI used `f08fea43c6979223ebf44f8b05020dd3033414ea`. These are integrated proof refs, not the individual PR heads.

- Actual Control UI rotation **1→2** committed and published, preserving the root and admitted native node (`studio-ui-rebind-v4-call-result.json`).
- The earlier CLI **2→3** committed but reported failure; that defect remains recorded above/in #196388. A deliberately new repaired CLI **3→4** exited **0**, reported `moved:true`/`published:true`, and authenticated readback confirmed binding/published 4. Root, two owner certificates and membership remained intact (`studio-cli4-owner-follow-call-result.json`).
- The same persistent remote owner browser and saved native node followed **3→4** and reconnected after a separate actual Gateway restart. Production SQLite trust load showed pin/freshness 4 before native dialing; `system.which(uname)` passed (`studio-cli4-restart-call-result.json`). This does not retroactively prove owner-browser following of each earlier rotation.
- Actual native transport with copied real node trust refused a signed snapshot claiming binding 4 under verified binding 3 as `snapshot_ahead`, without advancing pin/freshness or connecting. This used an isolated signed HTTP fixture, not a malicious write to staging (`studio-snapshot-ahead-native-result.json`).
- Production `readStoredClaw`/`publishClaw` used real old binding-3 SQLite and keys against staging: HTTP 409 `stale_binding` carried binding 4, verified under the root, producing non-retryable `binding_superseded`. Current-key authentication succeeded before/after; current Gateway/native/owner recovery then passed. This is persisted-state/publisher integration, **not a full old-Gateway boot** (`studio-rollback3-publisher-result.json`, `studio-post-rollback4-recovery-call-result.json`).
- Final exact-claw retirement completed once; database checks showed no claw/member/relay-key rows and a reserved retired hostname. Independent existing-owner authentication obtained descriptor **404**. Owned processes/listeners/transports were absent; private Studio/fsn1 profiles, snapshots, keys and kit copies were removed, with tracked checkouts clean. The original lock holder exited 0, the same canonical lock was verified available, and four reservation-owner release notices were queued. No merge or production deployment occurred.

**Shipped older-writer limitation:** the remotely verified latest stable `v2026.11.2` and beta `v2026.11.5-beta.1` examined here contain neither `src/gateway/openclaw-id` nor `packages/openclaw-id-protocol`. This is not an exhaustive statement about every historical release. See `shipped-old-writer-feasibility.json`.

issue.body:
Related: #196138 (design), #196380 and #196402 (landed prerequisites), #196456 (stacked Control UI).

Current head: `3087c8051a103cb117060f80321048b193832c5c`. Targets `main`. **No merge or production deployment is authorized or claimed.** Discovery and loader rollout remain separately gated.

## What Problem This Solves

A claw whose endpoint or Gateway key was lost or may have leaked needs a supported recovery without losing its people, owner devices, nodes, invitations or membership history. A restored backup must also move above the binding Discovery already knows.

## User Impact

On the computer running the claw, the owner runs `openclaw id rebind`, provides an owner-account link code and supplies the recovery kit through a hidden prompt or stdin, never argv. Both keys move together; the owner root and membership remain. The Control UI action follows in #196456. Remote callers are refused. `openclaw id status` reports access and publication; `openclaw id publish --code` can finish publication with a fresh code.

Once the binding commits, a later activation or status-read failure must not look like an uncommitted rotation. The CLI reports the committed binding, warning exit code **2**, and `openclaw id status` as the next step. It explicitly warns against repeating rebind, which would rotate again. No automatic commit retry was introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Prepare stages both keys; repeated preparation reuses them. The CLI verifies Discovery's descriptor under the recovery root and signs above both local and verified published sequences. `--binding-seq` is available when Discovery cannot be read, never below an observed verified binding.
- Authority commits only a root-signed binding naming exactly the staged replacement keys and a higher sequence. Live service/Labs authority is rechecked immediately before persistence. Registration must first be settled under the key Discovery knows.
- Restart promotes the staged keys. A crash after commit completes promotion at the next start. Publication sends descriptor and snapshot together and retains the owner code in memory for retries; missing/expired codes remain visible.
- A root-verified newer Discovery binding reports `binding_superseded`; unverifiable refusal data reports `discovery_integrity`. Pins and followers use the existing signed-binding protocol.
- The settlement repair removes a redundant postcommit pending-state write: binding-sequence lag already owns that fact. Recorded startup failures and thrown follow-up errors now retain `moved:true`, with `published:null`, `followUpError`, and a safe next step. Both CLI and companion UI consume that outcome.

Design decisions preserved: both keys move, an owner-account code authorizes publication, verified published sequence is respected, and the ceremony is local-only. Discovery must support atomic descriptor/snapshot publication before Gateway rollout. Owner-account notification remains outside this PR.

## Evidence

### Current repair

- Regression-first: postcommit bookkeeping/restart and CLI warning cases fail before the repair. Independent Astra review found that normal tunnel-start failures were caught into service status rather than thrown; a real-service-composition regression reproduced that missing warning before it was fixed.
- Settlement repair at `2434f64e61c8`: **40/40** focused service, publication-retry, actual local-Gateway rebind/crash, and registered CLI tests passed in **101.03s**. Command: `pnpm test src/gateway/openclaw-id/service.rebind.test.ts src/cli/id-cli.commands.test.ts src/gateway/server.openclaw-id-rebind.test.ts src/gateway/openclaw-id/publication-retry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Core and affected test-shard typechecks, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, diff checks and exact test-line allocation pass. The settlement allocation is **149**, matching net test growth without added slack. The earlier CLI mock/type repair allocation is **192**.
- Fresh independent Astra P0–P2 source reassessment found no verified findings. The committed patch exactly matches the reviewed and locally tested snapshot. This was a narrative independent review, not independent test execution or live acceptance.
- Existing protocol/authority proofs cover signature, sequence, staged-key and lifetime refusal boundaries. The server rebind test's positive and crash cases launch a real local Gateway; its relayed-client denial assertion invokes the handler directly with a fixture. **That assertion is not an actual relayed request through the running Gateway.**
- A final-head staging attempt was performed and stopped during browser owner enrollment, before the requested denial/lifetime proofs. The exact fresh fixture was retired, an independent authenticated descriptor read returned 404, private state was removed, and the canonical lock was released. This is cleanup success, not acceptance success. Historical integrated receipts below retain their original execution revisions.

### Type-only CI follow-up

At `2434f64e61c8`, [CI run 42877734773](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42877734773) completed with a Madge import-cycle failure: `service-rebind-owner → service-rebind → service`. The final head moves the unchanged status union into a leaf type contract and updates its two consumers. It changes no runtime statements or authorization behavior.

- The actual failing Madge gate now reports **0 cycles**.
- Production and owning Gateway-test types, three-file type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks pass.
- Focused service, publication-retry and registered CLI checks: **38/38 passed**, two shards in **88.00s**. The earlier invocation hit its outer command deadline and is not credited as a pass; its owned processes were confirmed stopped before the completed run.
- The same independent Astra reviewer verified the frozen three-file delta and unchanged status union: **no verified P0–P2 findings**. Review did not independently execute tests.
- Final-head real-relayed refusal and ended-lifetime persistence acceptance remain blocked by the owner-enrollment timeout described below. No passing final-head staging acceptance is claimed.

### Final-head staging attempt: enrollment blocked, cleanup verified

The exact `3087c8051a103cb117060f80321048b193832c5c` Gateway ran against the verified staging deployment window under one canonical lock. Dedicated owner sign-in succeeded. Before requesting a link code, account-authenticated `GET /v1/access` returned HTTP 200 with the exact selected email and `preview_access: true`. Initial publication and an authenticated descriptor read succeeded at binding 1.

The browser reached the new claw origin and the loader's `enrolling` phase. Opening recovery-kit entry succeeded, but filling `#kit-input` timed out. The retained safe error identifies that exact operation; it does not establish why the input was unavailable. The deployed loader's source provenance remains unknown. No extra fixture, retry, product fix or deployment was performed to work around this failure.

**Not reached:** successful remote owner enrollment, actual relayed rebind refusal, ended-lifetime refusal, and the new authorized rebind positive control. Their acceptance gates remain open; final hosted re-review is held.

After the failure, the Gateway exited with code 0 and the private browser closed. Only then was the exact new fixture retired through the supported service path. Read-only service verification found zero claw/member/relay rows and the exact hostname marked retired. The proof independently fetched the descriptor with its account session and received 404, removed its private state, and released the canonical lock. Parent verification confirmed the owned processes/listener and private directory were absent and the lock was available. Redacted final fields:

```json
{
  "proofPassed": false,
  "failureStage": "real-relay-owner-enrollment",
  "failureName": "TimeoutError",
  "authenticatedDescriptorStatus": 404,
  "processCleanupConfirmed": true,
  "privateCleanupConfirmed": true,
  "localCleanupConfirmed": true
}
```

Cleanup completed on 2026-11-10 at 21:04:07 UTC. Service/image metadata is not a loaded-binary attestation. No merge or production deployment is claimed.

### Exact-head CI

The final `3087c8051a10` push uses normal PR CI, not a broad manual dispatch. These are observed states, not a claim that queued/running checks passed. Merge/deployment holds remain.

- [CodeQL](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42882708607): in_progress
- [macOS Periphery Dead Code [report]](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42882708839): in_progress
- [OpenGrep — PR Diff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42882708781): in_progress
- [Workflow Sanity](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42882708882): in_progress
- [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42882709491): in_progress
- [CodeQL Critical Quality](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42882708673): in_progress
- [PR context and evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42882704819): completed / success
- [Auto response](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42882704845): in_progress
- [Labeler](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42882704815): completed / success
- [ClawSweeper Dispatch](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42882704840): completed / success
- [Security Review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42882704714): in_progress

## Redacted integrated acceptance evidence (2026-11-10)

The excerpts below retain original result-field names and values, with identity, endpoint, credential and operator-path fields omitted. They show bounded outcomes, not a claim that every authority-denial case passed.

**Executed revisions:** the Gateway build, restart runs and restored-state publisher used `f864514d93a08efda68c14eabc42768f081af854`. The repaired CLI and native snapshot-ahead run used `f08fea43c6979223ebf44f8b05020dd3033414ea`. These are historical execution revisions, not the final heads of PR #196388 or #196456. Later source repairs and restacks require their own qualification.

### Wrong recovery kit: observed binding did not change

The actual registered CLI rejected an unrelated recovery kit at binding 2. A subsequent authenticated read compared the **complete binding object** with its pre-attempt value. Supported cancellation then succeeded. This establishes the wrong-kit case's bounded binding outcome; preparation can stage keys, so it does not mean that no temporary state was created.

```json
{
  "bindingBefore": 2,
  "wrongKit": {
    "case": "wrong_kit",
    "ok": false,
    "category": "wrong-kit",
    "exit": 1,
    "movedOutput": false,
    "publishedOutput": false
  },
  "wrongKitBindingUnchanged": true,
  "stagedCancellationAccepted": true,
  "cancel": {"ok": true, "exit": 0}
}
```

The encompassing run has `passed: false`: a **later, separate** correct-kit CLI invocation returned an error after committing binding 2→3. That later error is not denial evidence. The chronology attributes this pre-repair CLI run to `f864514d93a08efda68c14eabc42768f081af854`; the outer receipt pins that Gateway revision, but the wrong-kit subresult contains no independent CLI-source SHA.

The missing-code receipt contains only this CLI input-validation result:

```json
{"case":"missing_code","ok":false,"category":"missing-link-code","errorClass":"Error"}
```

It contains no binding readback, RPC count, retained exit field or embedded source revision. It is not independent final-effect denial evidence and does not prove a server-side authority check.

### Snapshot ahead: native transport refused without advancing persisted trust

The real native transport and SQLite worker used a private, WAL-aware copy of saved node trust. An isolated signed HTTP response supplied verified binding 3 with a signed snapshot claiming binding 4. This was **not a malicious response served by staging Discovery**. The native bridge request returned 502, the refusal was `snapshot_ahead`, and the real persistence callback left the complete target, pin and freshness unchanged.

```json
{
  "passed": true,
  "descriptorBindingSeq": 3,
  "snapshotClaimedBindingSeq": 4,
  "requestSignatureVerified": true,
  "fixtureSignatureVerified": true,
  "descriptorRequests": 1,
  "bridgeHttpStatus": 502,
  "refusal": "snapshot_ahead",
  "persistedRefreshes": 1,
  "targetUnchanged": true,
  "pinUnchanged": true,
  "freshnessUnchanged": true,
  "noServerConnection": true,
  "stagingDiscoveryChanged": false
}
```

This is native transport/persistence integration, not merely a protocol unit test. It does not exercise authority mutation through a running Gateway. The signed snapshot used empty membership arrays; the refusal precedes membership authorization.

### Restored old binding: real staging publication refused; binding 4 remained

Production store hydration and `publishClaw` used a separate restored binding-3 SQLite/key copy. Exactly one old-binding descriptor PUT reached staging Discovery. Current-key signed registration reads succeeded before and after. The publisher verified the returned newer binding under the root and reported a non-retryable supersession.

```json
{
  "noGatewayLaunch": true,
  "remote": {
    "publisher": {
      "realStoredBinding": 3,
      "requests": [
        {"operation":"current_registration","status":200},
        {"operation":"old_binding_descriptor","status":409,"code":"stale_binding","publishedBindingSeq":4},
        {"operation":"current_registration","status":200}
      ],
      "outcome": {
        "state":"failed",
        "code":"binding_superseded",
        "retryable":false,
        "superseded":{"bindingSeq":3,"publishedBindingSeq":4}
      },
      "supersededBindingRootVerified": true,
      "currentKeyAuthenticatedBefore": true,
      "currentKeyAuthenticatedAfter": true,
      "publishedBindingUnchanged": true
    },
    "current4Unchanged": true,
    "baseline3Unchanged": true
  }
}
```

The current binding-4 durable files and retained binding-3 baseline hashes stayed unchanged. This proves restored-state/publisher refusal, **not a full old-Gateway boot**, a remote rebind denial, or a shipped-old-writer upgrade.

### Successful move and recovery: positive controls, not denial substitutes

The repaired registered CLI completed one real 3→4 move against the pinned Gateway. The saved native node and existing owner browser followed without re-admission; the owner pin and freshness binding advanced 3→4 while the membership snapshot sequence stayed 3.

```json
{
  "gatewaySourceCommit":"f864514d93a08efda68c14eabc42768f081af854",
  "cliSourceCommit":"f08fea43c6979223ebf44f8b05020dd3033414ea",
  "passed":true,
  "bindingBefore":3,
  "bindingAfter":4,
  "bindingPublished":true,
  "cli":{"exit":0,"movedOutput":true,"publishedOutput":true},
  "rootPreserved":true,
  "ownerCertificatesPreserved":true,
  "savedNodeFollowed":true,
  "harmlessCommandAfterRebind":true,
  "ownerFollowed":true
}
```

A subsequent actual Gateway stop/start retained binding 4 and both saved followers. Native persisted trust was checked before dialing:

```json
{
  "passed":true,
  "bindingSeq":4,
  "publishedBindingSeq":4,
  "bindingUnchanged":true,
  "nativePersisted4":true,
  "sameNativeNodeReconnected":true,
  "sameOwnerReconnected":true,
  "harmlessCommand":true
}
```

A separate recovery run after the old-binding refusal also records `realRollbackRefusalVerified: true`, `bindingSeq: 4`, `publishedBindingSeq: 4`, `bindingUnchanged: true`, both reconnect booleans `true`, and `harmlessCommand: true`.

### Missing authority-denial coverage

These retained staging receipts do **not** establish:

- **Real relayed rebind refusal through a running Gateway.** There is no retained relayed prepare/commit request, corresponding server refusal such as `not_local_operator`, and before/after authority, binding and publication readback proving no unauthorized final effect. Successful remote reconnect and local wrong-kit rejection do not establish this boundary.
- **Work refused after its service/Labs lifetime ends through a running Gateway.** There is no retained acceptance trace of queued prepare/commit or signature verification spanning shutdown/Labs disable, followed by a refusal and durable-state comparison showing no late write. Source descriptions and service/authority tests remain separate evidence. The same staging receipts do not establish browser sign-out/account-replacement races at commit.
- **Other server-side commit denials from these traces.** A wrong-kit client refusal is not a captured `wrong_signer`, mismatched-key, one-key-only or replayed-commit rejection through the running authority. Protocol/unit-test claims must not be relabelled as these staging outcomes.

No “all authority-denial acceptance complete” conclusion follows from the successful move, restart, snapshot fixture or publisher refusal.

### Shipped-writer qualification limit

The last stable and beta checked in this run lacked the compatible OCID writer paths. Their remote tag objects matched the examined commits:

```json
{
  "examined": [
    {"tag":"v2026.11.2","commit":"b556fdf457b026574bf0f1e7b4914b15f3f179ce","remoteTagObjectMatched":true,"hasOcidWriterPaths":false},
    {"tag":"v2026.11.5-beta.1","commit":"bc061f935bfd79ad09e3e98c6df9f2e8f1e28bea","remoteTagObjectMatched":true,"hasOcidWriterPaths":false}
  ]
}
```

No compatible shipped writer was identified in **those two releases**, so no shipped-writer upgrade was executed. This is not a claim about all historical releases.

With no matching main-failure evidence, these remain PR-owned for the requested full-shard/worker comparison against main, even if the single rerun passes. Both rerun cases must pass and matching main-history failures must exist before calling them pre-existing flakes. Otherwise they remain owned by this PR for CI-like concurrent reproduction and repair; no assertions will be weakened.

The original failing test jobs are:

- [UI E2E 6/7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42885829576/job/130074852343): `config-quick-thinking-persistence.e2e.test.ts:116`, Fast checked-state expected `true`, received `false` after the patch request was observed (634 cases passed, one failed).

The older draft/manual workflow failures are not final-head CI. Normal CI must finish on `829e19d639a0`; one final hosted re-review will follow the required gates. Historical integrated acceptance below keeps its original revisions and limitations. Final-head real-relayed/lifetime proof is being coordinated in the parent ceremony lane, not claimed here.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on the computer that runs a claw, the Control UI had no way to move it to new keys, and it never said why remote access stopped when a key file was lost or newer keys were published elsewhere. Only `openclaw id rebind` and `openclaw id status` could tell or fix that.

## User Impact

User impact: the owner can recover a claw with lost or leaked keys from the browser, with the recovery code and their signed-in account. The account menu and system Inbox show each key problem with its fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Account menu, this computer only:** offers **Move to new keys** while signed in with OpenClaw ID.
- **Dialog flow:**
  - the link code comes from the signed-in account (`account_link_code`), with nothing to paste;
  - the recovery code typed in the browser derives R, which signs the staged keys' binding;
  - the J7 check of Discovery's published binding runs in the browser;
  - the owner confirms the owner, endpoint and Gateway key fingerprints, then `rebind_commit` stores the binding and publishes it.
- **Signing owner:** `signRebind` moves from `src/cli` into the protocol package, so the CLI and the browser share one implementation.
- **Warnings with fixes:**
  - `keys_refused`: a key file is missing or doesn't match;
  - `binding_superseded`: Discovery lists newer keys;
  - `needs_link_code`: new keys aren't published yet, with **Publish new keys**, which also uses the account's code.

Stacked on #196388 (`feat/ocid-owner-rebind`).

## Changes
- `packages/openclaw-id-protocol/src/enrollment/rebind.ts`: `signRebind`, moved from `src/cli/id-cli-rebind.ts` together with its tests.
- `ui/src/lib/openclaw-id/rebind.ts`: prepare/sign, commit, cancel and publish-with-code. A non-kit string is refused before anything is staged.
- `ui/src/components/openclaw-id/move-keys-dialog.tsx`: the dialog.
- `account-menu.tsx` and `identity-menu.tsx`: warning rows and actions. The publication state is read from `openclawId.people`, owner-only, on this computer.
- `docs/cli/id.md`: describes the Control UI path.

**Before / after (signed in, linked, 1280 px):** the menu gains **Move to new keys**.

**Tests:**
- `ui/src/e2e/openclaw-id-move-keys.e2e.test.ts` (mocked Gateway, real Chromium), 2/2:
  - the three warnings each show their action;
  - the dialog sends exactly `account_link_code`, `rebind_prepare`, `rebind_commit`, and the committed binding is signed by the kit's root with the account's code.
- `ui/src/lib/openclaw-id/rebind.test.ts`: real kit signing that verifies under R, a non-kit refused before any request, and another claw's kit refused.
- `account-menu.test.tsx`: the warnings appear only on this computer, and Publish uses the account's code.
- Results:
  - Earlier-head UI unit suites for OpenClaw ID: 79/79;

- **Dismissal during a running step (P2):** Escape or the backdrop during a running check or commit is refused, so a move that completes is never reported as cancelled. `move-keys-dialog.test.tsx` fails on the previous head and passes now.
- **Signing before confirmation (P2), not changed:** the binding is still signed at **Check**, as in `openclaw id rebind`. The signature stays in browser memory and is sent only by **Move to new keys**; Cancel discards it. Signing later would mean keeping the recovery code in memory until confirmation, which is worse custody for no protection gained.
- **Secret handling on close:**
  - The kit secret S and the derived seed are byte arrays, zeroed inside `signRebind`.
