issue.body:
Related: Linear OCF-495

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an already-approved OpenClaw ID browser must ask the owner for approval again after signing out and signing back in, even when it requests the same access.

## User Impact

User impact: returning browsers reconnect with their previously approved access. New roles, broader scopes, or a different device key still require approval. Approval prompts describe the role or scopes being requested.

OpenClaw ID Control UI browsers are managed through Access and the account menu's Your devices, rather than device removal or token revocation. Devices UI and CLI identify these browsers; `devices clear` preserves them. Nodes, native apps, ordinary browsers, and pairings with OpenClaw ID disabled keep normal device management.

## Why This Change Was Made

Sign-out revokes Gateway credentials but intentionally retains device approval and membership. The pairing planner now restores the same approved role only on the OpenClaw ID lane, bounded by live membership, connection limits and the device's approved scopes. Revoked credentials no longer widen a narrower replacement. The existing approval and credential owners retain their live-authority checks.

The existing tunnel-token binding also identifies Access-managed browsers, including tokenless browser lanes. Sign-out retains that binding; membership removal and device deletion clean it up. Accepted availability tradeoff: a custom same-origin proxy sharing one browser key between ordinary and OpenClaw ID ingress binds that key's token to its OpenClaw ID peer. This does not add authority.

## Evidence

Local test command wall times: Gateway/CLI 185 s (includes cold worker compilation), UI 8 s, supplemental HTTP/ingress 117 s, node-pairing 140 s. Exact-head CI completed; the failing UI shard ran for 694 s. The added tunnel suite completed in 31 s (19 tests); Devices and lifecycle suites passed 48 tests in the combined run, and the binding suite passed 7 tests. An earlier supplemental invocation passed its assertions but was invalidated by concurrent formatting; the reported 117 s run kept source unchanged and completed successfully.

- Rebased onto main `604aacb6cdf4df3ecf6fb5b7bf690dd58d6804c5`. The repair is still needed: main's planner excludes the revoked-token `role-upgrade` case. Two textual conflicts preserved main's CLI unknown-ID handling and keyed/accessor UI warning rows alongside this PR's changes.
- Updated the two current-main binding-owner test fixtures to implement the new cleanup contract. No restoration or membership behavior was changed by conflict resolution.
- Focused Gateway/CLI tests: 108 passed across tunnel restoration, trusted-proxy exclusion, device management, binding ownership, remote sign-out and CLI suites. UI tests: 57 passed across login feedback and device inventory. Supplemental HTTP/remote-ingress tests: 15 passed; current-main node-pairing/listing regressions: 7 passed. Core, UI and Gateway-server test typechecks passed. Type-aware lint passed for touched core/UI files and the added fixture repairs.
- [Prior isolated staging live proof at `c1c539d`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194354#issuecomment-6715102894): real Chromium owner/member sign-out and sign-in over staging ID/Discovery/relay without an approval prompt; removed-member sign-in refused with no replacement token. The throwaway claw and isolated Gateway were retired afterwards. This remains historical proof of the unchanged restoration logic, **not a final-head live run**. Later Access-management changes are covered by production-path Gateway and UI tests, not that staging run. The new tokenless cases use a real isolated Gateway and WebSocket RPC with synthetic ingress attribution and membership owners, not live external ID/Discovery/relay services.
- Test budget: 442 added test/support lines with a matching PR-owned allocation. The review repair adds a stalled-cleanup ordering assertion and two production-boundary tokenless membership cases while removing the helper-only tokenless test. The shared ceiling is unchanged.
- Exact-head review at `b6c78b319a0a` identified a real P1: device removal awaited binding cleanup before revoking connected clients. The cleanup is now inside the existing teardown protection, after synchronous client invalidation. The deferred-cleanup regression failed on `b6c78b319a0a` (zero invalidation calls while cleanup was pending) and passes with the repair; caller-retirement and worker-cleanup-failure lifecycle tests remain green.
- Tokenless production-boundary proof: with configured operator roles, a member receives no device token, appears as Access-managed, completes an allowed `health` RPC, and is refused an admin RPC. Removing its peer or reassigning that peer to another account then closes the connection before another `health` RPC can run. The initial fixture expected generic configured-role scopes; source inspection confirmed the tunnel's built-in operator policy takes precedence. The corrected test asserts that exact policy and passes both cases.
- Fresh independent Astra review covered the complete rebased diff and supplemental repairs, then separately reviewed the removal-ordering and tokenless proof delta. No remaining verified P0–P2 findings. [Exact-head hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194354#issuecomment-6698222852) at `09a3f91d12d1` found no remaining defects and accepted the proof.

Login gate before and after, using the same `role-upgrade` request (same role and same six scopes as in the issue):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Same role, same six scopes (the OCF-495 case) | ![before: Approve the new role](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da1daa69-ea38-495b-9bea-15735b2e1bc5) | ![after: Approve this browser again](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2f939eb9-b0b4-4819-af8a-5aec6429833c) |
| Role not yet approved (a real new role) | ![before: Approve the new role](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f65aeb5-3781-4ba4-99da-c3e5dc59877c) | ![after: Approve the new role, naming operator](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bad753c2-7703-4bcc-b185-275e7d890f4c) |

Captured from the production Control UI build with a mocked Gateway connect rejection (`role-upgrade`, request `7f6e33d0…`), on main `936f38793bab` and on this branch.


### Final CI qualification

[CI run 42785043378, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42785043378) completed for `09a3f91d12d1aa81a29193c6504e5a36121a4660`. Core/changed-node tests, UI unit tests, production/test typechecks, lint, security and baseline ratchets passed. CI remains red for two independently verified inherited failures; landing uses the native inherited-failure route, not a claim that CI passed:

- [check-docs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42785043378/job/129724783224): `pnpm format:check` fails on `scripts/lib/full-release-child-reuse.mjs`, `test/scripts/full-release-receipt-recovery.test.ts`, `test/scripts/plugin-npm-cli-process.test.ts`, and `test/scripts/plugin-npm-cli-recovery.test-support.mjs`. All four blobs and formatter configuration are identical between tested merge `f1b22eb5491d` and its main parent `7f7c1a70699a`. Checking extracted main-parent bytes with the same oxfmt 0.74.0 reproduces exactly these four failures. All actual docs-content checks passed.
- [checks-ui-e2e (4/7)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42785043378/job/129724784043): the mobile/tablet/desktop thinking-argument completion cases expect `/think ultra` after Tab but receive `/think `. [Scheduled main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42782788359/job/129717133294) fails the same three cases with the same assertion at `chat-thinking-arguments.e2e.test.ts:148` (assigned to shard 5 there). The failing test, test harness, and chat-components subtree are unchanged by this PR.

The aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` failure follows those two jobs. No CI rerun or unrelated source repair was used to obtain green results.

issue.body:
Related: Linear OCF-495

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an already-approved OpenClaw ID browser must ask the owner for approval again after signing out and signing back in, even when it requests the same access.

## User Impact

User impact: returning browsers reconnect with their previously approved access. New roles, broader scopes, or a different device key still require approval. Approval prompts describe the role or scopes being requested.

OpenClaw ID Control UI browsers are managed through Access and the account menu's Your devices, rather than device removal or token revocation. Devices UI and CLI identify these browsers; `devices clear` preserves them. Nodes, native apps, ordinary browsers, and pairings with OpenClaw ID disabled keep normal device management.

## Why This Change Was Made

Sign-out revokes Gateway credentials but intentionally retains device approval and membership. The pairing planner now restores the same approved role only on the OpenClaw ID lane, bounded by live membership, connection limits and the device's approved scopes. Revoked credentials no longer widen a narrower replacement. The existing approval and credential owners retain their live-authority checks.

The existing tunnel-token binding also identifies Access-managed browsers, including tokenless browser lanes. Sign-out retains that binding; membership removal and device deletion clean it up. Accepted availability tradeoff: a custom same-origin proxy sharing one browser key between ordinary and OpenClaw ID ingress binds that key's token to its OpenClaw ID peer. This does not add authority.

## Evidence

Local test command wall times: Gateway/CLI 185 s (includes cold worker compilation), UI 8 s, supplemental HTTP/ingress 117 s, node-pairing 140 s. Exact-head CI completed; the failing UI shard ran for 694 s. The added tunnel suite completed in 31 s (19 tests); Devices and lifecycle suites passed 48 tests in the combined run, and the binding suite passed 7 tests. An earlier supplemental invocation passed its assertions but was invalidated by concurrent formatting; the reported 117 s run kept source unchanged and completed successfully.

- Focused Gateway/CLI tests: 108 passed across tunnel restoration, trusted-proxy exclusion, device management, binding ownership, remote sign-out and CLI suites. UI tests: 57 passed across login feedback and device inventory. Supplemental HTTP/remote-ingress tests: 15 passed; current-main node-pairing/listing regressions: 7 passed. issue.body:
Related: #196138 (re-bind design, "Key files at every start")

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a linked claw silently creates a new endpoint key or Gateway key when its key file is lost (disk loss, a restore that skipped `openclaw-id/`, an accidental delete), then publishes and signs under keys its owner-signed server binding does not name, which strands every device.

## User Impact

User impact: when a linked claw's key file is missing or holds a different key, OpenClaw ID remote access stays off with status `keys_refused` (`key: endpoint | gateway`, `reason: keys_missing | key_mismatch`). Nothing is created, published, signed or dialed with another key. The Gateway itself keeps running, so everything on the machine works as before. Restoring the original key file brings remote access back. The way to move a claw to new keys (`openclaw id rebind`) follows in a stacked PR. Unlinked Gateways create keys exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Once a claw is linked, its stored binding is the only record of which K_srv and K_gw are current. At every start the Gateway (for K_gw) and the tunnel child (for K_srv, via `expectedEndpointKey` in its start message) use the key file only when its seed derives the bound public key. Otherwise they promote a staged `<file>.next` only if *its* seed derives the bound key, so a planted file is never used, and if neither matches they refuse. The re-bind uses that `.next` promotion to finish an interrupted commit. The child exits with new codes 76/75, which the supervisor does not retry. The Gateway never reads the K_srv file.

Owner decision for this fix: the Gateway is not blocked from starting, and nothing in startup or Doctor treats this state as fatal.

<details><summary>Notes for reviewers</summary>

- `claw-name-check.ts` and `service-gateway-key.ts` are extracted from `service.ts` (max-lines). Name-check behavior is unchanged, and the lifetime signal is still captured on admission.
- The tunnel child's K_srv requirement survives authority withdrawn after an uncertain store write. It keeps the last bound K_srv rather than falling back to the unlinked "create" start (from the independent review).
- Test fixtures: `linkedClaw()` now writes its K_gw seed into a per-claw state dir. Several existing tests relied on the bug, because the Gateway minted a key for a linked claw.

</details>

## Evidence

- Real Gateway (`src/gateway/server.openclaw-id-keys.test.ts`). A linked claw with `gateway.key` gone returns `keys_refused/gateway/keys_missing`, with no key files created and `health` still answering. With `endpoint.key` gone, the real tunnel child returns `keys_refused/endpoint/keys_missing` and creates no key. **Both fail on `main`** (status `on`, keys minted).
- Real tunnel child: it serves on the bound key and promotes a staged key the binding names. This shows the Ed25519 seed→pubkey derivation equals iroh's endpoint id.
- Service: K_gw missing or mismatched means no `fetch`, no file, and `publish()` → `failed keys_missing`. A local membership change is still accepted and stays pending for publication. Red on `main`.
- Key rule matrix (`keyfile.test.ts`): match, staged match, missing, mismatch, and a planted staged key that is not promoted. Supervisor: 76/75 are not retried.
- Withdrawn-authority restart regression: red without the fix, green with it.
- Link-commit regression: a Gateway that starts unlinked and links, then has its authority withdrawn by an uncertain write before any child restart reads the binding. The restart getter still returns the committed K_srv. Red without the fix, green with it (ClawSweeper P2/security).
- Recovery copy (log lines and docs/concepts/experimental-features.md): restore the original key files, **then restart the Gateway**. After a refusal the supervisor does not retry, so restoring the file alone does not bring remote access back (ClawSweeper P2).
- `linkedClaw` key directories are tracked and removed after each test file (ClawSweeper P3).
- Still open: runtime proof with an isolated Gateway and a stable-upgrade check. These run with the staging live proof.
- `src/gateway/openclaw-id` suite green, plus `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:ui`, oxlint and format. Inherited failure: `server.auth.openclaw-id-node-host.test.ts` "both streaming transfer routes use the same private bridge" fails identically on `main` in this environment.



## Initial-link uncertain settlement correction

`a71dce7` addresses the new current-head P2: the initial link may be durable even when its acknowledgement and reconciliation read both fail. The service now retains the supervisor-reported running K_srv before awaiting link settlement, rather than only after a successful return. It does not trust caller-supplied binding data or restore withdrawn authority. A readable binding still wins; a refused link attempt conservatively retains the already-running endpoint constraint for that process. Fresh unlinked startups remain unchanged.

The existing withdrawn-authority regression now covers both the initial-link and later-write cases. The initial case verifies the persisted binding, withdrawn authority and endpoint constraint delivered to the next child start. It fails on `3c40bfb` (getter returns undefined) and passes with this change. Focused service/keyfile/name/real-Gateway lost-key suites: 5 files, 20/20 tests. Core typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, format, diff check and the test-lines ratchet pass. Fresh independent source review found no P0–P2 findings. The test matrix reuses the existing fixture; production repair moves one assignment before settlement without introducing another owner or state field.

This regression reads the real service's restart-key getter with the native child mocked. The sibling real-Gateway tests exercise both lost key files, but the exact uncertain-initial-link path through an isolated real tunnel and stable upgrade is still an explicit proof gap, not claimed complete here. No deployment or merge.

## Integrated staging acceptance and final cleanup — November 10

This closes the earlier pending same-claw staging run, not exact-head hosted CI or every PR-specific test gap. The isolated Gateway used combined source `f864514d93a08efda68c14eabc42768f081af854`; the repaired registered CLI used `f08fea43c6979223ebf44f8b05020dd3033414ea`. These are integrated proof refs, not the individual PR heads.

- Actual Control UI rotation **1→2** committed and published, preserving the root and admitted native node (`studio-ui-rebind-v4-call-result.json`).
- The earlier CLI **2→3** committed but reported failure; that defect remains recorded above/in #196388. A deliberately new repaired CLI **3→4** exited **0**, reported `moved:true`/`published:true`, and authenticated readback confirmed binding/published 4. Root, two owner certificates and membership remained intact (`studio-cli4-owner-follow-call-result.json`).
- The same persistent remote owner browser and saved native node followed **3→4** and reconnected after a separate actual Gateway restart. Production SQLite trust load showed pin/freshness 4 before native dialing; `system.which(uname)` passed (`studio-cli4-restart-call-result.json`). This does not retroactively prove owner-browser following of each earlier rotation.
- Actual native transport with copied real node trust refused a signed snapshot claiming binding 4 under verified binding 3 as `snapshot_ahead`, without advancing pin/freshness or connecting. This used an isolated signed HTTP fixture, not a malicious write to staging (`studio-snapshot-ahead-native-result.json`).
- Production `readStoredClaw`/`publishClaw` used real old binding-3 SQLite and keys against staging: HTTP 409 `stale_binding` carried binding 4, verified under the root, producing non-retryable `binding_superseded`. Current-key authentication succeeded before/after; current Gateway/native/owner recovery then passed. This is persisted-state/publisher integration, **not a full old-Gateway boot** (`studio-rollback3-publisher-result.json`, `studio-post-rollback4-recovery-call-result.json`).
- Final exact-claw retirement completed once; database checks showed no claw/member/relay-key rows and a reserved retired hostname. Independent existing-owner authentication obtained descriptor **404**. Owned processes/listeners/transports were absent; private Studio/fsn1 profiles, snapshots, keys and kit copies were removed, with tracked checkouts clean. The original lock holder exited 0, the same canonical lock was verified available, and four reservation-owner release notices were queued. No merge or production deployment occurred.

**Shipped older-writer limitation:** the remotely verified latest stable `v2026.11.2` and beta `v2026.11.5-beta.1` examined here contain neither `src/gateway/openclaw-id` nor `packages/openclaw-id-protocol`. A compatible shipped writer was not available in that bounded set, so a shipped-writer upgrade was not executed and cannot be claimed. This is not an exhaustive statement about every historical release. See `shipped-old-writer-feasibility.json`.

Evidence files above are operator-local under `/tmp/ocid-rollout-evidence/`, not downloadable GitHub attachments. Final receipts: `studio-final-retirement-descriptor-result.json`, `studio-final-cleanup-result.json`, `studio-final-private-state-cleanup-result.json`, `studio-final-lock-release-result.json`; full run chronology: `studio-harness-integration-audit.md`.

For #196380 specifically, this combined run does not newly prove the exact uncertain-initial-link failure through a real tunnel; its existing focused regression and stated scope remain unchanged.

## Current-main CI comparison and clean rebase — November 10

The prior UI failure is **not classified as inherited**. The latest scheduled main run [42844215728](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42844215728), at `da0190f377a8384223fca256990dae0a2bff2678`, passed the exact `chat-transcript-end-follow.browser.test.ts` case `preserves clamp intent (settled, at end: true, movement: 8, before clamp: true)` in 409 ms ([job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42844215728/job/129927628372)). Newer main push runs skipped this UI lane; their success is not test-execution evidence. The PR was therefore rebased without conflicts onto pinned current main `b21829a4c85fb685888538b3bc1369bfb5b36bd4`, producing `8d20985e878b4eef195e040ea0fef6425536566d`. The complete PR patch has unchanged stable patch ID `5081067f0443cbe4937af751d3392ecd95d1bf1a`; `git diff --check` passes. The accepted independent full-PR review remains source-applicable; prior-head CI and integrated runtime proof retain their actual tested identities. New-head hosted CI is pending, not claimed green.

issue.body:
### Summary

Don't let automatic session maintenance (stale-dashboard, age and count-cap archiving) pause automations whose creating conversation it archives.

### Problem to solve

Since #178965, an automation pauses when the conversation that created it is archived or removed, and #184818 asks the user before they archive or delete such a conversation. Session maintenance can archive the same conversation without any user action:

- Dashboard conversations are archived after 7 idle days by default (`session.maintenance.archiveDashboardAfter`, [docs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/03121096e4e25fe0e959bbb6ba4917528210a778/docs/gateway/config-agents/sessions.md?plain=1#L130)). `pruneAfter` and `maxEntries` can archive conversations too.
- `archiveStaleDashboardEntries` sets `archiveReason = "stale-dashboard"` ([store-maintenance.ts#L333-L366](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/03121096e4e25fe0e959bbb6ba4917528210a778/src/config/sessions/store-maintenance.ts#L333-L366)). Its protections cover pinned rows, active work, recent activity and protected chat surfaces ([#L428-L444](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/03121096e4e25fe0e959bbb6ba4917528210a778/src/config/sessions/store-maintenance.ts#L428-L444)). None checks for an enabled bound automation, and none of the registered preserve-key providers comes from automation bindings ([store-maintenance-preserve.ts#L46](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/03121096e4e25fe0e959bbb6ba4917528210a778/src/config/sessions/store-maintenance-preserve.ts#L46)).
- At the next occurrence, `classifyScheduledParent` returns `"archived"` for any archived parent, whatever the archive reason ([execution-context.ts#L261-L282](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/03121096e4e25fe0e959bbb6ba4917528210a778/src/cron/execution-context.ts#L261-L282)), and admission pauses the job ([execution-context-admission.ts#L267](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/03121096e4e25fe0e959bbb6ba4917528210a778/src/cron/execution-context-admission.ts#L267)).

So a recurring automation created in a dashboard chat stops on its own once the user hasn't opened that chat for a week. That's typical for weekly reports, watchers and reminders, which run without the user returning to the chat. The #184818 confirmation never appears, because no one archived anything. Per #178965 the pause notice goes to the agent, not to the gone conversation, so the user may not notice until a run they expected is missing.

### Proposed solution

Treat a conversation that has an enabled bound automation as protected from automatic archiving, the way pinned conversations and active work are. For example, register a preserve-key provider from the cron bindings (the same data behind `hasAutomation` and the sidebar clock badge). Explicit archive and delete keep the #184818 confirmation and the #178965 pause.

If automatic archiving must stay, the fallback is to not pause for maintenance archive reasons (`stale-dashboard`, `age-retention`, `active-session-cap`), and only pause for an explicit archive or removal.

### Alternatives considered

- **Pin every conversation that owns an automation.** This works (pinned rows are preserved), but users can't be expected to know it, and only root conversations can be pinned.
- **Disable `archiveDashboardAfter`.** Gives up the sidebar tidying for everyone to protect a few conversations.
- **Create long-lived automations from the CLI or the Automations page.** Jobs without a parent link don't pause, but they also lose the parent-conversation authority that #178811 is building.

### Impact

- Affected: anyone who creates recurring automations from Control UI dashboard chats.
- Severity: blocks workflow silently; the automation stops and the user isn't asked.
- Frequency: deterministic after `archiveDashboardAfter` (7 days by default) without activity in the creating chat.
- Consequence: missed reports, reminders and monitoring until someone notices.

### Evidence/examples

- Source references above are on `main` at `0312109`. I derived this from the code and haven't reproduced it: our Gateway runs 2026.10.7, which doesn't include #178965 yet.
- Field data for the question in #184854 about how often the pause bites: on 2026.10.7, archiving one dashboard chat by hand disabled 7 enabled automations created in it, on two consecutive days (27 and 28 Oct 2026). We noticed only after the jobs had stopped, and had to re-enable them each time.
- Related: #178811, #178965, #184818, #184854.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance

### Additional information

Written with help from my OpenClaw agent, which checked the code references against `main`.

issue.body:
Related: #196138 (re-bind design, "Key files at every start")

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a linked claw silently creates a new endpoint key or Gateway key when its key file is lost (disk loss, a restore that skipped `openclaw-id/`, an accidental delete), then publishes and signs under keys its owner-signed server binding does not name, which strands every device.

## User Impact

User impact: when a linked claw's key file is missing or holds a different key, OpenClaw ID remote access stays off with status `keys_refused` (`key: endpoint | gateway`, `reason: keys_missing | key_mismatch`). Nothing is created, published, signed or dialed with another key. The Gateway itself keeps running, so everything on the machine works as before. Restoring the original key file brings remote access back. The way to move a claw to new keys (`openclaw id rebind`) follows in a stacked PR. Unlinked Gateways create keys exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Once a claw is linked, its stored binding is the only record of which K_srv and K_gw are current. At every start the Gateway (for K_gw) and the tunnel child (for K_srv, via `expectedEndpointKey` in its start message) use the key file only when its seed derives the bound public key. Otherwise they promote a staged `<file>.next` only if *its* seed derives the bound key, so a planted file is never used, and if neither matches they refuse. The re-bind uses that `.next` promotion to finish an interrupted commit. The child exits with new codes 76/75, which the supervisor does not retry. The Gateway never reads the K_srv file.

Owner decision for this fix: the Gateway is not blocked from starting, and nothing in startup or Doctor treats this state as fatal.

<details><summary>Notes for reviewers</summary>

- `claw-name-check.ts` and `service-gateway-key.ts` are extracted from `service.ts` (max-lines). Name-check behavior is unchanged, and the lifetime signal is still captured on admission.
- The tunnel child's K_srv requirement survives authority withdrawn after an uncertain store write. It keeps the last bound K_srv rather than falling back to the unlinked "create" start (from the independent review).
- Test fixtures: `linkedClaw()` now writes its K_gw seed into a per-claw state dir. Several existing tests relied on the bug, because the Gateway minted a key for a linked claw.

</details>

## Evidence

- Real Gateway (`src/gateway/server.openclaw-id-keys.test.ts`). A linked claw with `gateway.key` gone returns `keys_refused/gateway/keys_missing`, with no key files created and `health` still answering. With `endpoint.key` gone, the real tunnel child returns `keys_refused/endpoint/keys_missing` and creates no key. **Both fail on `main`** (status `on`, keys minted).
- Real tunnel child: it serves on the bound key and promotes a staged key the binding names. This shows the Ed25519 seed→pubkey derivation equals iroh's endpoint id.
- Service: K_gw missing or mismatched means no `fetch`, no file, and `publish()` → `failed keys_missing`. A local membership change is still accepted and stays pending for publication. Red on `main`.
- Key rule matrix (`keyfile.test.ts`): match, staged match, missing, mismatch, and a planted staged key that is not promoted. Supervisor: 76/75 are not retried.
- Withdrawn-authority restart regression: red without the fix, green with it.
- Link-commit regression: a Gateway that starts unlinked and links, then has its authority withdrawn by an uncertain write before any child restart reads the binding. The restart getter still returns the committed K_srv. Red without the fix, green with it (ClawSweeper P2/security).
- Recovery copy (log lines and docs/concepts/experimental-features.md): restore the original key files, **then restart the Gateway**. After a refusal the supervisor does not retry, so restoring the file alone does not bring remote access back (ClawSweeper P2).
- `linkedClaw` key directories are tracked and removed after each test file (ClawSweeper P3).
- Still open: runtime proof with an isolated Gateway and a stable-upgrade check. These run with the staging live proof.
- `src/gateway/openclaw-id` suite green, plus `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:ui`, oxlint and format. Inherited failure: `server.auth.openclaw-id-node-host.test.ts` "both streaming transfer routes use the same private bridge" fails identically on `main` in this environment.



## Initial-link uncertain settlement correction

`a71dce7` addresses the new current-head P2: the initial link may be durable even when its acknowledgement and reconciliation read both fail. The service now retains the supervisor-reported running K_srv before awaiting link settlement, rather than only after a successful return. It does not trust caller-supplied binding data or restore withdrawn authority. A readable binding still wins; a refused link attempt conservatively retains the already-running endpoint constraint for that process. Fresh unlinked startups remain unchanged.

The existing withdrawn-authority regression now covers both the initial-link and later-write cases. The initial case verifies the persisted binding, withdrawn authority and endpoint constraint delivered to the next child start. It fails on `3c40bfb` (getter returns undefined) and passes with this change. Focused service/keyfile/name/real-Gateway lost-key suites: 5 files, 20/20 tests. Core typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, format, diff check and the test-lines ratchet pass. Fresh independent source review found no P0–P2 findings. The test matrix reuses the existing fixture; production repair moves one assignment before settlement without introducing another owner or state field.

This regression reads the real service's restart-key getter with the native child mocked. The sibling real-Gateway tests exercise both lost key files, but the exact uncertain-initial-link path through an isolated real tunnel and stable upgrade is still an explicit proof gap, not claimed complete here. issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agents misread `github_publish`. They conclude they can't land a PR, give up on a refused publish they believed had succeeded, or chase an unrelated `workspacePath` error.

## User Impact

User impact: `github_publish` now tells agents its limits and their next step. Only messages change; no behavior changes.
- **Landing scope:** `inspect`, `ready`, `merge` and `close` act only on the session's published or bound PR (including one bound with `prepare_pr`), or a delegated child's `publishingSessionKey`. Any other PR lands through the repository's native route (`scripts/pr` for OpenClaw). In one session, an agent concluded a PR "couldn't be merged" when the native route worked.
- **Publishing:** with `workspacePath`, `started` is not success. The result, which may be a refusal, resumes the session as the next turn. Running background commands, unfinished children, open terminals or another active run refuse preparation. A session publishes one checkout; use a separate session for another.
- **`readiness`:** says it doesn't check that busy condition. When the conversation has no bound checkout, the result adds a `next` line saying how to publish.
- **Errors:** a call that fills optional fields with placeholders now says to omit them, instead of "workspacePath is only available for local host publication". `readiness` and `inspect_pr` name the fields to remove.

## Why This Change Was Made

An investigation of two weeks of publisher failures on a production Gateway found these wordings behind repeated agent mistakes:
- 121 calls rejected with the misleading `workspacePath` error.
- 9 "different checkout" refusals with no warning in the description.
- Wrong-target `inspect`/`ready` calls.
- A refused publish reported only in the following turn.

The behavior fixes are separate: #196077 (stopped background commands blocking publish) and #196083 (ClawRouter GPT placeholder arguments).

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/agents/tools/github-publish-tool.test.ts src/agents/tools/github-publish-tool.handoff.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 30 + 8 passing. The two new behavioral tests fail on base and pass with the change; a description-only test was dropped at review.
- `prompt:snapshots:check` reports the snapshots are current, and `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` passes (14/14).
- `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test` and `check:test-lines-ratchet` all pass. The ratchet uses a 32-line allocation for the new tests.

issue.body:
Fixes #187590

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an automation created in a dashboard chat pauses on its own when automatic session maintenance archives that chat for being idle. This happens after 7 days by default, or through `pruneAfter` or `maxEntries`.

## User Impact

User impact: a conversation that created an enabled automation is no longer archived by automatic maintenance, so weekly reports, watchers and reminders keep running even if nobody opens the chat. Disabling or removing the automation makes the chat eligible again. Archiving or deleting the chat yourself still asks for confirmation (#184818) and still pauses its automations (#178965).

## Why This Change Was Made

Since #178965, an automation pauses when the conversation that created it is archived. Scheduled runs never touch that conversation (#185341), so it looks idle to maintenance. This PR registers a session-maintenance preserve provider fed from the cron service's loaded jobs. It uses the same mechanism as pinned rows and active work, so stale-dashboard archiving, age retention and the entry cap all honor it.

- Only enabled jobs protect a chat, and only the exact creating conversation. The provider resolves that conversation with `resolveScheduledPrincipal`, the same call occurrence admission uses before it pauses. Wake, delivery and run-session bindings don't pin anything.
- Under `maxEntries`, a protected chat still counts toward the cap, the same as a pinned chat. If protection prevents reaching the cap, the store stays above it, as documented.
- No new config option. Docs are updated in `docs/gateway/config-agents/sessions.md` and `docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md`.

- **Gateway startup:** cron loads its jobs in the background, after post-ready maintenance has started. A preserve provider can now report `isPending()`. While any provider is pending, the snapshot carries `archivingDeferred` and the planner skips only the archiving actions: stale-dashboard, `pruneAfter` age and `maxEntries` cap. Everything else runs as today, including removal of disposable runtime rows. The planner change is generic; nothing in it is cron-specific.
  - The Gateway's cron provider is pending from the moment a cron service is created until its jobs register. This includes hot-reload replacements, which are built directly: the replacement arms pending while its predecessor still serves, so the gap after the predecessor unregisters stays protected. A reload that switches cron to disabled builds its replacement with `cronEnabled=false`, which clears any leftover pending state, so archiving isn't paused for the rest of the process.
  - If cron is disabled (`cron.enabled: false` or `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CRON=1`), or no cron service is created, the provider never becomes pending, so archiving proceeds. A disabled scheduler still loads its jobs, and the parents of enabled jobs stay protected. That's deliberate: re-enabling cron must not find those jobs paused because maintenance archived their chats while it was off.
  - If the cron load fails, the provider stays pending, so archiving waits until a later start succeeds. Not archiving errs on the safe side: a missed archive is a cosmetic sidebar delay, but a wrong archive silently stops the user's automations.
  - **Cost:** while the load stays failed, automatic archiving is paused for the whole process, so the unarchived session count can grow past `maxEntries` until cron starts. The Gateway logs one warning per process: `automatic session archiving is paused: automations failed to load`. There are no timers or retries; a later successful start, such as a config reload or restart, resumes archiving.
  - Doctor runs out of process and can't see this runtime-only state, so it isn't surfaced there. The warning and the existing cron start error are the signal.
  - A commit whose planning saw "ready" but whose final protection check sees "pending" is rejected and replanned, like any newly protected row.

Known limits:
- While a provider is pending, disposable runtime rows such as sub-agent sessions are still pruned. A job whose creating conversation is a sub-agent session can still lose its parent in that window, as it already could before this PR.
- A local `openclaw sessions cleanup --dry-run` runs without the Gateway's jobs. `--enforce` runs in the Gateway and honors the protection.

## Evidence

- **Unit (real maintenance planner):** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/session-automation-index.maintenance.test.ts src/gateway/session-automation-index.test.ts`: 20 passed. The tests cover each of the stale-dashboard, `pruneAfter` and `maxEntries` phases:
  - An idle chat with an enabled bound automation is kept, its job stays enabled, and admission's `classifyScheduledParent` still reports `current`.
  - The same chat with a disabled automation, or none, is archived as before.
- **Red on base:** with the provider registration removed, the three "keeps" tests fail.
- **Before cron loads (unit, all three phases):** with the Gateway's cron service created but not yet loaded, maintenance archives nothing and still prunes the disposable subagent row. Once jobs register, only the protected parent is kept. With no cron service, archiving proceeds as before. After a failed load, archiving stays deferred and the warning is emitted once. A hot-reload test covers the predecessor-to-replacement handoff; it fails when a replacement doesn't arm pending while a source is registered. A second test covers a reload from enabled (not yet loaded) to disabled and checks that archiving resumes. Red: with `isPending` forced to false, the three deferral tests fail.
- **Shared maintenance suites:** `store.pruning`, `store-maintenance.dashboard-archive`, the `session-accessor.sqlite-maintenance-{kick,cap,worker,writer}` tests, `cleanup-service.{cap-archive,deferred-sources}` and `sqlite-exact-read`: 9 files passed.
- **Static checks:** `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint and oxfmt on changed files: clean.
- **Real Gateway, local (mock-openai QA scenario):**
  - A real turn in another chat triggers automatic maintenance, which archives the idle chats with a disabled automation and with none.
  - The chat with the enabled automation stays unarchived, including after `sessions.cleanup --enforce`.
  - Its job runs `ok` and stays enabled.
  - Re-enabling the archived control's job pauses it with the "it was archived" notice.
- **Test-line budget:** the new regression tests add 168 net test lines. `config/test-lines-allocations/196297-automation-parent-retention.txt` grants exactly that, as `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` requires.
- **Crabbox AWS proof on `6b7c92c9`**. The final head `89097433` changes only the test-line allocation file; no runtime, test or doc file differs from the proven head:
  - Run `run_94e3713e8a808a96b20bd63fbff0b901`, lease `cbx_c5d662ff7d0e` (c7a.8xlarge, us-east-1). Exit 0; the lease is released.
  - All 21 changed and proof files on the box are sha256-identical to the head.
  - Command: `crabbox run --provider aws -- bash proof.sh`. The script runs the QA scenario, then the upgrade script.
  - **QA scenario `cron-automation-parent-retention`** (real Gateway, mock-openai, `archiveDashboardAfter: 6s`), 5/5 steps passed:
    - Automatic maintenance, triggered by a real turn in another chat, archives the idle chat with a disabled automation and the idle chat with none.
    - The idle chat with an enabled automation stays unarchived through that pass and through `sessions.cleanup --enforce`.
    - Its job then runs `ok`, reaches the model, and stays enabled.
    - Re-enabling the control's job pauses it: "it was archived".
  - **Upgrade from v2026.11.2** (same state dir, `doctor --fix`, then the PR build with `archiveDashboardAfter: 5s`). All 8 checks passed, 0 failed:
    - Baseline on v2026.11.2: the idle chat with an enabled automation is archived. Stable has no archived-parent pause, so its job still runs.
    - On the PR build, chats and jobs created on stable before the upgrade, and chats and jobs created after it, behave the same:
      - The chat with an enabled automation is kept through automatic maintenance and enforce cleanup. Its job runs `ok`, reaches the model and stays enabled.
      - The chat with a disabled automation is archived (`stale-dashboard`). Its job, once re-enabled, pauses with the archived-parent notice, which shows the parent link survived the upgrade.

<details><summary>Upgrade proof results.jsonl (abridged)</summary>

```

{"check":"stable-enabled-automation-chat-kept","pass":true}
{"check":"post-upgrade-control-chat-archived","pass":true}

```

issue.body:
## Executive summary

Before moving any code, write down exactly how a session handles turns: which states it can be in, what each kind of input does in each state, and which rules must never break. Then encode that description as a small executable model and a test harness that runs thousands of random event sequences against it. Every later change in this project runs against the same harness, so the migration cannot change user-visible behavior by accident.

Part of #160737.

## Problem

Turn handling is spread across six in-memory records (listed in #160737). No document or type describes how they interact. [`docs/concepts/queue.md`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/docs/concepts/queue.md) describes each queue mode on its own, but not what happens when a mode meets compaction, `/stop`, `/new`, a restart, or a queue that already has messages waiting. One consequence: `interrupt` does not interrupt when follow-ups are queued ([`src/auto-reply/reply/queue-policy.ts:22`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/auto-reply/reply/queue-policy.ts#L22)), which contradicts [`docs/concepts/queue.md:45`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/docs/concepts/queue.md#L45).

## Deliverables

1. **Concept doc** at `docs/concepts/session-controller.md`, linked from `queue.md`, `agent-loop.md`, and `session.md`. It covers states, input kinds, queue policies, stop semantics, lifecycle mutations, and restart behavior.
2. **Typed statechart**: state and event unions plus a pure `transition(state, event)` function that returns the next state and a list of effects (start run, inject, abort, emit reply, and so on). It has no I/O and no timers.
3. **Model-based test harness**: a seeded generator of event sequences (inputs of every kind, run progress, compaction start and end, stop requests, settle, mutations, drain) with a fake clock. After each step it checks the invariants below. The same harness later drives the real controller through a thin adapter, so #160739 to #160744 reuse it.

## Proposed states

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `idle` | No run holds the session |
| `admitting` | A run holds the session slot and waits for deferred maintenance or a global lane slot |
| `preparing` | Preflight compaction or memory flush before inference |
| `running` | The attempt loop is active. Sub-flags: `streaming`, `compacting` |
| `finishing` | The run can no longer be aborted (today's `freezeAbort`) |
| `settling` | The outcome is recorded, delivery is settling, and the next input is chosen |
| `mutating` | A reset, delete, or compaction holds the session |

The mailbox of waiting inputs is a separate ordered list that exists in every state.

## Invariants

1. At most one run holds the session slot for a session key.
2. Every accepted input reaches exactly one disposition: steered into a run, started a turn, merged into a collect batch, dropped by a named policy, cancelled by a stop, or interrupted by a restart.
3. A stop or interrupt applies to the run that holds the slot when the request is accepted. It never aborts that run's successor.
4. When a run settles, at most one successor starts, and only after the settled run's outcome is recorded.
5. No run starts while a lifecycle mutation holds the session. A mutation starts while a run holds the slot only if the mutation's policy preempts the run.
6. Every caller that asks whether the session is busy gets the same answer, because they read one value.
7. A session cannot stay busy without a live run for longer than the watchdog bound.

## Decisions to record in the doc

- **Name and home module.** The recommendation is to grow the reply-operation registry and move it to `src/sessions/`, because both `src/auto-reply` and `src/gateway` call it.
- **Interrupt with a waiting backlog.** Recommendation: follow the documented behavior. Abort the running turn, run the newest message next, and keep the older waiting messages in order after it.
- **What counts as busy** during `finishing`, `preparing`, and deferred maintenance.
- **Steering during compaction.** Recommendation: keep today's rule (reject the steer and leave the input queued), but model it as the input staying in the mailbox.
- **Heartbeat inputs.** Recommendation: keep dropping them while the session is busy.
- **Which mutations preempt a run.** `/new` and `/reset` preempt today. Decide for `sessions.delete` and manual `/compact`.
- **Which inputs enter the mailbox:** channel messages, Gateway `chat.send` and agent RPC turns, subagent completion announcements, cron and heartbeat wakes, and stop requests.

## Acceptance

- The doc, statechart module, and harness are merged. The harness runs without real timers or a Gateway boot, and the PR states its measured cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`).
- The harness includes a regression that fails for interrupt with a waiting backlog.
- CODEOWNERS for `src/auto-reply/reply`, `src/sessions`, and `src/gateway` have reviewed the recorded decisions.

## Dependencies

None. Every other child issue of #160737 depends on this one.

Still open: running that harness against the real controller for invariants 1–7, including a regression for an interrupt with a waiting backlog.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agents misread `github_publish`. They conclude they can't land a PR, give up on a refused publish they believed had succeeded, or chase an unrelated `workspacePath` error.

## User Impact

User impact: `github_publish` now tells agents its limits and their next step. Only messages change; no behavior changes.
- **Landing scope:** `inspect`, `ready`, `merge` and `close` act only on the session's published or bound PR (including one bound with `prepare_pr`), or a delegated child's `publishingSessionKey`. Any other PR lands through the repository's native route (`scripts/pr` for OpenClaw). In one session, an agent concluded a PR "couldn't be merged" when the native route worked.
- **Publishing:** with `workspacePath`, `started` is not success. The result, which may be a refusal, resumes the session as the next turn. Running background commands, unfinished children, open terminals or another active run refuse preparation. A session publishes one checkout; use a separate session for another.
- **`readiness`:** says it doesn't check that busy condition. When the conversation has no bound checkout, the result adds a `next` line saying how to publish.
- **Errors:** a call that fills optional fields with placeholders now says to omit them, instead of "workspacePath is only available for local host publication". `readiness` and `inspect_pr` name the fields to remove.

## Why This Change Was Made

An investigation of two weeks of publisher failures on a production Gateway found these wordings behind repeated agent mistakes:
- 121 calls rejected with the misleading `workspacePath` error.
- 9 "different checkout" refusals with no warning in the description.
- Wrong-target `inspect`/`ready` calls.
- A refused publish reported only in the following turn.

The behavior fixes are separate: #196077 (stopped background commands blocking publish) and #196083 (ClawRouter GPT placeholder arguments).

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/agents/tools/github-publish-tool.test.ts src/agents/tools/github-publish-tool.handoff.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 30 + 8 passing. The two new behavioral tests fail on base and pass with the change; a description-only test was dropped at review.
- `prompt:snapshots:check` reports the snapshots are current, and `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` passes (14/14).
- `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test` and `check:test-lines-ratchet` all pass. The ratchet uses a 32-line allocation for the new tests.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A browser with no Gateway credential has no way to ask for one. Today it needs a pasted token, or a one-time link from `openclaw dashboard` carried over from the host. On a headless Gateway reached over SSH, both mean moving a secret by hand.

## User Impact

- A browser can pair without a token, link or host browser. Approving its code on the host pairs it as an ordinary operator device with the Control UI's admin scopes. That is the same result as approving it with `openclaw devices approve`, so it appears in `openclaw devices list` and the Devices page, and `openclaw devices remove` ends its access.
- New CLI command `openclaw pair <code>` and a new public route, both documented in `/cli/pair` and `/web/control-ui/connect-and-pair`.
- A browser that is already paired with a revoked or narrowed operator token keeps that limit. Its code is refused, and the message names `openclaw dashboard` or `openclaw devices remove <id>` as the next step. The owner handoff stays with `openclaw dashboard` and onboarding.
- Pairing works when browser storage is blocked or full. The approved token is kept for the life of the page, as the browser's device identity already is, so the page still connects and **Forget this browser** still clears it. A reload in that state needs pairing again.
- When `gateway.roles` is configured, bootstrap connections need a verified identity, so code pairing is refused there the same way `openclaw dashboard` links are.
- **Known low-impact limit:** a network client that rotates its source address can keep the 32-row pending table full, so other browsers see "Too many pairing requests". State stays bounded and nobody can replace another browser's request. Token and `openclaw dashboard` sign-in keep working.
- On a plain `http://` address, anyone on that network can read Gateway traffic after pairing, as with any plain-HTTP Control UI.

## Why This Change Was Made

1. The login gate's sign-in card gains a **Pair with a code instead** link. It opens a card that holds only pairing. **Get a code** shows `openclaw pair ABCD-EFGH` and a Browser ID while the browser waits. The link is offered only when the selected Gateway URL matches the page's scheme (`ws:` for `http:`, `wss:` for `https:`), host and base path.

   ![Sign-in card with code pairing link](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b0598b57-272f-4ea4-9d85-4c476a42c6e4)

   ![Pairing card waiting with command and Browser ID](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f421e08d-c6a2-4cb1-807c-b0885c26c1aa)

   ![Pairing card waiting at phone width](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d572f64c-71da-4a82-891a-edd473332bf0)

2. On the host, over SSH if needed, `openclaw pair` shows who is asking and waits for an answer:

   ```text
   A browser is asking to pair with administrator access to this Gateway.

     Code                34EL-ZNRU
     Browser (reported)  Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10_15_7) ... Safari/605.1.15
     Address             127.0.0.1
     Page (reported)     http://127.0.0.1:18789
     Browser ID          e2de4320
     Requested           just now

   Approve only if you opened this page yourself and it shows this code and Browser ID.
   If someone sent you this code or command, answer no: approving gives their browser administrator control of this Gateway.
   Approve this browser? [y/N]
   ```

3. The waiting browser keeps its device token for that Gateway and connects with it.

   ![Control UI connected after approval](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6952e4cd-4691-4d4f-81c0-fe40e85439ac)

### How it works

- **`POST <base>/__openclaw__/browser-pair/start`** is public and same-origin. Each filed request spends the source's pairing budget under the Gateway's auth rate limit. It takes a signature from the browser's device key and files one row in a new `device_pairing_browser_requests` table, returning a request ID and an eight-character code.
- **`device.pair.code`** requires `operator.admin`.
  - With `code`, it returns the request.
  - With `requestId` and `decision`, it settles exactly that request.
  - Approval files an operator pairing request for the request's key and approves it through the existing approval kernel, using the approving caller's scopes. The browser's own earlier pending requests are closed, not merged into the grant.
- **`POST .../collect`** returns the outcome only to a signature from the requesting key.
  - After approval it returns the paired device's operator token, read from the device record, until the request expires.
  - Collect has its own budget, spent only by invalid signatures and unknown requests, so filing requests cannot lock a waiting browser out of its answer.
- **Expiry and rotation:** the request deadline and the shared-auth generation are checked again when the database writer takes the approval. An approval that waited past expiry or a shared-secret rotation rolls back. Collect checks the deadline again right before it answers, so a collect that waited past expiry answers `expired`.

### Security properties

- The code names a request and is not a bearer secret.
- On the signed pairing and WebSocket paths, the device token works only with the requesting key. Treat it as a secret, like any operator token.
- Code-paired tokens carry the Gateway's shared-auth generation, so rotating the shared secret retires them, like tokens issued at connect.
- An administrator revoked while their approval waits is refused at the final effect, and nothing is issued.
- A collected token is handed out only while it is the token that approval issued; rotation, revocation or removal ends collection.
- Requests expire after ten minutes. At most 32 are pending. Filing and invalid collects are each limited per source.
- **Origin policy:** the route uses the Gateway's browser origin policy, including the check that a loopback page came from a loopback socket. It is a CSRF guard, not a network boundary; authority comes from host approval and the key proof.
- `Browser` and `Page` are marked `(reported)` because the requester chooses them.
- The request table is covered by the secret-table policy, so redacted backups omit it.
- Without a terminal the CLI approves nothing unless `--yes` is passed. The page never suggests `--yes`.

### Decisions for review

- **Ordinary operator pairing, not the owner handoff.** Approval goes through the same approval rules as `openclaw devices approve`. The result is a normal paired device, so the existing ways of listing it, narrowing its token and removing it all apply.
- **Worker-private issuer selection.** The browser-pairing worker supplies the live shared-auth generation directly to the approval kernel. Public Plugin SDK approval options cannot select an issuer, including through extra JavaScript object properties. Browser generation binding and existing scope/revocation checks are preserved.
- **Page-lifetime token fallback.** When storage rejects a write, the device-token store keeps a page-lifetime copy, as the device identity does. This applies to every user of that store, not only pairing.
- **Separate table for unauthenticated input.** Route input stays out of the list operators approve from, including `openclaw devices approve --latest`. Only an admin's decision turns it into a pairing.
- **One additive protocol method and one additive lazy table.** No protocol version change.
- **Test-line allocation.** `config/test-lines-allocations/browser-pair-code.txt` covers the net test lines this PR adds.

## Evidence

### Current qualification — November 10, `6470ceb`

Daniel’s [identity-loader simplification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6470cebe66d91dfdefbd692da76ec540fc14c20d) preserves the issuer repair and assigns the active identity on all three successful return paths. Focused identity/token/credential tests pass **43/43**. Independent autoreview of the complete committed range `a928ca1..6470ceb` finished with no actionable P0–P2 findings; earlier full-range and issuer reviews remain historical supporting evidence.

[CI run 42720533533, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42720533533) completed with 102 terminal jobs and no cancellations. Performance, all UI unit shards, type/lint jobs, PostgreSQL conformance, and security-fast passed. New-session boot JavaScript is **803,267 B gzip against an 803,364 B ceiling**. The unchanged total-CSS overage remains an advisory warning, not a claim of zero warnings.

The only failed roots are [session ownership (2/7)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42720533533/job/129513675733), with 14px spacing versus 13px expected, and [native conversation (5/7)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42720533533/job/129513675766), with a 56px header versus 64px expected. They match the actual main failures in [ownership job129450751868](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42702382436/job/129450751868) and [native job129450751908, shard3/7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42702382436/job/129450751908). Equal shard names are not equivalent test coverage; the published classifier explicitly compares job names, not these signatures.

The actual tested merge is `872f5b21a3f2205005297c4a07a036321718ca77`, with parents `626bc347dd926c2dd961757643da1412b6621b22` and `6470cebe66d91dfdefbd692da76ec540fc14c20d`. Both failing test blobs and the entire styles tree are unchanged from that exact base. The older comparison-main styles differ only in inspected dashboard/usage cleanup, not the failing geometry; the test blobs are identical. No assertions or budgets were weakened.

CI and its aggregate remain **failed**, not relabeled green. Native preparation is bound to this exact head with pending GitHub gates. Required final-head maintainer security approval, enforced reviews, and native landing checks still apply. Prior packaged-browser and upgrade results below retain their recorded source provenance; this incremental qualification does not claim updater orchestration or re-execution of every earlier proof.


### Original implementation

The following records validation before the November 7 review follow-up. Current repair validation and remaining gaps are recorded below.

**Gateway suite** (`src/gateway/server.browser-pair.test.ts`, 20 cases): passes against a real Gateway. It covers:
- first-time pairing by code as an ordinary admin device, with the token refused over WebSocket for another key;
- refusing to restore a narrowed operator token;
- closing the browser's earlier pending request instead of widening the grant;
- expiry while the approval waits in the writer queue, and while a collect waits;
- a queued approval refused once its administrator is revoked through the Gateway's live revocation owner;
- rollback when authority ends at any check;
- callers holding only `operator.pairing`, `operator.read` or `operator.write`;
- a browser that still collects its approval after filing spent its source's budget (`maxAttempts=1`), while forged collects are still limited;
- rejection, unknown or expired codes, origin and key checks, and the start rate limit.

**Control UI** (223 cases across the pairing card, device-identity and device-token storage, device credentials and forgetting, the connection page, the login gate, gateway connect and the app root): passes. It includes a browser whose storage rejects writes: it still connects with its approved token through the real connect auth selection, and that token is listed and forgotten through the real forget path.

**Regressions proven:**
- The storage, forget, collect-budget, token-rotation, collect-expiry and incomplete-stored-identity tests fail without their fixes.
- With the expiry recheck, the narrowed-token refusal or the superseded-request cleanup disabled, its test fails.

**Static checks:** core, UI and the touched test typecheck shards, plus oxlint and oxfmt on changed files, are clean. The generated protocol validators, Kysely types and Postgres schema verify.

**Not covered:**
- the full suite;
- a live browser run on this head, including real blocked storage;
- a browser on a different machine from the Gateway;
- trusted-proxy and Tailscale Serve deployments;
- the Postgres state engine;
- an upgrade from the latest stable;
- translated strings, which `control-ui-locale-refresh` adds.

## Review follow-up — November 7

Pushed as [`26338b1`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191513/commits/26338b121d8e9d93409caed8c0544c808715f4cf).

- Cancel now withdraws a pending request in the authoritative worker. Only confirmed removal reports cancellation; missing requests are terminal, and approval winning the race does not revoke the device or silently connect the browser.
- Direct browser-code pairing is hidden in OpenClaw ID remote/embedded contexts. Gateways with configured roles explicitly require normal identity-aware sign-in; approval rechecks current policy instead of issuing an unusable grant or bypassing role restrictions.
- The card identifies administrator access (not guest invitation), says to run the command on the Gateway host, and shows bounded reconnect/cancellation retry states while retaining the same request.

CI follow-up [`2c96e0d`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191513/commits/2c96e0d36ebcec31594455be5200a3b3e99975fa) registers the new browser proof in the serial E2E inventory expectation. The three CI inventory failures were reproduced locally; all 15 inventory tests now pass (15.96s), with lint and formatting clean. This follow-up changes no production behavior.

**Repair validation:** 23 Gateway pairing tests, 2 HTTP tests, 3 worker tests, 66 UI tests (including 23 pairing tests), and 4 CLI tests pass. Regression checks fail against the pre-repair boundary/UI implementations. Core/UI and selected Gateway-test typechecks, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks pass.

One real Chromium/source-Gateway scenario proves first-time approval, token connection/reload, interrupted polling, confirmed withdrawal preventing subsequent approval, and approval winning cancellation. Approval uses the real administrator RPC; packaged CLI launch was not qualified because its worker build required unavailable cross-platform downloads in the offline sandbox. Existing CLI behavior is covered separately by its unit suite.

Local runner durations: Gateway pairing 26.79s; focused UI pairing 1.18s; related UI suite 3.10s; real-browser lifecycle 108.36s. CI timings will be supplied by this head's CI run. The single longer browser scenario proves the HTTP/WebSocket/UI/persistence boundary that the fast tests cannot. A separate 520-line regression allocation covers the withdrawal, identity-policy, reconnect/remote-ingress, and real-browser proof additions; the shared baseline is unchanged.

[Inspected before/after screenshots and repair evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191513#issuecomment-6700537343). Independent review through P2 found only pre-repair index defects, all addressed by the reviewed working-tree repairs included in this commit.

## November 7 integration candidate — `24bd44e` (historical)

The current integration commit is [`24bd44e9c48ce4596b2ba4233b76fddc7357f275`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191513/commits/24bd44e9c48ce4596b2ba4233b76fddc7357f275), incorporating main `d77362b0`. The inventory resolution retains both the browser-pair proof and upstream gateway-fresh-visit case.

- The real Gateway now belongs to the E2E suite lifecycle, and successful approvals run the actual packaged `openclaw pair` CLI. The source-only bootstrap was removed. This supersedes the packaged-CLI qualification gap noted above.
- The packaged CLI/Chromium scenario passes, including same-request offline recovery, authoritative withdrawal, approval winning cancellation, token connection/reload, and cleanup (36.95s including fixture setup).
- All 15 E2E inventory tests pass. Core/UI typechecks, touched type-aware lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. The separate review-repair test allocation is now 505 lines.

Settings, password, API key, device identity, role scopes, and exact node/operator tokens survived without re-pairing or rotation; missing-password rejection remained enforced. The integration test passed in 76.15s. This qualifies binary handoff and data compatibility, not updater download/service-restart orchestration.

### Packaged CLI → browser connection: retained runtime evidence

This excerpt is from the successful packaged lifecycle run used to qualify `24bd44e9c48ce4596b2ba4233b76fddc7357f275` (November 7). It reuses that completed run; it is not a newly executed test. ## Worker-private issuer follow-up — `a928ca1` (historical)

Published as [a928ca1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/a928ca1896672ccb91fdbc324e3bb3dd81ccf361), preserving the existing PR ancestry. issue.body:
Fixes #187590

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an automation created in a dashboard chat pauses on its own when automatic session maintenance archives that chat for being idle. This happens after 7 days by default, or through `pruneAfter` or `maxEntries`.

## User Impact

User impact: a conversation that created an enabled automation is no longer archived by automatic maintenance, so weekly reports, watchers and reminders keep running even if nobody opens the chat. Disabling or removing the automation makes the chat eligible again. Archiving or deleting the chat yourself still asks for confirmation (#184818) and still pauses its automations (#178965).

## Why This Change Was Made

Since #178965, an automation pauses when the conversation that created it is archived. Scheduled runs never touch that conversation (#185341), so it looks idle to maintenance. This PR registers a session-maintenance preserve provider fed from the cron service's loaded jobs. It uses the same mechanism as pinned rows and active work, so stale-dashboard archiving, age retention and the entry cap all honor it.

- Only enabled jobs protect a chat, and only the exact creating conversation. The provider resolves that conversation with `resolveScheduledPrincipal`, the same call occurrence admission uses before it pauses. Wake, delivery and run-session bindings don't pin anything.
- Under `maxEntries`, a protected chat still counts toward the cap, the same as a pinned chat. If protection prevents reaching the cap, the store stays above it, as documented.
- No new config option. Docs are updated in `docs/gateway/config-agents/sessions.md` and `docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md`.

- **Gateway startup:** cron loads its jobs in the background, after post-ready maintenance has started. A preserve provider can now report `isPending()`. While any provider is pending, the snapshot carries `archivingDeferred` and the planner skips only the archiving actions: stale-dashboard, `pruneAfter` age and `maxEntries` cap. Everything else runs as today, including removal of disposable runtime rows. The planner change is generic; nothing in it is cron-specific.
  - The Gateway's cron provider is pending from the moment a cron service is created until its jobs register. This includes hot-reload replacements, which are built directly: the replacement arms pending while its predecessor still serves, so the gap after the predecessor unregisters stays protected. A reload that switches cron to disabled builds its replacement with `cronEnabled=false`, which clears any leftover pending state, so archiving isn't paused for the rest of the process.
  - If cron is disabled (`cron.enabled: false` or `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CRON=1`), or no cron service is created, the provider never becomes pending, so archiving proceeds. A disabled scheduler still loads its jobs, and the parents of enabled jobs stay protected. That's deliberate: re-enabling cron must not find those jobs paused because maintenance archived their chats while it was off.
  - If the cron load fails, the provider stays pending, so archiving waits until a later start succeeds. Not archiving errs on the safe side: a missed archive is a cosmetic sidebar delay, but a wrong archive silently stops the user's automations.
  - **Cost:** while the load stays failed, automatic archiving is paused for the whole process, so the unarchived session count can grow past `maxEntries` until cron starts. The Gateway logs one warning per process: `automatic session archiving is paused: automations failed to load`. There are no timers or retries; a later successful start, such as a config reload or restart, resumes archiving.
  - Doctor runs out of process and can't see this runtime-only state, so it isn't surfaced there. The warning and the existing cron start error are the signal.
  - A commit whose planning saw "ready" but whose final protection check sees "pending" is rejected and replanned, like any newly protected row.

Known limits:
- While a provider is pending, disposable runtime rows such as sub-agent sessions are still pruned. A job whose creating conversation is a sub-agent session can still lose its parent in that window, as it already could before this PR.
- A local `openclaw sessions cleanup --dry-run` runs without the Gateway's jobs. `--enforce` runs in the Gateway and honors the protection.

## Evidence

- **Unit (real maintenance planner):** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/session-automation-index.maintenance.test.ts src/gateway/session-automation-index.test.ts`: 20 passed. The tests cover each of the stale-dashboard, `pruneAfter` and `maxEntries` phases:
  - An idle chat with an enabled bound automation is kept, its job stays enabled, and admission's `classifyScheduledParent` still reports `current`.
  - The same chat with a disabled automation, or none, is archived as before.
- **Red on base:** with the provider registration removed, the three "keeps" tests fail.
- **Before cron loads (unit, all three phases):** with the Gateway's cron service created but not yet loaded, maintenance archives nothing and still prunes the disposable subagent row. Once jobs register, only the protected parent is kept. With no cron service, archiving proceeds as before. After a failed load, archiving stays deferred and the warning is emitted once. A hot-reload test covers the predecessor-to-replacement handoff; it fails when a replacement doesn't arm pending while a source is registered. A second test covers a reload from enabled (not yet loaded) to disabled and checks that archiving resumes. Red: with `isPending` forced to false, the three deferral tests fail.
- **Shared maintenance suites:** `store.pruning`, `store-maintenance.dashboard-archive`, the `session-accessor.sqlite-maintenance-{kick,cap,worker,writer}` tests, `cleanup-service.{cap-archive,deferred-sources}` and `sqlite-exact-read`: 9 files passed.
- **Static checks:** `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint and oxfmt on changed files: clean.
- **Real Gateway, local (mock-openai QA scenario):**
  - A real turn in another chat triggers automatic maintenance, which archives the idle chats with a disabled automation and with none.
  - The chat with the enabled automation stays unarchived, including after `sessions.cleanup --enforce`.
  - Its job runs `ok` and stays enabled.
  - Re-enabling the archived control's job pauses it with the "it was archived" notice.
- **Test-line budget:** the new regression tests add 168 net test lines. `config/test-lines-allocations/196297-automation-parent-retention.txt` grants exactly that, as `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` requires.
- **Crabbox AWS proof on `6b7c92c9`**. The final head `89097433` changes only the test-line allocation file; no runtime, test or doc file differs from the proven head:
  - Run `run_94e3713e8a808a96b20bd63fbff0b901`, lease `cbx_c5d662ff7d0e` (c7a.8xlarge, us-east-1). Exit 0; the lease is released.
  - All 21 changed and proof files on the box are sha256-identical to the head.
  - Command: `crabbox run --provider aws -- bash proof.sh`. The script runs the QA scenario, then the upgrade script.
  - **QA scenario `cron-automation-parent-retention`** (real Gateway, mock-openai, `archiveDashboardAfter: 6s`), 5/5 steps passed:
    - Automatic maintenance, triggered by a real turn in another chat, archives the idle chat with a disabled automation and the idle chat with none.
    - The idle chat with an enabled automation stays unarchived through that pass and through `sessions.cleanup --enforce`.
    - Its job then runs `ok`, reaches the model, and stays enabled.
    - Re-enabling the control's job pauses it: "it was archived".
  - **Upgrade from v2026.11.2** (same state dir, `doctor --fix`, then the PR build with `archiveDashboardAfter: 5s`). All 8 checks passed, 0 failed:
    - Baseline on v2026.11.2: the idle chat with an enabled automation is archived. Stable has no archived-parent pause, so its job still runs.
    - On the PR build, chats and jobs created on stable before the upgrade, and chats and jobs created after it, behave the same:
      - The chat with an enabled automation is kept through automatic maintenance and enforce cleanup. Its job runs `ok`, reaches the model and stays enabled.
      - The chat with a disabled automation is archived (`stale-dashboard`). Its job, once re-enabled, pauses with the archived-parent notice, which shows the parent link survived the upgrade.

<details><summary>Upgrade proof results.jsonl (abridged)</summary>

```

{"check":"stable-enabled-automation-chat-kept","pass":true}
{"check":"post-upgrade-control-chat-archived","pass":true}
{"check":"post-upgrade-enabled-automation-chat-kept","pass":true}
{"check":"stable-protected-automation-still-runs","pass":true,"detail":{"run":{"status":"ok"},"enabledAfter":true}}
{"check":"stable-archived-control-pauses-when-reenabled","pass":true,"detail":{"status":"skipped"}}
{"check":"post-upgrade-protected-automation-still-runs","pass":true,"detail":{"run":{"status":"ok"},"enabledAfter":true}}
{"check":"post-upgrade-archived-control-pauses-when-reenabled","pass":true,"detail":{"status":"skipped"}}
{"observation":"automatic-maintenance-archived-controls-within-30s","detail":{"archived":true}}
```
</details>

issue.body:
## Executive summary

Heartbeats run as ordinary inputs in the session mailbox, but before reserving one the heartbeat runner checks command, cron, recovery, and controller activity, including any active session for the agent, and skips the heartbeat if anything looks busy. That duplicate busy check can drop heartbeats the mailbox would have handled. This issue moves the decision into mailbox admission, which already drops a heartbeat while competing work owns the session.

Part of #160737. Depends on #160740.

## Problem

- The heartbeat runner skips on its own busy checks before reserving a mailbox input ([`src/infra/heartbeat-runner-execution.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2e022fc146b656e1466099dc8ac02fb277666fc5/src/infra/heartbeat-runner-execution.ts)). This risks lost heartbeats, not overlapping turns.
- The mailbox already applies the documented rule: drop a heartbeat while competing session work owns admission.

## Recommended implementation

1. Keep the runner's checks that are not about session busyness (disabled, quiet hours, empty heartbeat file, no route).
2. Delete the busy checks and reserve the heartbeat input; mailbox admission drops it under the existing rule.

## Acceptance

- The heartbeat runner has no session-busy check of its own.
- Tests: heartbeat while idle runs; while a turn runs it is dropped by the mailbox with a recorded reason; while a cron run is active on another session it still runs.
