Steering adds a message to a turn that is already running. Most steering goes through the session mailbox, so the controller records that the message was accepted and what happened to it. Three callers still inject messages straight into the running backend: Talk, agent-to-agent `sessions_send`, and subagent completion announcements. The controller then does not know those messages exist, so they can be lost or attributed to the wrong turn. This issue gives the controller one injection path that every caller uses, and makes the runner's low-level injection call internal to the controller.

Part of #160737. Depends on #160740. Coordinates with #163058.

## Problem

Found by a read-only trace of the draft implementation (#162433):

- `sessions_send` with an explicit steer, or fire-and-forget delivery to an active session, calls `queueEmbeddedAgentMessageWithOutcomeAsync` and reports "steered" without reserving a controller input ([`src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.delivery.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2e022fc146b656e1466099dc8ac02fb277666fc5/src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.delivery.ts)). Normal `sessions_send` delivery goes through Gateway `agent` and is fine.
- Subagent active-wake announcements call the same function directly; Gateway `agent` is only the fallback ([`src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-active-wake.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2e022fc146b656e1466099dc8ac02fb277666fc5/src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-active-wake.ts)).
- Talk steer and follow-up call guarded or unguarded embedded injection ([`src/talk/agent-run-control.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2e022fc146b656e1466099dc8ac02fb277666fc5/src/talk/agent-run-control.ts), [`src/talk/agent-run-control.runtime.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2e022fc146b656e1466099dc8ac02fb277666fc5/src/talk/agent-run-control.runtime.ts)).
- The low-level path selects the native attachment and calls its injection queue ([`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2e022fc146b656e1466099dc8ac02fb277666fc5/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.ts)).

## Recommended implementation

1. Add one controller API to submit an input with policy `steer` to a session. It reserves the input, attempts injection into the exact active operation, and on a definite rejection leaves the input queued, as mailbox steering already does.
2. Move `sessions_send`, subagent announcements (shared with #163058), and Talk onto it.
3. Make the runner's injection function internal to the controller. The plugin SDK export `queueEmbeddedAgentMessageWithOutcome` is a public contract: keep its signature and implement it on the new API.

## Acceptance

- Outside the controller, the only caller of runner injection is the plugin SDK export, which delegates to the controller API.
- Every steered message has a mailbox input with one recorded disposition.
- QA: `sessions_send` steer into an active session; a subagent completion while its parent is running; a Talk steer during a tool call; each also during compaction (falls back to queued).

issue.body:
## Executive summary

When an agent is waiting for an `ask_user` answer, the next inbound message is offered to the question first. If the sender is not allowed to answer, the message is consumed and the user gets an error, even when they meant to send an ordinary message. This issue keeps the refusal notice but lets the refused message continue into the session mailbox, queued behind the waiting turn like any other message.

Part of #160737. Depends on #160740.

## Problem

- Inbound replies are first offered to the pending question through `runReplyQuestionInput` ([`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-question-input.ts:34`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2e022fc146b656e1466099dc8ac02fb277666fc5/src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-question-input.ts#L34)) and `claimPendingAgentQuestionAnswerFromCaller` ([`src/agents/harness/gateway-question.ts:226`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2e022fc146b656e1466099dc8ac02fb277666fc5/src/agents/harness/gateway-question.ts#L226)).
- When the caller does not match the question's policy, the message is consumed and the user sees "The answer was not sent: … Use the question controls in the Control UI" ([`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-question-input.ts:105`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2e022fc146b656e1466099dc8ac02fb277666fc5/src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-question-input.ts#L105)). It never becomes a turn.
- Pending questions themselves are correctly scoped: abort and completion of the asking turn remove the pending entry. The defect is only what happens to a refused message.

#150795 shows the worst case: every message from the session owner is refused. Its root cause is that the continuation turn after `sessions_yield` runs with internal caller identity instead of the original requester's. That is tracked in #163058.

## Recommended implementation

1. On a refused answer, send the refusal notice (or a shorter "queued as a normal message" notice) and pass the message on as a normal mailbox input.
2. Keep refusal without queueing only when the refusal reason is an authority failure that would also refuse a normal turn.

## Acceptance

- Tests: a non-answerer's message during a pending question is queued and runs after the turn; an authority failure is refused and not queued.

issue.body:
## Executive summary

OpenClaw runs a background check that looks for sessions that appear stuck and forcibly releases them by aborting runs and resetting per-session lanes. Much of that work exists because the separate ownership records can disagree about whether a session is busy. Once the controller is the only owner, a small watchdog inside it can detect a run that stopped making progress and stop it through the normal stop operation, with one set of thresholds.

Part of #160737. Depends on #160742 and #160743.

## Problem

- `recoverStuckDiagnosticSession` ([`src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts:142`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts#L142)) aborts and drains runs. It resets session lanes directly when an orphaned lane task passes its release window, or when work is still queued after an abort ([`src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts:400`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts#L400), [`src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts:438`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts#L438)).
- A coordinator module schedules these recoveries and resets diagnostic state afterwards.
- #150769: sessions waiting on an approval-gated tool call never recover and need a manual Gateway restart.

## Recommended implementation

1. The controller records progress timestamps for the run that holds the slot: model output, tool start and end, compaction start and end.
2. The watchdog keeps the documented classifications (`session.long_running`, `session.stalled`, `session.stuck`, [`docs/concepts/queue.md:208-212`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/docs/concepts/queue.md#L208-L212)) and the existing thresholds, and reads progress from the controller.
3. Its only action is `controller.stop({ source: "watchdog" })`. It does not reset lanes, because #160743 removes session lanes.
4. Decide in this issue whether approval-gated waits get a bound, which is the case in #150769, and record the decision in the #160738 doc.
5. Delete the lane-reset and reconciliation branches and the coordinator state that only served them.

## Acceptance

- The #160738 harness passes invariant 7 with a fake clock.
- Tests cover a run that stops producing progress, a run that is slow but progressing, and a run waiting on approval.
- Stuck-session recovery no longer calls `resetCommandLane`.

comment.body:
Done in #175837 (36e277d). Checked on main at b39848a:

- Stuck-session recovery (`src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts`) now ticks the controller operation's watchdog, and `resetCommandLane` no longer exists.
- `src/sessions/session-controller.watchdog.test.ts` covers stalled runs, slow runs that are still progressing, and approval waits that use the real approval expiry.

Model-harness coverage of invariant 7 stays with #160738. Closing.

issue.body:
## Executive summary

A user can stop a running turn by typing `/stop`, by typing a stop word such as "stop" or "abort", by pressing Esc in a client, or through the `chat.abort` and `sessions.abort` Gateway calls. These paths run different code and have different effects. Some stop subagents and clear waiting messages, some only abort the current turn, and only one fires the `command:stop` hook. This issue gives the controller one stop operation that records where the request came from. Every entry point then has the same effect and reports it the same way.

Part of #160737. Depends on #160739. Queue clearing depends on #160740.

## Problem

| Entry point | Code | Stops subagents | Clears waiting messages | Fires `command:stop` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stop text on the inbound fast path | `tryFastAbortFromMessage` → `executeFastAbortRequest` ([`src/auto-reply/reply/abort.ts:71`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/auto-reply/reply/abort.ts#L71), [`src/auto-reply/reply/abort-operation.ts:175`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/auto-reply/reply/abort-operation.ts#L175)) | yes | yes | no |
| `/stop` command handler | `handleStopCommand` ([`src/auto-reply/reply/commands-session-abort.ts:128`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/auto-reply/reply/commands-session-abort.ts#L128)) | yes | yes | yes |
| Bare stop word through the command handler | `handleAbortTrigger` ([`src/auto-reply/reply/commands-session-abort.ts:168`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/auto-reply/reply/commands-session-abort.ts#L168)) | no | no | no |
| `chat.abort` | `abortChatRunsForSessionKeyWithPartials`, `abortChatRunById` ([`src/gateway/server-methods/chat-abort-runtime.ts:676`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/gateway/server-methods/chat-abort-runtime.ts#L676), [`src/gateway/chat-abort.ts:530`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/gateway/chat-abort.ts#L530)) | the aborted turn's subagents, plus descendants with `cascadeDescendants` | aborts queued Gateway turns | no |
| `sessions.abort`, interrupt mode, supersession, restart | separate callers of `abortByUser`, `abortForRestart`, `supersede` | varies | varies | no |

Stop, abort, and cancel problems appear in about 470 issue titles since 2026-06-24.

## Recommended implementation

1. Add `controller.stop({ source, scope, clearWaiting, stopChildren })`. `source` is one of `user-text`, `user-command`, `client`, `rpc`, `interrupt`, `supersede`, `restart`, or `watchdog`. The defaults for each source are recorded in the #160738 doc.
2. Every entry point in the table calls it. Authorization stays at the entry point ([`src/gateway/server-methods/chat-abort-authorization.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/gateway/server-methods/chat-abort-authorization.ts)).
3. The controller records the abort cutoff, chooses the reply text ("aborted", "already finalizing", or "stopped N subagents"), and fires `command:stop` once for every user-initiated stop.
4. A stop that arrives while the run is `finishing` returns the "already finalizing" result without side effects, as it does today.
5. Remove the per-path abort sequencing and the duplicated queue-clearing calls.

## Acceptance

- Each entry point is covered by a test that asserts the same effects for the same `source`.
- QA scenarios:
  - `/stop` during a tool call
  - `/stop` during compaction
  - `/stop` while finishing
  - `/stop` with waiting follow-ups
  - `/stop` with running subagents
  - Esc from the Control UI
  - `chat.abort` for a queued turn

issue.body:
## Executive summary

A user can stop a running turn by typing `/stop`, by typing a stop word such as "stop" or "abort", by pressing Esc in a client, or through the `chat.abort` and `sessions.abort` Gateway calls. These paths run different code and have different effects. Some stop subagents and clear waiting messages, some only abort the current turn, and only one fires the `command:stop` hook. This issue gives the controller one stop operation that records where the request came from. Every entry point then has the same effect and reports it the same way.

Part of #160737. Depends on #160739. Queue clearing depends on #160740.

## Problem

| Entry point | Code | Stops subagents | Clears waiting messages | Fires `command:stop` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stop text on the inbound fast path | `tryFastAbortFromMessage` → `executeFastAbortRequest` ([`src/auto-reply/reply/abort.ts:71`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/auto-reply/reply/abort.ts#L71), [`src/auto-reply/reply/abort-operation.ts:175`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/auto-reply/reply/abort-operation.ts#L175)) | yes | yes | no |
| `/stop` command handler | `handleStopCommand` ([`src/auto-reply/reply/commands-session-abort.ts:128`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/auto-reply/reply/commands-session-abort.ts#L128)) | yes | yes | yes |
| Bare stop word through the command handler | `handleAbortTrigger` ([`src/auto-reply/reply/commands-session-abort.ts:168`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/auto-reply/reply/commands-session-abort.ts#L168)) | no | no | no |
| `chat.abort` | `abortChatRunsForSessionKeyWithPartials`, `abortChatRunById` ([`src/gateway/server-methods/chat-abort-runtime.ts:676`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/gateway/server-methods/chat-abort-runtime.ts#L676), [`src/gateway/chat-abort.ts:530`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/gateway/chat-abort.ts#L530)) | the aborted turn's subagents, plus descendants with `cascadeDescendants` | aborts queued Gateway turns | no |
| `sessions.abort`, interrupt mode, supersession, restart | separate callers of `abortByUser`, `abortForRestart`, `supersede` | varies | varies | no |

Stop, abort, and cancel problems appear in about 470 issue titles since 2026-06-24.

## Recommended implementation

1. Add `controller.stop({ source, scope, clearWaiting, stopChildren })`. `source` is one of `user-text`, `user-command`, `client`, `rpc`, `interrupt`, `supersede`, `restart`, or `watchdog`. The defaults for each source are recorded in the #160738 doc.
2. Every entry point in the table calls it. Authorization stays at the entry point ([`src/gateway/server-methods/chat-abort-authorization.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/gateway/server-methods/chat-abort-authorization.ts)).
3. The controller records the abort cutoff, chooses the reply text ("aborted", "already finalizing", or "stopped N subagents"), and fires `command:stop` once for every user-initiated stop.
4. A stop that arrives while the run is `finishing` returns the "already finalizing" result without side effects, as it does today.
5. Remove the per-path abort sequencing and the duplicated queue-clearing calls.

## Acceptance

- Each entry point is covered by a test that asserts the same effects for the same `source`.
- QA scenarios:
  - `/stop` during a tool call
  - `/stop` during compaction
  - `/stop` while finishing
  - `/stop` with waiting follow-ups
  - `/stop` with running subagents
  - Esc from the Control UI
  - `chat.abort` for a queued turn
- `docs/concepts/queue.md` and the `/stop` command docs describe one behavior.

issue.body:
## Executive summary

When a message arrives during a running turn, OpenClaw can add it to that turn (`steer`), queue it for later (`followup`), merge several into one later turn (`collect`), or stop the turn and run the new message (`interrupt`). Waiting messages live in a separate queue with its own admission path, a retry loop, and its own bookkeeping. `interrupt` does not interrupt when other messages are already waiting. This issue makes waiting messages the controller's mailbox and applies the four modes as rules on that mailbox. A queued message then starts its turn through the same path as a first message.

Part of #160737. Depends on #160739.

## Problem

- Waiting messages live in the process-global `FOLLOWUP_QUEUES` map ([`src/auto-reply/reply/queue/state.ts:59`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/auto-reply/reply/queue/state.ts#L59)). Adoption progress is tracked in separate WeakSets, and steer candidates are parked with a `steerPending` phase ([`src/auto-reply/reply/queue/enqueue.ts:131`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/auto-reply/reply/queue/enqueue.ts#L131)).
- Queued turns use a second admission path, `admitFollowupTurn` ([`src/auto-reply/reply/followup-turn-admission.ts:105`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/auto-reply/reply/followup-turn-admission.ts#L105)). When the session is still held, it throws `FollowupRunDeferredError` and the drain loop reschedules ([`src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.ts:142`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.ts#L142), [`src/auto-reply/reply/queue/drain.ts:1305`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/auto-reply/reply/queue/drain.ts#L1305)).
- The follow-up admission path runs preflight compaction without the memory flush that the first-turn path runs.
- `interrupt` with a waiting backlog queues the new message instead of interrupting ([`src/auto-reply/reply/queue-policy.ts:22`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/auto-reply/reply/queue-policy.ts#L22)).
- Related open issues:
  - #54488: the follow-up drain holds the session lane and blocks new inbound messages for 20 to 30 minutes.
  - #147759: WebChat prompts are delayed 8 to 62 minutes after steering failures.
  - #159692: a queued turn fails when compaction rewrites the transcript while it waits.

## Recommended implementation

1. **Mailbox.** The controller keeps an ordered list of inputs for each session. Each input records its kind, the queue policy in effect, and its delivery context. The existing limits move into the controller unchanged: debounce (500 ms default), cap (20), drop policy (`old`, `new`, `summarize`), and collect batching by delivery context.
2. **Steer.** For a `steer` input, the controller tries to inject it into the current run through the runner's injection primitive. If the runner rejects it (compacting, not streaming, authority mismatch), the input stays at its position in the mailbox. The separate `steerPending` parking state is removed.
3. **One admission path.** When a run settles, the controller chooses the next input or collect batch and starts the turn through the same admission and preflight path as a first message, including the memory flush. `admitFollowupTurn`, `FollowupRunDeferredError`, and the reschedule loop are removed.
4. **Interrupt.** Apply the rule recorded in #160738. The recommendation is to abort the running turn, run the newest message next, and keep older waiting messages in order after it.
5. **Heartbeat.** Keep dropping heartbeat inputs while the session is busy.
6. **Legacy mode names.** `normalizePersistedQueueMode` maps `queue` and `steer-backlog` at read time ([`src/auto-reply/reply/queue/normalize.ts:28-40`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/auto-reply/reply/queue/normalize.ts#L28-L40)). If this change touches queue-mode reading, move that mapping to a Doctor config migration, which is where the repository rules assign legacy normalization.

## Acceptance

- `FOLLOWUP_QUEUES`, the adoption WeakSets, `admitFollowupTurn`, and `FollowupRunDeferredError` are deleted.
- The #160738 harness passes invariants 2 to 4 for all four modes.
- QA scenarios on at least one channel:
  - `steer` during a tool call
  - `steer` during compaction (falls back to a queued turn)
  - `followup` and `collect` with three rapid messages
  - `interrupt` with an empty queue and with a waiting backlog
  - queue overflow with `summarize`
- Docs: [`docs/concepts/queue.md`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/docs/concepts/queue.md) and [`docs/concepts/queue-steering.md`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/docs/concepts/queue-steering.md) describe the mailbox behavior.

issue.body:
## Executive summary

Many parts of OpenClaw ask "is this session busy?" and each checks a different record. For a short time after a turn starts, ends, or is replaced, those records can disagree. When that happens, a session can look busy with nothing running, or a new turn can start while the old one is still finishing. This issue makes the session controller the one place that answers the question and holds the running turn. Callers stop checking several records and combining the results.

Part of #160737. Depends on #160738.

## Problem

- Admission computes "busy" by combining the reply-operation registry, the embedded run registry, and a restart-recovery owner check ([`src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run-admission.ts:482-514`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run-admission.ts#L482-L514)).
- The two run registries use different keys. `ReplyOperation` is keyed by session key. `ACTIVE_EMBEDDED_RUNS` is keyed by session id ([`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run-state.ts:184`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run-state.ts#L184)).
- `resolveEmbeddedAgentRunProgressState` merges both and documents that they are "independent lifecycle owners" ([`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.ts:1016-1071`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.ts#L1016-L1071)).
- #148707 is one result: a reply is lost when a second run displaces an in-flight turn on the same session.

Busy and ownership queries outside the owning modules (non-test files at `5c30c9a`):

| API | Files |
| --- | --- |
| `isEmbeddedAgentRunActive` | 21 |
| `waitForEmbeddedAgentRunEnd` | 12 |
| `isEmbeddedAgentRunStreaming` | 5 |
| `resolveEmbeddedAgentRunProgressState`, `isReplyRunActiveForSessionId` | several in `src/auto-reply` and `src/gateway` |

## Recommended implementation

1. Extend the reply-operation registry into the controller as decided in #160738. Its run slot is the only record of which run holds a session.
2. `setActiveEmbeddedRun` ([`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.ts:1534`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.ts#L1534)) registers the attempt's handle with the controller operation that owns the run. The controller holds the handle for as long as the run holds the slot.
3. Add controller queries: `isBusy(sessionKey)`, `currentRun(sessionKey)`, `waitForIdle(sessionKey)`, and `progress(sessionKey)`. Move every caller of the APIs in the table to them.
4. Keep a run-id index of handles inside the runner only for attempt-level operations, such as the injection primitive in `run/attempt-queue-message.ts`. Remove the session-level busy queries from the runner.
5. Register main-session restart recovery runs as controller runs, so admission no longer needs a separate recovery-owner check.
6. Delete the replaced queries, their exports from `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner.ts`, and their tests.

## Out of scope

Queueing (#160740), stop (#160742), and lifecycle mutations (#160743). This issue changes where busy state and run ownership live. It does not change what happens to a new input.

## Acceptance

- A search for the removed APIs outside the controller finds nothing.
- The #160738 harness drives the real controller for start, settle, supersede, and recovery runs and passes invariants 1, 4, and 6.
- QA proof: two rapid messages in `steer` and `followup` modes on one channel, plus the same through `chat.send`, with unchanged transcripts and replies.
- The PR reports removed production and test lines.

- `setActiveEmbeddedRun` registers the attempt's handle with the owning controller operation and requires host admission. The runner keeps only the run-ID handle index this issue allows for attempt-level operations.

Two stale mock keys remain in `extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply.test-harness.ts`; they are test-only. Model-harness coverage of invariants 1, 4 and 6 stays with #160738. Closing.

- #148707 is one result: a reply is lost when a second run displaces an in-flight turn on the same session.

Busy and ownership queries outside the owning modules (non-test files at `5c30c9a`):

| API | Files |
| --- | --- |
| `isEmbeddedAgentRunActive` | 21 |
| `waitForEmbeddedAgentRunEnd` | 12 |
| `isEmbeddedAgentRunStreaming` | 5 |
| `resolveEmbeddedAgentRunProgressState`, `isReplyRunActiveForSessionId` | several in `src/auto-reply` and `src/gateway` |

## Recommended implementation

1. Extend the reply-operation registry into the controller as decided in #160738. Its run slot is the only record of which run holds a session.
2. `setActiveEmbeddedRun` ([`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.ts:1534`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.ts#L1534)) registers the attempt's handle with the controller operation that owns the run. The controller holds the handle for as long as the run holds the slot.
3. Add controller queries: `isBusy(sessionKey)`, `currentRun(sessionKey)`, `waitForIdle(sessionKey)`, and `progress(sessionKey)`. Move every caller of the APIs in the table to them.
4. Keep a run-id index of handles inside the runner only for attempt-level operations, such as the injection primitive in `run/attempt-queue-message.ts`. Remove the session-level busy queries from the runner.
5. Register main-session restart recovery runs as controller runs, so admission no longer needs a separate recovery-owner check.
6. Delete the replaced queries, their exports from `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner.ts`, and their tests.

## Out of scope

Queueing (#160740), stop (#160742), and lifecycle mutations (#160743). This issue changes where busy state and run ownership live. It does not change what happens to a new input.

## Acceptance

- A search for the removed APIs outside the controller finds nothing.
- The #160738 harness drives the real controller for start, settle, supersede, and recovery runs and passes invariants 1, 4, and 6.
- QA proof: two rapid messages in `steer` and `followup` modes on one channel, plus the same through `chat.send`, with unchanged transcripts and replies.
- The PR reports removed production and test lines.

issue.body:
## Executive summary

A few code paths still stop a running turn by aborting the backend directly instead of going through the controller: killing a subagent when the controller holds no record of it, replacing a session writer by run id, and ending a turn with `sessions_yield`. Each can leave the controller's record of the turn out of step with what the backend actually did. This issue routes all three through controller operations, keeping the exact backend cancellation as a step under the controller's control.

Part of #160737. Depends on #160742.

## Problem

Found by a read-only trace of the draft implementation (#162433):

- **Subagent kill fallback.** Normal kill uses `runSessionMutation` and captured operations. When the capture is empty, it calls `abortEmbeddedAgentRun` directly and clears queues separately ([`src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-control-kill-runtime.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2e022fc146b656e1466099dc8ac02fb277666fc5/src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-control-kill-runtime.ts)).
- **Writer supersede by run id.** Session bootstrap resolves the incumbent by run id and calls `supersedeEmbeddedAgentRunByRunId`, which cancels the native handle directly when one exists and falls back to the controller only when it does not ([`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/session-bootstrap.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2e022fc146b656e1466099dc8ac02fb277666fc5/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/session-bootstrap.ts), [`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2e022fc146b656e1466099dc8ac02fb277666fc5/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.ts)).
- **`sessions_yield`.** The yield queues a hidden steer and aborts the runner and session abort controllers directly ([`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-sessions-yield.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2e022fc146b656e1466099dc8ac02fb277666fc5/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-sessions-yield.ts)). A yield is a deliberate handoff, not a cancellation, so it should end the operation with its own recorded outcome.

## Recommended implementation

1. Kill with no captured operation becomes an explicit reconciliation: look up the controller entry and stop through `stopSession`; if the controller has no record, report that state instead of aborting by session id.
2. Writer supersede calls `stopSession` with source `supersede` against the exact operation.
3. `sessions_yield` ends the operation through a controller transition that records a yielded outcome, and the backend cancellation runs as part of that transition. The registry's custody of the owed continuation is unchanged (#163058).

## Acceptance

- Outside the controller, nothing calls `abortEmbeddedAgentRun`, the native handle's cancel, or `supersedeEmbeddedAgentRunByRunId` to end a session turn (the plugin SDK `abortAgentHarnessRun` export delegates to the controller).
- Tests: kill with and without a controller record; supersede of a finishing writer; yield while a steer is pending.

comment.body: Done in #175837 (36e277d). `supersedeEmbeddedAgentRunByRunId` is gone, and `abortEmbeddedAgentRun` (also exported to plugins as `abortAgentHarnessRun`) now stops a session turn through the controller's `interruptSessionTurn`. Only detached runtimes that have no session turn cancel through their own handle. Closing.

issue.body:
## Executive summary

After a Gateway restart, OpenClaw resends a main session's interrupted request. That resend goes through its own admission, capacity, and live-owner logic, so ordinary turn admission has to check a separate "recovery owner" in addition to the session controller. This issue makes the resend an ordinary controller input, so the controller decides when it runs and admission has a single source of truth.

Part of #160737. Depends on #160739 and #160743.

## Problem

- Turn admission still combines the controller with a recovery-owner check (`recoveryOwnerActive`, [`src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run-admission.ts:486-497`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2e022fc146b656e1466099dc8ac02fb277666fc5/src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run-admission.ts#L486-L497)). In the draft implementation (#162433), recovery registers as a controller lifecycle effect with an owner symbol, not as a turn, so this combined check survives.
- Recovery has its own admission and dispatch modules: `main-session-recovery-admission.ts` ([`src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-recovery-admission.ts:8`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2e022fc146b656e1466099dc8ac02fb277666fc5/src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-recovery-admission.ts#L8)), `main-session-recovery-capacity.ts`, `main-session-recovery-live-owners.ts`, and `main-session-restart-dispatch*.ts`. They decide when the resend may start, which is the controller's job.
- The resend itself reaches the mailbox: dispatch calls the internal Gateway `agent` RPC ([`src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-dispatch.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2e022fc146b656e1466099dc8ac02fb277666fc5/src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-dispatch.ts)), which reserves an ordinary input. The problem is the step before it. Recovery first creates a lifecycle effect under its owner symbol, and turn admission treats that effect as "busy", disables steering, and forces follow-up mode for any message that arrives meanwhile.

## Recommended implementation

1. The recovery runtime keeps its durable decisions (which sessions were interrupted, retry count, tombstone on exhaustion, replay safety).
2. The resend reserves an input on the session's mailbox with the recovery provenance, and runs through normal admission. A user message that arrives first is ordered by the mailbox like any other input. Decide and document whether the resend takes priority over inputs that arrive during startup.
3. Delete `recoveryOwnerActive` and the recovery-owner branch from turn admission, and delete the recovery admission, capacity, and live-owner logic that the mailbox replaces. Keep global capacity limits in the existing global lane.
4. Retry exhaustion and tombstoning stay where they are and record their outcome when the input settles.

## Acceptance

- Turn admission has no recovery-specific busy check.
- QA: Gateway restart with an interrupted main-session turn; a user message arrives before the resend; the resend fails three times and the session is tombstoned.
- Net production lines go down. Report the change against the parent commit.

issue.body:
## Executive summary

Messages sent from the Control UI, the TUI, and other Gateway clients take a separate path from channel messages. That path has its own list of waiting turns and its own table of running turns to abort. It repeats the controller's job and can disagree with it about whether a session is busy. This issue sends Gateway turns through the session controller. A message from the Control UI and a message from Telegram to the same session then queue, steer, and stop the same way.

Part of #160737. Depends on #160739 and #160740.

## Problem

- Gateway turns keep their own waiting list, `chatQueuedTurns` ([`src/gateway/chat-queued-turns.ts:100`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/gateway/chat-queued-turns.ts#L100)), referenced from 23 non-test files.
- Running Gateway turns are tracked in `chatAbortControllers`, referenced from 55 non-test files.
- `chat.send` admission implements its own interrupt handling and its own "previous run is still settling" retry response ([`src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-admission.ts:277`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-admission.ts#L277), [`src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-admission.ts:588`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5c30c9afcb5ec0d27085cbecce199ca986e532f5/src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-admission.ts#L588)).
- `chat.abort` aborts in a different order depending on whether it has a run id: queued turns first without one, the active run first with one.
- #135880: queued `chat.send` turns are lost when the Gateway restarts.

## Recommended implementation

1. `chat.send` and agent RPC turns submit an input to the controller. The controller returns a disposition (started, steered, queued, or rejected). The Gateway maps that disposition onto its existing responses and events.
2. Waiting Gateway turns become controller mailbox entries, and `chatQueuedTurns` is deleted.
3. Per-run abort handles move to the controller's run slot. The Gateway keeps only the mapping from RPC run id to controller run that it needs for responses and events. Split `chatAbortControllers` callers into two groups: those that only need that mapping, and those that abort, which call the #160742 stop operation.
4. `session_pending_inputs` custody for accepted `chat.send` inputs is unchanged. The controller consumes those rows the way the Gateway does today. Making the whole mailbox durable is #160745.
5. The Gateway protocol schema does not change. If a response shape has to change, that needs protocol approval under the repository rules before the change.

## Acceptance

- `chatQueuedTurns` is deleted, and `chatAbortControllers` no longer holds per-run abort state.
- Mixed-surface QA: Telegram and the Control UI send to the same session in `steer`, `followup`, and `interrupt` modes, with identical queueing results.
- Control UI end-to-end proof for send, queued send, abort, and abort of a queued send, using the existing mocked-Gateway harness.
- Restart behavior for accepted `chat.send` inputs is unchanged: they come back as `interrupted` pending inputs.

comment.body: Done in #175837 (36e277d), which landed the session-controller cutover from #165957. On main, `chatQueuedTurns` and `chatAbortControllers` no longer exist in the Gateway; the names survive only in the plugin registrar's removed-capability list. Closing.

issue.body:
### Summary

Tracking issue for making scheduled automations reliable. A scheduled `agentTurn` run executes in its own `cron:<jobId>` session that is not the conversation that created the job and carries no owner identity. Many layers decide what the run can reach from that session key, so jobs created from chat lose resources and actions the creating conversation had. This issue records the evidence, the chosen direction, and the filed work.

### Problem to solve

**Observed failures.** One maintainer gateway recorded about 450 failed or skipped automation runs between 2026-09-20 and 2026-10-20 (2026.10.5, `27e327f`). Grouped by cause:

1. Heartbeat skipped with `no-route` (no owner DM route), about 290 skips.
2. The run lacked a tool, action or resource its task needed (most real failures):
   - `show_widget` absent and `dashboard` bound to the run's own empty board, about 50 failed refreshes of one dashboard job.
   - Knowledge reported a conversation scope with zero records for ingestion jobs.
   - The `automations` tool exposed no `wake`, so a PR babysitter could not hand control back to its parent.
3. The job's `cron:<jobId>` session was archived, so every later run fails ("Session ... is archived. Restore it before starting new work."), nightly since 2026-10-01 for one job.
4. Gateway restarts and setup timeouts.
5. A runtime change made the stored inference account incompatible ("candidate is incompatible with its recorded inference account and route").
6. A job outlived the worktree its prompt referenced (`ENOENT`).
7. No delivery channel configured.

Classes 2, 3, 5 and 6 share one cause. The job is authored in one execution context and replayed later in a different one, and nothing compares the two until a run fails.

**Why the existing fix is incomplete.** #162432 made default agent-created jobs use the owner conversation's tool policy (`*`) at run time. That fixes the tool *list*. The failures in class 2 continued after it merged, because other layers decide from the run's session identity:

- [`src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts:416-422`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/27e327f0bb58f45b4b6841ddab49cc3c6e8ba962/src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts#L416-L422) never builds pinned `show_widget` authoring for a cron run session key.
- [`src/agents/tools/cron-tool-schema.ts:38`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/27e327f0bb58f45b4b6841ddab49cc3c6e8ba962/src/agents/tools/cron-tool-schema.ts#L38) limits scheduled runs to `status`, `list`, `get`, `remove`, `runs` and `next_check`.
- `dashboard` reads the board of the run session ([`src/agents/tools/dashboard-tool.ts:247-264`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/27e327f0bb58f45b4b6841ddab49cc3c6e8ba962/src/agents/tools/dashboard-tool.ts#L247-L264)).
- The memory audience grants the owner-private vault only when the root session is a direct chat whose sender is the owner ([`src/plugins/memory-audience.ts:282-287`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/27e327f0bb58f45b4b6841ddab49cc3c6e8ba962/src/plugins/memory-audience.ts#L282-L287)). A scheduled run is neither.

**History.**
- Session targets:
  - `current` and `session:<id>` were added in #16511 (`current` resolved to `session:<creating key>` and ran inside the conversation).
  - #98755 detached session-targeted runs and #98947 reverted that the next day.
  - #98236 reintroduced detached execution for `current` without intent. See the session-target bug linked below.
  - #114328 made `current` the default for agent turns created in chat.
- Permissions:
  - #63878 set `senderIsOwner: false` for scheduled runs, and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/02182d5a303 removed it.
  - #91499, #112483, #137832 and #147969 changed what a saved creator tool snapshot means.
  - #162432 replaced default snapshots with `*`.

Each change addressed one layer.

### Proposed solution

A scheduled run is a **child of the conversation that created the job** and inherits that conversation's authority, the same model spawned sessions use. Each occurrence receives one execution context minted at admission, and every layer reads that object. Requirements:

- Existing automations keep working without a stored-data migration. The context is derived from fields jobs already store.
- A comparison-mode release logs every divergence between the new context and the existing decisions before the switch.
- Doctor reports, by job, any reduction in access.

**Filed work**

- [ ] #178812 Resolve scheduled-run authority into one per-occurrence execution context
- [ ] #178813 Scheduled agent turns get different owner-only tools on embedded and CLI runtimes
- [x] #178814 `sessionTarget: "current"` runs in a detached cron session since #98236
- [ ] #178815 Consolidate authority inheritance for spawned child sessions (follows #178812)

**Roadmap (not filed yet).** Each depends on the execution context above.

- Validate a new job against its execution context at creation, and report missing tools, actions or resources before saving.
- Require one successful rehearsal run in the scheduled context before a new job is enabled.
- Store job dependencies (sessions, worktrees, dashboards, inference accounts, delivery routes) as typed references. Check them before each run, and flag dependent jobs when one changes (archive, reset, worktree removal, model or config change).
- Separate permanent from transient failures, pause a job after repeated identical permanent failures, and send one notice.
- Retain complete run history (the run-history API covered 7 days and receipts missed failures in the observed window).
- End-to-end tests that create jobs the way users do (from chat) and run them in the scheduled context for common job types, plus a live canary job.

### Alternatives considered

- **Keep fixing layers one at a time.** The history above shows five rounds of changes to tool snapshots alone, while the dashboard, memory and action-level failures remained.
- **A separate automation principal with its own grants.** This adds a new identity users must manage. The child model matches what a user expects: an automation requested from a conversation can do what that conversation can do.
- **Stamp `spawnedBy` lineage onto cron run sessions.** This pulls in consumers that match lineage by session key only and freezes the owner bit at creation, which conflicts with per-run revalidation. Details are in the execution-context issue.

### Evidence/examples

Run-receipt error text from the observed window, after #162432:

```text
Refresh blocked: the required `show_widget` tool is unavailable, and the available dashboard tool only exposes this scheduled run's empty board, not the target dashboard.
knowledge_status grants this run conversation-only scope with zero records
Could not wake parent ... it explicitly states "waking sessions are unavailable" and exposes no `wake` action.
cron script payload failed (internal_error): Invalid arguments for tool "automations": action: must be equal to one of the allowed values (allowed: "status", "list", "get", "remove", "runs", "next_check")
Session "agent:main:cron:<jobId>" is archived. Restore it before starting new work.
Automation candidate is incompatible with its recorded inference account and route.
```

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes. @jalehman owns Automations and will open the PRs for the filed work.

### Additional information

Related, not duplicates: #166061, #140889, #118817, #149564, #171071, #177930.

issue.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Agent-turn automations with `sessionTarget: "current"` run in a detached `cron:<jobId>` session that reads only a bounded tail of the creating conversation. Before #98236 they ran inside the creating conversation. The change in #98236 was not intended. Since #114328, chat-created agent turns default to `current`, so this affects most automations created from chat.

Tracking: #178811

### Steps to reproduce

1. #16511 added `current`. At creation it resolved to `session:<creating session key>`, so runs executed inside that conversation.
2. #98755 detached all session-targeted runs. #98947 reverted that the next day, with the message "Cron jobs run in the session they were created from unless the job explicitly requests an isolated fresh session."
3. #98236 (SQLite session storage) reintroduced `isDetachedCronSessionTarget` for `isolated` and `current`. It also changed `resolveCronCurrentSessionTarget` to store the literal `current` ([`src/cron/session-target.ts:33-48`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/27e327f0bb58f45b4b6841ddab49cc3c6e8ba962/src/cron/session-target.ts#L33-L48)). The commit message does not mention the behavior change, and the author has confirmed it was unintended.
4. Create an agent-turn automation from a chat without `--session`. It is stored with `sessionTarget: "current"` and runs under `cron:<jobId>`.

### Expected behavior

A `current` job runs with the creating conversation's context and authority, as it did after #98947.

### Actual behavior

A `current` job runs detached, as documented in `docs/automation/cron-jobs/payloads.md` ("Detached; commits to the creation-bound conversation"). It receives the run session's resources: its own empty dashboard, a memory scope that is not the owner's, and no parent conversation to `wake`. Its own workspace and worktree context is not inherited either. Several delivery fixes since then route results back to the conversation while execution stays detached: #126860, #133323, #167363 and #168996. #171071 is another symptom of the detached run.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.5 (`27e327f`); since #98236 (2026-07-11)

### Operating system

Linux (not specific to an OS)

### Install method

Source checkout

### Model

Any

### Provider / routing chain

N/A

### Additional provider/model setup details

N/A

### Logs

N/A

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Commit history above. The 30-day failure evidence is in #178811.

### Impact and severity

- **Affected:** automations created from chat without an explicit `--session`.
- **Severity:** jobs miss resources the conversation had.
- **Frequency:** every run.

### Additional information

**Resolution choice.** Either restore in-conversation execution for `current`, or define `current` as the child execution context in #178812. Both change the behavior of existing `current` jobs. Fold the change into the comparison-mode and Doctor reporting described in #178812, so the change is visible per job.

issue.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The same scheduled agent-turn job receives a different set of owner-only tools depending on whether it runs on the embedded runtime or a CLI backend. Cron does not set `senderIsOwner`. The embedded path passes it through as `undefined`, and the CLI loopback converts it to `false`. Tool gates treat those two values differently.

Tracking: #178811

### Steps to reproduce

Found by reading the code at `27e327f`. This has not been reproduced on a live gateway.

1. In https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/02182d5a303 ("refactor: remove sender owner tool gating"), cron stopped setting `senderIsOwner`. No production code under `src/cron` sets it.
2. **Embedded runs.** `runEmbeddedAgent` is called without `senderIsOwner` ([`src/cron/isolated-agent/run-prompt-executor.ts:629-690`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/27e327f0bb58f45b4b6841ddab49cc3c6e8ba962/src/cron/isolated-agent/run-prompt-executor.ts#L629-L690)). The owner-only deny path in [`src/agents/tools/session-portal-target.ts:18-56`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/27e327f0bb58f45b4b6841ddab49cc3c6e8ba962/src/agents/tools/session-portal-target.ts#L18-L56) with [`src/security/dangerous-tools.ts:77-82`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/27e327f0bb58f45b4b6841ddab49cc3c6e8ba962/src/security/dangerous-tools.ts#L77-L82) denies only `intent` when the value is `undefined`.
3. **CLI-backend runs.** [`src/agents/cli-runner/mcp-grant-context.ts:268`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/27e327f0bb58f45b4b6841ddab49cc3c6e8ba962/src/agents/cli-runner/mcp-grant-context.ts#L268) sets `senderIsOwner: params.run.senderIsOwner === true`, which is `false`. [`src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts:252-285`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/27e327f0bb58f45b4b6841ddab49cc3c6e8ba962/src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts#L252-L285) then denies the owner-only gateway tools and `sessions`, and scopes `portal` to the worker.
4. Create an agent-turn automation with `--tools "*"` that calls `sessions` or `gateway`. Run it once with an embedded model and once with a CLI-backed model.

### Expected behavior

One job receives one tool surface regardless of runtime. The surface comes from the job's stored authority.

### Actual behavior

Embedded runs keep `sessions`, `portal`, `nodes`, `conversations_*`, `gateway` and `plugins`, subject to `toolsAllow`. CLI-backend runs lose them. Other gates also disagree on `undefined`:

issue.body:
### Summary

Replace the scattered decisions about what a scheduled run may do with one execution context, minted per occurrence at admission and read by every layer. The context identifies the run as a child of the conversation that created the job.

Tracking: #178811

### Problem to solve

A read of `main` at `27e327f` found 49 places that decide a scheduled run's authority or the resources it acts on (full table below):

| Decision | Places |
|---|---|
| Which tools exist | 9 |
| Which actions a tool allows | 14 |
| Which resource or scope a tool acts on (memory, dashboard, workspace, sandbox, delivery) | 24 |
| Owner or operator status | 15 |
| Inference account | 4 |

A place can fall into more than one category. They identify a scheduled run with six independent signals:

1. Session-key shape. Three predicates: `isCronSessionKey`, `isCronRunSessionKey`, and raw `startsWith("cron:")`.
2. `trigger === "cron"`.
3. The tri-state `senderIsOwner`.
4. Presence of a scheduled tool policy.
5. Admission source: `operator-schedule` or `requester-schedule`.
6. Capabilities minted per run.

Because the signals disagree, the same job behaves differently by path:

- **Embedded and CLI runtimes expose different tools** for the same job. Filed as #178813.
- **`session:<key>` jobs keep a non-cron session key.** They skip every check based on key shape even though their trigger is `cron`.
- **Event-triggered jobs map to `trigger: "event"`** ([`src/cron/isolated-agent/run-prompt-executor.ts:97`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/27e327f0bb58f45b4b6841ddab49cc3c6e8ba962/src/cron/isolated-agent/run-prompt-executor.ts#L97)). They appear to skip the `trigger === "cron"` checks, including the self-scoped `automations` restriction ([`src/agents/agent-tools.ts:115-116`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/27e327f0bb58f45b4b6841ddab49cc3c6e8ba962/src/agents/agent-tools.ts#L115-L116)). This comes from reading the code and has not been reproduced.
- **The pinned-widget branch for scheduled turns cannot fire.** [`src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts:416-422`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/27e327f0bb58f45b4b6841ddab49cc3c6e8ba962/src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts#L416-L422) requires a non-cron-run session key, and `isolated` and `current` runs always have one.
- **Operator status is decided two ways:** by admission source in `gateway-tool.ts` and `presence-tool-authority.ts`, and by scheduled-policy presence in `openclaw-tools.transcripts.ts`.
- **The CLI loopback path appears to drop scheduled context.** [`src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts:425-433`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/27e327f0bb58f45b4b6841ddab49cc3c6e8ba962/src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts#L425-L433) passes no `gatewayCallerScheduled` and no self-management job id.

Two places already use the target pattern, because they gate on a capability bound to the run: `message-tool-turn-authority.ts` and `message-action-dispatch.ts`.

### Proposed solution

**Execution context.** Mint one object per occurrence in cron run admission, with these fields:

- `principal`: a child of the creating conversation's exact incarnation (`sessionKey`, `sessionId`, `lifecycleRevision`). Jobs already record this as `sourceConversation` ([`src/cron/types.ts:423-427`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/27e327f0bb58f45b4b6841ddab49cc3c6e8ba962/src/cron/types.ts#L423-L427)), which is used only for delivery.
- `ownerAuthority`: revalidated on each occurrence against the parent conversation and current policy. This follows the `session:<key>` operator continuation in [`src/gateway/cron-operator-source.ts:12-67`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/27e327f0bb58f45b4b6841ddab49cc3c6e8ba962/src/gateway/cron-operator-source.ts#L12-L67), which checks the exact source incarnation and the operator's scopes on every occurrence.
- `toolPolicy`: the result of `resolveCronRunToolsAllow` and the scheduled tool policy.
- `resourceScopes`:
  - memory audience (the parent's partition);
  - dashboard board (the parent's);
  - workspace and cwd;
  - sandbox;
  - exec host;
  - message accounts;
  - delivery route.
- `inferenceAccount`: the stored `inferenceBinding` and runtime authority, with one refusal path.

**Consumers.** Each of the 49 places reads the object. None infers authority from session-key shape, `trigger` or `senderIsOwner`. The CLI loopback carries the whole object.

**Parent lifecycle.** When the parent conversation is reset, archived or removed, a recurring job pauses with a notice naming the parent. It does not fall back to a different authority.

**Compatibility.** Existing automations keep working:

- **No stored-data migration.** The context is derived from fields jobs already store. On the maintainer gateway, 89 stored jobs break down as follows:
  - 46 are `session:<key>` agent turns, whose parent is the target.
  - 13 are `current` agent turns, with a parent in `owner.sessionKey` or `sessionKey`. Only 1 has `sourceConversation`.
  - 25 are `isolated` agent turns. 18 have no parent link, because they were created by the CLI or an operator, or predate the field.
- **Jobs without a parent link** keep the operator-created behavior they have today.
- **Comparison mode first.** One release computes the context alongside the existing decisions and logs every divergence per job. The switch happens after each divergence class is explained.
- **No silent reduction in access.** Doctor lists any job whose effective access shrinks, with the reason. Expanded access (the parent's memory partition, the parent's dashboard, `wake` back to the parent) is the intended change and is recorded in the release notes.

### Alternatives considered

- **Stamp subagent lineage (`spawnedBy`, `spawnedBySenderIsOwner`) on cron run sessions.**
  - Session visibility (`tree`), group policy and cron creator admission match lineage by session key, so a recreated parent with the same key would gain the job.
  - The owner bit is frozen at spawn, which conflicts with revalidating authority on each occurrence.
  - Subagents freeze a tool-policy snapshot, while `*` cron jobs re-resolve the owner policy on each run.
- **Fix each failing layer separately.** This keeps six signals in place. Each new tool or resource scope would need its own scheduled-run rule.

### Impact

Fixes the largest class of automation failures: missing tools, actions or resources in the scheduled run. It also gives a single object to inspect when a job fails, and a single place to validate at creation time (roadmap in #178811).

### Evidence/examples

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Every row in the inventory below reads the execution context, or is removed.
- [ ] No production code outside admission derives scheduled authority from `isCronSessionKey`, `isCronRunSessionKey`, `startsWith("cron:")`, `trigger === "cron"` or `senderIsOwner`.
- [ ] CLI and embedded runtimes receive the same tool surface for the same job (#178813).
- [ ] Event-triggered jobs receive the same self-scoped `automations` restriction as timer jobs (verify first).
- [ ] Regression tests cover:
  - `show_widget` and the parent's dashboard;
  - the parent's memory partition;
  - `wake` to the parent;
  - an archived parent pausing the job with a notice;
  - an inference-account mismatch reported once.
- [ ] A comparison-mode release with a per-job divergence log precedes the switch.
- [ ] Doctor reports jobs with reduced access.

issue.body:
### Summary

Replace the scattered decisions about what a scheduled run may do with one execution context, minted per occurrence at admission and read by every layer. The context identifies the run as a child of the conversation that created the job.

Tracking: #178811

### Problem to solve

A read of `main` at `27e327f` found 49 places that decide a scheduled run's authority or the resources it acts on (full table below):

| Decision | Places |
|---|---|
| Which tools exist | 9 |
| Which actions a tool allows | 14 |
| Which resource or scope a tool acts on (memory, dashboard, workspace, sandbox, delivery) | 24 |
| Owner or operator status | 15 |
| Inference account | 4 |

A place can fall into more than one category. They identify a scheduled run with six independent signals:

1. Session-key shape. Three predicates: `isCronSessionKey`, `isCronRunSessionKey`, and raw `startsWith("cron:")`.
2. `trigger === "cron"`.
3. The tri-state `senderIsOwner`.
4. Presence of a scheduled tool policy.
5. Admission source: `operator-schedule` or `requester-schedule`.
6. Capabilities minted per run.

Because the signals disagree, the same job behaves differently by path:

- **Embedded and CLI runtimes expose different tools** for the same job. Filed as #178813.
- **`session:<key>` jobs keep a non-cron session key.** They skip every check based on key shape even though their trigger is `cron`.
- **Event-triggered jobs map to `trigger: "event"`** ([`src/cron/isolated-agent/run-prompt-executor.ts:97`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/27e327f0bb58f45b4b6841ddab49cc3c6e8ba962/src/cron/isolated-agent/run-prompt-executor.ts#L97)). They appear to skip the `trigger === "cron"` checks, including the self-scoped `automations` restriction ([`src/agents/agent-tools.ts:115-116`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/27e327f0bb58f45b4b6841ddab49cc3c6e8ba962/src/agents/agent-tools.ts#L115-L116)). This comes from reading the code and has not been reproduced.
- **The pinned-widget branch for scheduled turns cannot fire.** [`src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts:416-422`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/27e327f0bb58f45b4b6841ddab49cc3c6e8ba962/src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts#L416-L422) requires a non-cron-run session key, and `isolated` and `current` runs always have one.
- **Operator status is decided two ways:** by admission source in `gateway-tool.ts` and `presence-tool-authority.ts`, and by scheduled-policy presence in `openclaw-tools.transcripts.ts`.
- **The CLI loopback path appears to drop scheduled context.** [`src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts:425-433`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/27e327f0bb58f45b4b6841ddab49cc3c6e8ba962/src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts#L425-L433) passes no `gatewayCallerScheduled` and no self-management job id.

Two places already use the target pattern, because they gate on a capability bound to the run: `message-tool-turn-authority.ts` and `message-action-dispatch.ts`.

### Proposed solution

**Execution context.** Mint one object per occurrence in cron run admission, with these fields:

- `principal`: a child of the creating conversation's exact incarnation (`sessionKey`, `sessionId`, `lifecycleRevision`). Jobs already record this as `sourceConversation` ([`src/cron/types.ts:423-427`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/27e327f0bb58f45b4b6841ddab49cc3c6e8ba962/src/cron/types.ts#L423-L427)), which is used only for delivery.
- `ownerAuthority`: revalidated on each occurrence against the parent conversation and current policy. This follows the `session:<key>` operator continuation in [`src/gateway/cron-operator-source.ts:12-67`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/27e327f0bb58f45b4b6841ddab49cc3c6e8ba962/src/gateway/cron-operator-source.ts#L12-L67), which checks the exact source incarnation and the operator's scopes on every occurrence.
- `toolPolicy`: the result of `resolveCronRunToolsAllow` and the scheduled tool policy.
- `resourceScopes`:
  - memory audience (the parent's partition);
  - dashboard board (the parent's);
  - workspace and cwd;
  - sandbox;
  - exec host;
  - message accounts;
  - delivery route.
- `inferenceAccount`: the stored `inferenceBinding` and runtime authority, with one refusal path.

**Consumers.** Each of the 49 places reads the object. None infers authority from session-key shape, `trigger` or `senderIsOwner`. The CLI loopback carries the whole object.

**Parent lifecycle.** When the parent conversation is reset, archived or removed, a recurring job pauses with a notice naming the parent. It does not fall back to a different authority.

**Compatibility.** Existing automations keep working:

- **No stored-data migration.** The context is derived from fields jobs already store. On the maintainer gateway, 89 stored jobs break down as follows:
  - 46 are `session:<key>` agent turns, whose parent is the target.
  - 13 are `current` agent turns, with a parent in `owner.sessionKey` or `sessionKey`. Only 1 has `sourceConversation`.
  - 25 are `isolated` agent turns. 18 have no parent link, because they were created by the CLI or an operator, or predate the field.
- **Jobs without a parent link** keep the operator-created behavior they have today.
- **Comparison mode first.** One release computes the context alongside the existing decisions and logs every divergence per job. The switch happens after each divergence class is explained.
- **No silent reduction in access.** Doctor lists any job whose effective access shrinks, with the reason. Expanded access (the parent's memory partition, the parent's dashboard, `wake` back to the parent) is the intended change and is recorded in the release notes.

### Alternatives considered

- **Stamp subagent lineage (`spawnedBy`, `spawnedBySenderIsOwner`) on cron run sessions.**
  - Session visibility (`tree`), group policy and cron creator admission match lineage by session key, so a recreated parent with the same key would gain the job.
  - The owner bit is frozen at spawn, which conflicts with revalidating authority on each occurrence.
  - Subagents freeze a tool-policy snapshot, while `*` cron jobs re-resolve the owner policy on each run.
- **Fix each failing layer separately.** This keeps six signals in place. Each new tool or resource scope would need its own scheduled-run rule.

### Impact

Fixes the largest class of automation failures: missing tools, actions or resources in the scheduled run. It also gives a single object to inspect when a job fails, and a single place to validate at creation time (roadmap in #178811).

### Evidence/examples

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Every row in the inventory below reads the execution context, or is removed.
- [ ] No production code outside admission derives scheduled authority from `isCronSessionKey`, `isCronRunSessionKey`, `startsWith("cron:")`, `trigger === "cron"` or `senderIsOwner`.
- [ ] CLI and embedded runtimes receive the same tool surface for the same job (#178813).
- [ ] Event-triggered jobs receive the same self-scoped `automations` restriction as timer jobs (verify first).
- [ ] Regression tests cover:
  - `show_widget` and the parent's dashboard;
  - the parent's memory partition;
  - `wake` to the parent;
  - an archived parent pausing the job with a notice;
  - an inference-account mismatch reported once.
- [ ] A comparison-mode release with a per-job divergence log precedes the switch.
- [ ] Doctor reports jobs with reduced access.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent can't publish its checkout with `github_publish` after it has stopped or finished a background command without polling that command.

## User Impact

User impact: once a background command has exited, a local `github_publish` with `workspacePath` goes ahead. Before this fix, a command the agent stopped with `process kill`, or one that finished and was reported back automatically, still blocked publishing. It blocked for up to 30 minutes, until finished-process retention dropped it. The error never said which work was the problem, so agents ended up opening PRs with `gh` instead. Work that is really still running is still refused, and the refusal now names it, for example `background exec <id> is still running; poll or kill it`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before PR publication adopts a local checkout, a busy check makes sure nothing is still running in the conversation. Its own comment says that only competing execution should block. But it also counted any exited background process whose result had never come back through `process poll` or `process log`. Neither `process kill` nor an automatic completion wake marks a result as polled, so those finished processes counted as busy. This change blocks only on exec that is still running or still finishing cleanup; unread output stays available through `process log`. The refusal now names the first thing that blocks: an exec id, a child session, a terminal, or another active run.

The clause came from #178756 (sandboxed `prepare_pr` adoption). #184531 then routed local `workspacePath` publication through the same adoption, and that is when it started to affect ordinary local publishing.

## Evidence

- **Production incident (2026-11-09, production Gateway on 2026.11.1 `d4d6fe7`):** a session's two publish attempts were refused. The first, at 14:15 UTC, was correct: E2E Gateways and tests really were running. The second, at 14:31 UTC, came when its only remaining processes were four it had stopped with `process kill` and never polled. The session then opened its PRs with `gh`. Across the last two weeks there were 14 such refusals in 8 sessions. Several came when only killed or finished, unpolled processes remained.
- **Isolated Gateway** (own state dir and port, `env -i`; the publish target was a scratch repo whose `origin` is a local bare repo, so nothing could reach GitHub):
  - On `d4d6fe7`, run in background, kill, no poll, publish: refused with `UNAVAILABLE`.
  - Same steps plus one `process poll`: goes ahead to the credential step.
  - A background command that exits on its own, with its completion delivered automatically, and a publish in a later turn: refused.
  - With this fix, the kill-without-poll case and the exits-on-its-own case both go ahead to the credential step. The isolated Gateway has no GitHub identity, so the credential failure is expected. A `sleep 900` that is still running is refused with `background exec tender-ember:… is still running; poll or kill it`.
- **Regression test** in `session-pr-workspace-adoption.test.ts`: the fixture now kills the running process without polling it and expects adoption to continue.
  - Red on base: with only the old clause restored, the run is refused as busy.
  - Green with the fix: `pnpm test src/gateway/session-pr-workspace-adoption.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` gives 4/4 passing.
- **Gates:** `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `pnpm build` and `check:test-lines-ratchet` all pass. The ratchet uses a justified 5-line allocation for the new assertions.
- **Not changed:** `sessions_yield` in subagents (`openclaw-tools.requester-yield.ts`) has its own similar "uncollected result" check. It is left as is and noted as a follow-up.

issue.body:
Related: #193993, #193982

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a saved OpenClaw ID node keeps dialing the Gateway server key it learned at enrollment, so it cannot reconnect after the Gateway honestly rotates that key.

## User Impact

User impact: nodes refresh and verify the claw's current signed server authority and membership before every connection, follow an honest server-key rotation without rejoining, close a connection whose server key was replaced, and keep learned trust across restarts and refused rejoins. A node whose access was removed stops with a rejoin instruction, and the reason for any other refusal is printed once instead of a bare connection failure.

- A preview target saved without a Discovery origin no longer breaks `openclaw node` config loading. It still never connects: the owner removes the node on the Access page, then it rejoins with a new link and `--discovery-url`, keeping its verified trust.
- Reconnects now fail closed when Discovery is unreachable or serves stale evidence. A Discovery outage therefore interrupts node connections until it recovers. This is an intended tradeoff.
- Pairing assumes the invitation stays secret. The six-digit comparison does not protect against a stolen invitation combined with control of pairing delivery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Enrollment and reconnect share one node-signed Discovery client and descriptor verifier. Before each dial and periodic probe, the node verifies the binding, snapshot freshness and its own membership. The canonical SQLite writer saves the strongest binding, the membership order and the binding-retirement facts before any dial, without touching unrelated node settings. If that save fails, the node stops.

Rebased onto `main` after #193993. Its pre-mail re-enroll refusal, recovery-hint messages, `loadNodeTunnelKey` export and supervised foreground join are kept. Maintainer follow-up commits on top of Josh Avant's commit:

- Signed trust from a Discovery response is saved even when the response's unsigned relay URL is invalid; that response is still never dialed. Before this fix, a later attempt could accept older evidence that was still fresh.
- Preview targets without `discoveryUrl` load for an explicit-origin rejoin, but the runner refuses to dial them.
- Refusal reasons reach the node operator: once per distinct reason, built locally, with no Discovery response text.
- When Discovery refuses to serve a node's descriptor (403), for example after a removed node restarts, the host prints re-join guidance and keeps retrying without dialing. The refusal is unsigned, so it does not stop the host the way verified removal does.

## Evidence

- Regression tests, each red on the pre-fix code and green with the fix:
  - invalid relay URLs (`ftp:`, embedded credentials) keep binding 2 and snapshot 3, then refuse the older binding-1 evidence;
  - a preview SQLite row without `discoveryUrl` loads, refuses to dial, keeps stronger trust on a refused rejoin, and adopts the explicit origin on an admitted rejoin;
  - a refusal is reported once across repeated bridged requests;
  - an unsigned Discovery 403 prints re-join guidance and neither stops the host nor dials.
- Focused suites pass on the final head: enrollment, join, connection, transport, target, SQLite config, runner and protocol freshness (107 tests).
- The native node-host Gateway suite passes 6 of 7 with the real Linux iroh addon. The remaining case, `both streaming transfer routes use the same private bridge` (ECONNRESET), fails the same way on unmodified `origin/main` on the same host.
- Other checks: `pnpm tsgo:core`, changed-file oxlint and format, `git diff --check`, the mock-export ratchet and knip pass. The test-line ratchet against `origin/main` passes with an exact allocation (+776, slack 0). `deadcode:exports` reports only untouched exports in `src/daemon/launchd.ts` and `ui/.../dashboard-tools.tsx`, so that failure comes from `main`.
- An independent review found no P0 or P1 issues. Two findings were verified and fixed: refusal diagnostics (P2) and the preview-target recovery path, which conflicted with the re-enroll refusal (P3).
- At `92bbf99`, CI failed only `checks-node-changed-12`. Two `update-command-resume-completion.test.ts` cases failed because their Doctor fixture timed out (exit 124) under Bun. This PR does not touch that file, and it passes locally (11 of 11). At head `7863d1d`, all CI checks pass, including `checks-node-changed-12`, `Scan changed paths (precise)`, `check-lint-core-2` and `openclaw/ci-gate`.
- ClawSweeper's input scanner (TruffleHog `URI` detector) refused two synthetic `https://user:…@` test fixtures: one added here and one already on `main` in `openclaw-id-target.test.ts`. Both fixtures now build their userinfo at runtime. A local TruffleHog scan of all changed files at `58ac569` reports 0 findings. That head changes only those two tests and the line allocation.

### Live proof

The proof ran 7 of 7 steps green on build `92bbf99`, against staging OpenClaw ID and Discovery with a throwaway claw.

- **Gateway:** an isolated Gateway on the Mac Studio, with its own profile, state directory and port.
- **Owner:** real Chromium.
- **Node:** this PR's CLI on Linux, with `env -i` and isolated profiles.
- **Discovery:** the node reached staging Discovery through a local untrusted proxy. In pass mode the proxy forwards node-signed requests unchanged. It can also corrupt the unsigned `relay_url` or replay an earlier captured response.

| Step | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Join | Owner and node codes matched; the node connected over the tunnel with binding 1. |
| Honest rotation 1→2 while the node runs | The Gateway restarted on a new key (`iroh:3abd…` → `iroh:c952…`). The same node ID reconnected in about 7 s without rejoining. `system.which` ran over the new connection. The saved target is binding 2 with the new key, snapshot seq 3. |
| Restarted node, replayed binding 1 (still fresh) | Refused once: `Possible claw substitution: rollback`. No connection while the replay was served. The node connected once current evidence returned, without a restart. |
| (a) Rotation 2→3 served with relay `ftp://…` | Refused: `Discovery returned an invalid relay URL…`, and nothing was dialed. The saved target advanced to binding 3 with the new key and kept the previous relay. A replay of binding 2 was then refused (`rollback`), and the node connected on current evidence. |
| (b) Preview target without `discoveryUrl` | `node run` exits with the owner-removal and re-join guidance and makes no Discovery request. `node join --discovery-url` loads the profile, the owner approves, and the node connects. The saved target has the explicit origin and binding 3. |
| Verified removal | The owner removed the running node on Access. The host stopped with `OpenClaw ID node access was removed or is not admitted; re-join this node`. A restarted node never connected. |

Gaps:

- **No production rotation path.** `main` has no Gateway command that rotates the server key. Proof-only plumbing stopped the isolated Gateway, generated a new endpoint key, and signed `ServerBinding(seq+1)` for it with the claw root from the throwaway recovery kit. The unmodified Gateway then republished on start.
- **Retiring a still-live old connection was not shown live.** The old key went away with the restart, so this proof cannot separate retiring a still-live old connection from losing it. The transport tests cover that retirement.
- **The removed-restart guidance was fixed after this run.** On `92bbf99` the restarted node retried silently on Discovery's 403. On `7863d1d`, a rerun against the same removed node prints `Discovery does not list this node for the claw; retrying. If the owner removed this node, re-join it with a new link.` and does not dial.

Cleanup: the throwaway claw was retired from staging Discovery. The isolated Gateway was stopped, and its profile was backed up and removed. The local node profiles, proxy and secrets were removed, and the staging lock was released.

Landing note (maintainer): ClawSweeper could not review this PR, and that was not caused by anything in this PR's final code.
