issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a `sessions_send` or other `dispatch_action` call reports `SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite` even though it already ran. This happens when a child-coordination turn makes the call in the same tool batch as `message(action=send)`.

## User Impact

User impact: in these turns, `dispatch_action` calls now return their real result. The agent no longer sees a false failure for a message that was already delivered, so it stops retrying, which used to deliver the same message twice.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a deferred tool called through `dispatch_action` finishes, the run records a nested tool activity row (#154068). A nested send can advance the transcript before that row is written. #163264 let such a row rebase onto newer same-turn rows, but only when `readNestedToolActivity` recognizes it, and that check requires `display: true`.

In a child coordination turn (#150625), the transcript-visibility projection writes every row of the run with `display: false`. The nested activity row is then not recognized. The append runs against the session manager's stale mutation fence with no retry. A parallel `message(action=send)` reply that commits first causes the conflict. The executor then reports the persistence failure as the tool's result, even though the tool's effect has already happened.

`readOwnNestedToolActivity` validates the same schema but ignores a cleared display flag. Two places now use it:

- turn validation in `session-manager-append.ts`, for both the sync and worker paths. The database rebase check stays authoritative.
- `readAttemptNestedToolActivity`, which would otherwise throw `Accepted nested tool activity is no longer valid` for the run's own hidden activity.
- `isInterruptedTurnEntry` in interrupted-turn replay. Otherwise the run's own hidden activity would end the replay walk, and the turn would count as already delivered.

Display readers keep the strict reader, so hidden activity stays hidden.

## Evidence

- Regression test in `src/agents/sessions/session-manager.test.ts` covers a hidden (`display: false`) nested activity that is appended after a same-turn source reply committed out of band, through both `appendMessage` and `appendMessageAsync`. It fails on `origin/main` with the production error and passes with the fix.
- Regression test in `attempt-tool-search-executor.commit.test.ts` reads back nested activity from a hidden run. It fails without the fix (`Accepted nested tool activity is no longer valid`) and passes with it.
- Focused suites pass: session-manager, attempt-tool-search-executor and commit, session-boundary preparation, session replay, and transcript-lifecycle prepare (133 tests).
- Real Gateway end to end: isolated Gateways (`env -i`, own state dir and port) with a real model. A parent spawns a visible child, and the child reports with `sessions_send`. The parent's private turn calls `message(action=send)` and `dispatch_action(sessions_send)` in one batch.
  - On 2026.11.1 (`d4d6fe7`), 4 of 4 rounds failed with the conflict. On `origin/main` (`d88a384`), the run failed the same way. A debug stack showed the throw at the `expectedMutationAt` check in `runTranscriptWriteSnapshotSync`, reached through `applySessionMetadataAppendInTransaction` from the session actor. In every round the child still received the message, and the model's retry delivered it a second time.
  - With this fix, 2 of 2 rounds stored the activity after the source reply and `dispatch_action` returned `accepted`.
- Production: on 2026-11-08, three `dispatch_action(sessions_send)` calls in the affected session failed this way. The target session's transcript shows each message was delivered.
- Gates: `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` and `tsgo:core:test` pass on this branch. The three regressions add 55 test lines, covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/196034-hidden-nested-activity-rebase.txt` because the fix needs this regression proof. An independent review asked for the replay reader fix and the readback test above; both are included.

Related: a separate draft PR fixes the Control UI hiding the message-tool reply in these same turns.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent can't publish its checkout with `github_publish` after it has stopped or finished a background command without polling that command.

## User Impact

User impact: once a background command has exited, a local `github_publish` with `workspacePath` goes ahead. Before this fix, a command the agent stopped with `process kill`, or one that finished and was reported back automatically, still blocked publishing. It blocked for up to 30 minutes, until finished-process retention dropped it. The error never said which work was the problem, so agents ended up opening PRs with `gh` instead. Work that is really still running is still refused, and the refusal now names it, for example `background exec <id> is still running; poll or kill it`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before PR publication adopts a local checkout, a busy check makes sure nothing is still running in the conversation. Its own comment says that only competing execution should block. But it also counted any exited background process whose result had never come back through `process poll` or `process log`. Neither `process kill` nor an automatic completion wake marks a result as polled, so those finished processes counted as busy. This change blocks only on exec that is still running or still finishing cleanup; unread output stays available through `process log`. The refusal now names the first thing that blocks: an exec id, a child session, a terminal, or another active run.

The clause came from #178756 (sandboxed `prepare_pr` adoption). #184531 then routed local `workspacePath` publication through the same adoption, and that is when it started to affect ordinary local publishing.

## Evidence

- **Production incident (2026-11-09, production Gateway on 2026.11.1 `d4d6fe7`):** a session's two publish attempts were refused. The first, at 14:15 UTC, was correct: E2E Gateways and tests really were running. The second, at 14:31 UTC, came when its only remaining processes were four it had stopped with `process kill` and never polled. The session then opened its PRs with `gh`. Across the last two weeks there were 14 such refusals in 8 sessions. Several came when only killed or finished, unpolled processes remained.
- **Isolated Gateway** (own state dir and port, `env -i`; the publish target was a scratch repo whose `origin` is a local bare repo, so nothing could reach GitHub):
  - On `d4d6fe7`, run in background, kill, no poll, publish: refused with `UNAVAILABLE`.
  - Same steps plus one `process poll`: goes ahead to the credential step.
  - A background command that exits on its own, with its completion delivered automatically, and a publish in a later turn: refused.
  - With this fix, the kill-without-poll case and the exits-on-its-own case both go ahead to the credential step. The isolated Gateway has no GitHub identity, so the credential failure is expected. A `sleep 900` that is still running is refused with `background exec tender-ember:… is still running; poll or kill it`.
- **Regression test** in `session-pr-workspace-adoption.test.ts`: the fixture now kills the running process without polling it and expects adoption to continue.
  - Red on base: with only the old clause restored, the run is refused as busy.
  - Green with the fix: `pnpm test src/gateway/session-pr-workspace-adoption.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` gives 4/4 passing.
- **Gates:** `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `pnpm build` and `check:test-lines-ratchet` all pass. The ratchet uses a justified 5-line allocation for the new assertions.
- **Not changed:** `sessions_yield` in subagents (`openclaw-tools.requester-yield.ts`) has its own similar "uncollected result" check. It is left as is and noted as a follow-up.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: GPT models routed through ClawRouter's OpenAI Responses route fill every optional tool argument with placeholder values, which makes strict tools such as `github_publish` reject every call.

## User Impact

User impact: optional tool inputs stay optional for ClawRouter's OpenAI models (`openai/*` over OpenAI Responses), whether the model comes from the live catalog or from `models.providers.clawrouter.models` in config. Before this fix, GPT-6 Astra, Luna and Sol sent every property of every tool. `process` got empty strings and arrays. `github_publish` got values like `title: "x"`, zero SHAs and zero UUIDs, and it rejected all 130 such calls on one production Gateway over two weeks with an unrelated `workspacePath` error.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenAI Responses treats a function tool with no `strict` key as strict, so it requires every property. #192764 meant to send an explicit `strict=false` by putting `compat.supportsStrictMode` on ClawRouter's catalog rows. On a real Gateway that compat never reaches the transport, for configured rows or for catalog-only rows, so no tool carried `strict`. #192764's test called `streamSimple` directly with the catalog row, so it skipped both model resolution and the plugin's stream wrapper.

This change moves the route fact to the request boundary ClawRouter already owns. `prepareClawRouterRequestModel` runs for every request through the plugin's stream wrapper, so `openai/*` OpenAI Responses requests now get `supportsStrictMode` no matter how the model was resolved. An explicit operator `compat.supportsStrictMode` still wins. The catalog-row copy is removed, so only one place owns this decision.

## Evidence

- **Wire capture on an isolated Gateway (live build `d4d6fe7`, which already includes #192764):** a logging reverse proxy in front of ClawRouter recorded only tool names, the `strict` flag and required-field counts.
  - A configured `openai/gpt-6-astra` row and a catalog-only `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` both had 0/17 tools carrying `strict`.
  - Astra, asked for `github_publish` `readiness`, sent all 12 fields with placeholders and was rejected.
  - With the proxy injecting `strict:false` and nothing else changed, the same turn sent `{"action":"readiness"}` and succeeded.
- **Same isolated Gateway on this branch (fresh state dir, same proxy):** both the configured `openai/gpt-6-astra` row and the catalog-only `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` sent `strict: false` on 16 of 17 tools. The 17th is the hosted `web_search` tool, which is not a function tool. Both models called `github_publish` with just `{"action":"readiness"}`, and the call succeeded.
- **Production transcripts (one production Gateway, last two weeks):** every GPT `process` call (thousands) and every direct `github_publish` call (133) from `openai-responses` models had all fields filled, before and after #192764 was deployed. Anthropic models never did this.
- **Regression test** in `extensions/clawrouter/index.test.ts`: the real plugin `wrapStreamFn` runs over the real `streamSimple`, for a configured row and a discovered row, and checks that the serialized request has `strict: false` with the optional property left optional.
  - Red on base: both cases are missing `strict`.
  - Green with the fix: `pnpm test` on the three ClawRouter test files gives 47/47 passing.
- **Gates:** `oxfmt`, `oxlint` (extensions), `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test` and `check:test-lines-ratchet` all pass. The ratchet uses a 10-line allocation; the bypassing 45-line test was removed.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an MCP server that uses OAuth (e.g. the Granola plugin) stops working until the user signs in again when a brief DNS or network outage happens during an access-token refresh.

## User Impact

User impact: a transient DNS or connection failure during an MCP token refresh no longer locks the server's sign-in. The server reports the failure, and the next start retries the refresh with the saved grant. Users no longer need to sign in again after a short network blip.

## Why This Change Was Made

The refresh boundary marked a refresh as dispatched right before the token request, so any transport error, including a DNS lookup failure that never left the host, was recorded as an uncertain outcome. That kept the durable refresh claim fenced, and every later attempt, including after Gateway restarts, failed with "MCP OAuth refresh outcome is uncertain; sign in again." without contacting the server.

The boundary now uses the existing pre-connect proof (`isProvenDeliveryNotSentError`: DNS/connect errno with `getaddrinfo`/`connect` syscalls, Undici connect/DNS errors, every transport leaf must prove it). On such a failure the refresh counts as not attempted, and the claim is restored. Any failure after a connection could have carried the grant (resets, timeouts mid-exchange, lost responses, error responses) stays fenced exactly as before.

Accepted edge: the guarded fetch follows same-origin redirects internally, so a token endpoint that answers 307/308 and whose replay hop then fails DNS/connect is treated as not attempted. A redirect is not a token response, and if a non-conforming server had consumed the grant anyway, the replay at worst ends in `invalid_grant` and the same sign-in the fence would require. Tracking per-hop evidence through the transport wasn't worth the added machinery.

## Evidence

- Incident (operator Gateway, 2026-11-06 04:46 PST): host-wide `EAI_AGAIN` for ~6 minutes; Granola's refresh POST to its auth host failed DNS and was logged as `MCP OAuth refresh outcome is uncertain; sign in again. | getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN …`. The server stayed unavailable for three days, across a Gateway restart, while Linear, which hit the same outage without a refresh in flight, recovered on its own.
- Regression test in `src/agents/mcp-oauth-refresh-boundary.test.ts` (real MCP SDK + durable SQLite store): DNS (`EAI_AGAIN`/`getaddrinfo`) and refused-connect (`ECONNREFUSED`/`connect`) failures now return `before-dispatch / not-attempted`, clear the claim, and the next refresh succeeds. Both cases fail on `main` (`outcome: unknown`) and pass with the fix. Existing fence cases (lost response, 503, nested rejection, invalid success, rejected fresh token) are unchanged and still pass.
- Test-line budget: +17 lines, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/mcp-oauth-refresh-preconnect.txt`. That is the minimum regression proof at the owning boundary; the predicate's errno/syscall matrix is already covered by the delivery-recovery tests. File cost: about 39s wall with `--maxWorkers=1`, of which the two new cases take about 1.8s each.
- Production transport proof (temporary test, not committed): `resolveMcpOAuthAccessToken` with the default guarded MCP fetch against an unresolvable `.invalid` token endpoint.
  - `main`: attempt 1 → `uncertain; sign in again` with a `DNSException ENOTFOUND getaddrinfo` cause, and the claim is left set; attempt 2 → `uncertain` without any network call.
  - This branch: both attempts → `before-dispatch / not-attempted` with the same cause; the claim is cleared after each attempt, and each attempt retries the network.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` on `mcp-oauth-refresh-boundary`, `mcp-oauth`, `mcp-oauth-redirect`, `mcp-oauth-refresh`, `mcp-oauth-refresh-issuer` tests: 45/45 passed (before the test trim; the trimmed file was re-run red on `main` and green on this branch). `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; oxlint and format clean on changed files.
- Review: independent local review (OpenClaw subagent, gpt-6-astra, high reasoning) of the committed change. One P2: the same-origin redirect edge above. It was accepted and documented in code, with no other findings: store consistency, credential invalidation, SDK fallback POSTs, and proxy paths were all checked.

issue.body:
Related: #193993, #193982

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a saved OpenClaw ID node keeps dialing the Gateway server key it learned at enrollment, so it cannot reconnect after the Gateway honestly rotates that key.

## User Impact

User impact: nodes refresh and verify the claw's current signed server authority and membership before every connection, follow an honest server-key rotation without rejoining, close a connection whose server key was replaced, and keep learned trust across restarts and refused rejoins. A node whose access was removed stops with a rejoin instruction, and the reason for any other refusal is printed once instead of a bare connection failure.

- A preview target saved without a Discovery origin no longer breaks `openclaw node` config loading. It still never connects: the owner removes the node on the Access page, then it rejoins with a new link and `--discovery-url`, keeping its verified trust.
- Reconnects now fail closed when Discovery is unreachable or serves stale evidence. A Discovery outage therefore interrupts node connections until it recovers. This is an intended tradeoff.
- Pairing assumes the invitation stays secret. The six-digit comparison does not protect against a stolen invitation combined with control of pairing delivery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Enrollment and reconnect share one node-signed Discovery client and descriptor verifier. Before each dial and periodic probe, the node verifies the binding, snapshot freshness and its own membership. The canonical SQLite writer saves the strongest binding, the membership order and the binding-retirement facts before any dial, without touching unrelated node settings. If that save fails, the node stops.

Rebased onto `main` after #193993. Its pre-mail re-enroll refusal, recovery-hint messages, `loadNodeTunnelKey` export and supervised foreground join are kept. Maintainer follow-up commits on top of Josh Avant's commit:

- Signed trust from a Discovery response is saved even when the response's unsigned relay URL is invalid; that response is still never dialed. Before this fix, a later attempt could accept older evidence that was still fresh.
- Preview targets without `discoveryUrl` load for an explicit-origin rejoin, but the runner refuses to dial them.
- Refusal reasons reach the node operator: once per distinct reason, built locally, with no Discovery response text.
- When Discovery refuses to serve a node's descriptor (403), for example after a removed node restarts, the host prints re-join guidance and keeps retrying without dialing. The refusal is unsigned, so it does not stop the host the way verified removal does.

## Evidence

- Regression tests, each red on the pre-fix code and green with the fix:
  - invalid relay URLs (`ftp:`, embedded credentials) keep binding 2 and snapshot 3, then refuse the older binding-1 evidence;
  - a preview SQLite row without `discoveryUrl` loads, refuses to dial, keeps stronger trust on a refused rejoin, and adopts the explicit origin on an admitted rejoin;
  - a refusal is reported once across repeated bridged requests;
  - an unsigned Discovery 403 prints re-join guidance and neither stops the host nor dials.
- Focused suites pass on the final head: enrollment, join, connection, transport, target, SQLite config, runner and protocol freshness (107 tests).
- The native node-host Gateway suite passes 6 of 7 with the real Linux iroh addon. The remaining case, `both streaming transfer routes use the same private bridge` (ECONNRESET), fails the same way on unmodified `origin/main` on the same host.
- Other checks: `pnpm tsgo:core`, changed-file oxlint and format, `git diff --check`, the mock-export ratchet and knip pass. The test-line ratchet against `origin/main` passes with an exact allocation (+776, slack 0). `deadcode:exports` reports only untouched exports in `src/daemon/launchd.ts` and `ui/.../dashboard-tools.tsx`, so that failure comes from `main`.
- An independent review found no P0 or P1 issues. Two findings were verified and fixed: refusal diagnostics (P2) and the preview-target recovery path, which conflicted with the re-enroll refusal (P3).
- At `92bbf99`, CI failed only `checks-node-changed-12`. Two `update-command-resume-completion.test.ts` cases failed because their Doctor fixture timed out (exit 124) under Bun. This PR does not touch that file, and it passes locally (11 of 11). At head `7863d1d`, all CI checks pass, including `checks-node-changed-12`, `Scan changed paths (precise)`, `check-lint-core-2` and `openclaw/ci-gate`.
- ClawSweeper's input scanner (TruffleHog `URI` detector) refused two synthetic `https://user:…@` test fixtures: one added here and one already on `main` in `openclaw-id-target.test.ts`. Both fixtures now build their userinfo at runtime. A local TruffleHog scan of all changed files at `58ac569` reports 0 findings. That head changes only those two tests and the line allocation.

### Live proof

The proof ran 7 of 7 steps green on build `92bbf99`, against staging OpenClaw ID and Discovery with a throwaway claw.

- **Gateway:** an isolated Gateway on the Mac Studio, with its own profile, state directory and port.
- **Owner:** real Chromium.
- **Node:** this PR's CLI on Linux, with `env -i` and isolated profiles.
- **Discovery:** the node reached staging Discovery through a local untrusted proxy. In pass mode the proxy forwards node-signed requests unchanged. It can also corrupt the unsigned `relay_url` or replay an earlier captured response.

| Step | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Join | Owner and node codes matched; the node connected over the tunnel with binding 1. |
| Honest rotation 1→2 while the node runs | The Gateway restarted on a new key (`iroh:3abd…` → `iroh:c952…`). The same node ID reconnected in about 7 s without rejoining. `system.which` ran over the new connection. The saved target is binding 2 with the new key, snapshot seq 3. |
| Restarted node, replayed binding 1 (still fresh) | Refused once: `Possible claw substitution: rollback`. No connection while the replay was served. The node connected once current evidence returned, without a restart. |
| (a) Rotation 2→3 served with relay `ftp://…` | Refused: `Discovery returned an invalid relay URL…`, and nothing was dialed. The saved target advanced to binding 3 with the new key and kept the previous relay. A replay of binding 2 was then refused (`rollback`), and the node connected on current evidence. |
| (b) Preview target without `discoveryUrl` | `node run` exits with the owner-removal and re-join guidance and makes no Discovery request. `node join --discovery-url` loads the profile, the owner approves, and the node connects. The saved target has the explicit origin and binding 3. |
| Verified removal | The owner removed the running node on Access. The host stopped with `OpenClaw ID node access was removed or is not admitted; re-join this node`. A restarted node never connected. |

Gaps:

- **No production rotation path.** `main` has no Gateway command that rotates the server key. Proof-only plumbing stopped the isolated Gateway, generated a new endpoint key, and signed `ServerBinding(seq+1)` for it with the claw root from the throwaway recovery kit. The unmodified Gateway then republished on start.
- **Retiring a still-live old connection was not shown live.** The old key went away with the restart, so this proof cannot separate retiring a still-live old connection from losing it. The transport tests cover that retirement.
- **The removed-restart guidance was fixed after this run.** On `92bbf99` the restarted node retried silently on Discovery's 403. On `7863d1d`, a rerun against the same removed node prints `Discovery does not list this node for the claw; retrying. If the owner removed this node, re-join it with a new link.` and does not dial.

Cleanup: the throwaway claw was retired from staging Discovery. The isolated Gateway was stopped, and its profile was backed up and removed. The local node profiles, proxy and secrets were removed, and the staging lock was released.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: GPT models routed through ClawRouter's OpenAI Responses route fill every optional tool argument with placeholder values, which makes strict tools such as `github_publish` reject every call.

## User Impact

User impact: optional tool inputs stay optional for ClawRouter's OpenAI models (`openai/*` over OpenAI Responses), whether the model comes from the live catalog or from `models.providers.clawrouter.models` in config. Before this fix, GPT-6 Astra, Luna and Sol sent every property of every tool. `process` got empty strings and arrays. `github_publish` got values like `title: "x"`, zero SHAs and zero UUIDs, and it rejected all 130 such calls on one production Gateway over two weeks with an unrelated `workspacePath` error.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenAI Responses treats a function tool with no `strict` key as strict, so it requires every property. #192764 meant to send an explicit `strict=false` by putting `compat.supportsStrictMode` on ClawRouter's catalog rows. On a real Gateway that compat never reaches the transport, for configured rows or for catalog-only rows, so no tool carried `strict`. #192764's test called `streamSimple` directly with the catalog row, so it skipped both model resolution and the plugin's stream wrapper.

This change moves the route fact to the request boundary ClawRouter already owns. `prepareClawRouterRequestModel` runs for every request through the plugin's stream wrapper, so `openai/*` OpenAI Responses requests now get `supportsStrictMode` no matter how the model was resolved. An explicit operator `compat.supportsStrictMode` still wins. The catalog-row copy is removed, so only one place owns this decision.

## Evidence

- **Wire capture on an isolated Gateway (live build `d4d6fe7`, which already includes #192764):** a logging reverse proxy in front of ClawRouter recorded only tool names, the `strict` flag and required-field counts.
  - A configured `openai/gpt-6-astra` row and a catalog-only `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` both had 0/17 tools carrying `strict`.
  - Astra, asked for `github_publish` `readiness`, sent all 12 fields with placeholders and was rejected.
  - With the proxy injecting `strict:false` and nothing else changed, the same turn sent `{"action":"readiness"}` and succeeded.
- **Same isolated Gateway on this branch (fresh state dir, same proxy):** both the configured `openai/gpt-6-astra` row and the catalog-only `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` sent `strict: false` on 16 of 17 tools. The 17th is the hosted `web_search` tool, which is not a function tool. Both models called `github_publish` with just `{"action":"readiness"}`, and the call succeeded.
- **Production transcripts (one production Gateway, last two weeks):** every GPT `process` call (thousands) and every direct `github_publish` call (133) from `openai-responses` models had all fields filled, before and after #192764 was deployed. Anthropic models never did this.
- **Regression test** in `extensions/clawrouter/index.test.ts`: the real plugin `wrapStreamFn` runs over the real `streamSimple`, for a configured row and a discovered row, and checks that the serialized request has `strict: false` with the optional property left optional.
  - Red on base: both cases are missing `strict`.
  - Green with the fix: `pnpm test` on the three ClawRouter test files gives 47/47 passing.
- **Gates:** `oxfmt`, `oxlint` (extensions), `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test` and `check:test-lines-ratchet` all pass. The ratchet uses a 10-line allocation; the bypassing 45-line test was removed.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agents misread `github_publish`. They conclude they can't land a PR, give up on a refused publish they believed had succeeded, or chase an unrelated `workspacePath` error.

## User Impact

User impact: `github_publish` now tells agents its limits and their next step. Only messages change; no behavior changes.
- **Landing scope:** `inspect`, `ready`, `merge` and `close` act only on the session's published or bound PR (including one bound with `prepare_pr`), or a delegated child's `publishingSessionKey`. Any other PR lands through the repository's native route (`scripts/pr` for OpenClaw). In one session, an agent concluded a PR "couldn't be merged" when the native route worked.
- **Publishing:** with `workspacePath`, `started` is not success. The result, which may be a refusal, resumes the session as the next turn. Running background commands, unfinished children, open terminals or another active run refuse preparation. A session publishes one checkout; use a separate session for another.
- **`readiness`:** says it doesn't check that busy condition. When the conversation has no bound checkout, the result adds a `next` line saying how to publish.
- **Errors:** a call that fills optional fields with placeholders now says to omit them, instead of "workspacePath is only available for local host publication". `readiness` and `inspect_pr` name the fields to remove.

## Why This Change Was Made

An investigation of two weeks of publisher failures on a production Gateway found these wordings behind repeated agent mistakes:
- 121 calls rejected with the misleading `workspacePath` error.
- 9 "different checkout" refusals with no warning in the description.
- Wrong-target `inspect`/`ready` calls.
- A refused publish reported only in the following turn.

The behavior fixes are separate: #196077 (stopped background commands blocking publish) and #196083 (ClawRouter GPT placeholder arguments).

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/agents/tools/github-publish-tool.test.ts src/agents/tools/github-publish-tool.handoff.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 30 + 8 passing. The two new behavioral tests fail on base and pass with the change; a description-only test was dropped at review.
- `prompt:snapshots:check` reports the snapshots are current, and `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` passes (14/14).
- `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test` and `check:test-lines-ratchet` all pass. The ratchet uses a 32-line allocation for the new tests.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a `sessions_send` or other `dispatch_action` call reports `SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite` even though it already ran. This happens when a child-coordination turn makes the call in the same tool batch as `message(action=send)`.

## User Impact

User impact: in these turns, `dispatch_action` calls now return their real result. The agent no longer sees a false failure for a message that was already delivered, so it stops retrying, which used to deliver the same message twice.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a deferred tool called through `dispatch_action` finishes, the run records a nested tool activity row (#154068). A nested send can advance the transcript before that row is written. #163264 let such a row rebase onto newer same-turn rows, but only when `readNestedToolActivity` recognizes it, and that check requires `display: true`.

In a child coordination turn (#150625), the transcript-visibility projection writes every row of the run with `display: false`. The nested activity row is then not recognized. The append runs against the session manager's stale mutation fence with no retry. A parallel `message(action=send)` reply that commits first causes the conflict. The executor then reports the persistence failure as the tool's result, even though the tool's effect has already happened.

`readOwnNestedToolActivity` validates the same schema but ignores a cleared display flag. Two places now use it:

- turn validation in `session-manager-append.ts`, for both the sync and worker paths. The database rebase check stays authoritative.
- `readAttemptNestedToolActivity`, which would otherwise throw `Accepted nested tool activity is no longer valid` for the run's own hidden activity.
- `isInterruptedTurnEntry` in interrupted-turn replay. Otherwise the run's own hidden activity would end the replay walk, and the turn would count as already delivered.

Display readers keep the strict reader, so hidden activity stays hidden.

## Evidence

- Regression test in `src/agents/sessions/session-manager.test.ts` covers a hidden (`display: false`) nested activity that is appended after a same-turn source reply committed out of band, through both `appendMessage` and `appendMessageAsync`. It fails on `origin/main` with the production error and passes with the fix.
- Regression test in `attempt-tool-search-executor.commit.test.ts` reads back nested activity from a hidden run. It fails without the fix (`Accepted nested tool activity is no longer valid`) and passes with it.
- Focused suites pass: session-manager, attempt-tool-search-executor and commit, session-boundary preparation, session replay, and transcript-lifecycle prepare (133 tests).
- Real Gateway end to end: isolated Gateways (`env -i`, own state dir and port) with a real model. A parent spawns a visible child, and the child reports with `sessions_send`. The parent's private turn calls `message(action=send)` and `dispatch_action(sessions_send)` in one batch.
  - On 2026.11.1 (`d4d6fe7`), 4 of 4 rounds failed with the conflict. On `origin/main` (`d88a384`), the run failed the same way. A debug stack showed the throw at the `expectedMutationAt` check in `runTranscriptWriteSnapshotSync`, reached through `applySessionMetadataAppendInTransaction` from the session actor. In every round the child still received the message, and the model's retry delivered it a second time.
  - With this fix, 2 of 2 rounds stored the activity after the source reply and `dispatch_action` returned `accepted`.
- Production: on 2026-11-08, three `dispatch_action(sessions_send)` calls in the affected session failed this way. The target session's transcript shows each message was delivered.
- Gates: `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` and `tsgo:core:test` pass on this branch. The three regressions add 55 test lines, covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/196034-hidden-nested-activity-rebase.txt` because the fix needs this regression proof. An independent review asked for the replay reader fix and the readback test above; both are included.

Related: a separate draft PR fixes the Control UI hiding the message-tool reply in these same turns.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native OpenClaw ID nodes need a Swift/Kotlin transport with QUIC keep-alive and exact numeric application close codes for `openclaw/tunnel/1`.

## User Impact

No user-visible change yet. No app consumes this crate until Android #194194 and Apple #194201 land; default app builds are unchanged. This PR adds the standalone transport foundation, not an app cutover or a release.

**Remaining platform and release gates:** iOS builds successfully but has not been runtime-proven on a device or simulator. Device transport, mobile lifecycle, and final APK/AAB packaging remain consumer-lane work. License notices for UniFFI, `attohttpc`, and MPL-covered dependencies must be completed before shipping the apps; they are a release gate, not a gate for merging this source-only crate.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OpenClaw-owned adapter pins iroh 1.4.1 (matching the Node addon) and UniFFI 0.31.2. It exposes endpoint bind/connect, bidirectional streams, typed close information preserving every legal 62-bit QUIC application code, home-relay status, and explicit cancellation/shutdown. The existing Node addon is unchanged. Apps retain enrollment, destination verification, framing, protected key storage, and lifecycle ownership.

The native input seed is zeroized on success and failure; this does not promise erasure of Swift/Kotlin or UniFFI marshalling copies. The Minimal preset uses only the supplied relay, with no default discovery service. Android must install its Application context before binding. Swift cancellation must use native `CancelToken`/stream stop-reset/shutdown; Kotlin callers shield native result delivery with `NonCancellable` and use the same explicit cancellation signals to avoid abandoning lowered results.

`libc` stays pinned to 0.2.189 until follow-up **openclaw-85d** removes the incompatible iOS dependency path. The pin is guarded in CI and documented in `PACKAGING.md`; the locked dependencies are audited on changes and weekly. No dependency upgrade or pin removal is part of this merge.

## Evidence

Final candidate: **`d5003c1e09b565fd3b23f4e8dcfd991ac8ea3254`**. Its only change after `f1adbdd` corrects the README's obsolete no-upload claim to describe the short-lived Apple CI artifact; all code, bindings, lockfiles, tests, and workflows are byte-identical. Final-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42638547053), [native Linux/Android/Apple builds](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42638546821), and [dependency audit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42638546987) passed. Required CI/security gates were verified green before native merge submission.

Completed proof at code-identical head **`f1adbdd671ceb0219961d52d568d00ba7c688274`**:

- [Native CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42623477334) passed Linux, Android, and Apple. Linux runs Rust tests/lint, checks generated bindings, and builds the release library. Android builds all four ABIs with ELF LOAD alignment >=16 KiB. Apple builds all five Rust targets into the macOS/iOS-device/iOS-simulator XCFramework and typechecks the generated Swift.
- [Dependency audit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42623477771) passed, including the libc pin check and RustSec audit.
- Local Rust 1.99 validation passed: `cargo test --locked` (1 unit + 5 real loopback integration tests), `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, formatting, the pin check, deterministic Swift/Kotlin regeneration, and all 21 generated Kotlin ABI checksums against the rebuilt host library. The tests cover exact 2^62−1 application close codes, streams/FIN, input bounds, seed erasure, watcher shutdown, blocked read/accept/connect shutdown, and per-operation dial/stream cancellation while retaining endpoint/connection usability.
- Linux release library: 13,189,976 bytes; SHA-256 `cbda14805e7c8f583c7760a84228b84f590c2c48780654934c60846c11d03bb3`.
- [Apple CI artifact](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42623477334/artifacts/13678113168) is a short-lived workflow artifact, not a published package or app release.

Consumer-lane evidence is distinct from crate CI:
- Apple #194201 [Swift CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42624699734) passed at Apple head `ee25eeaea9129b4999b59c4dc7e535be760858a1`, based on this crate head `f1adbdd`. It builds matching bindings/macOS XCFramework and passes the native Swift → Rust loopback (1/1) and shared tests (25/25). This is macOS proof, not iOS runtime proof.
- Android #194194 passed [default-build/no-iroh validation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42623709966) and [opt-in build/tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42623719554) at Android head `d5f9459788221dc623e9b9f9e0ee778236f2ca61`, based on this crate head `f1adbdd`.
- The Android lane's JVM → generated Kotlin/JNA → Rust loopback (framing, FIN, 62-bit close code, cancelled/pre-cancelled dial) used the retained `.so` built at crate `92c2506`, whose ABI sources and generated bindings are unchanged at `f1adbdd`. This is prior-build evidence, not a freshly rebuilt exact-head JVM run or Android device proof.

Independent read-only Astra landing review covered the complete 25-file diff from merge-base `d88a384060d6d0f55920fc0092877c58d128cc3e` to `f1adbdd671ceb0219961d52d568d00ba7c688274`, including dependency ownership/cancellation and platform packaging contracts. It found **no verified P0–P2 findings**. This was static review, not an independent runtime rerun. The subsequent README-only correction was inspected separately and passes `git diff --check`; it changes no code or runtime inputs. The [completed final-head ClawSweeper re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194174#issuecomment-6689848396) reports no actionable findings and confirms both prior findings resolved. issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: updates an agent sends with `message(action=send)` never appear in the Control UI when the turn was started by a report from one of its spawned child sessions.

## User Impact

User impact: when a spawned child reports back with `sessions_send`, the parent's `message(action=send)` update now shows in the Control UI, both live and after a reload. The child's report and the parent's private coordination text stay hidden, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

A report from a spawned child starts a "child coordination" turn (#150625). The chat history and live projection hide the child's input and every row that carries that run's id. The same turn is told that its final text is private and that a visible reply must use `message(action=send)`. That reply is stored as a delivery-mirror row with the same run id (#127879), so the projection hid the only output meant for the user. The tool result already says the reply was only recorded in the transcript (#164860), so the agent gets no sign that the user never saw it.

A delivery mirror is, by definition, content delivered to the user. The coordination projection now keeps delivery-mirror rows and still hides everything else in the run. All history, delta, worker and live (SSE) readers share that projection, so one change covers them.

## Evidence

- Regression test in `src/gateway/session-history.subagent-visibility.test.ts` covers a hidden child-coordination run with a message-tool reply, through the history page and through live inline append. It fails on `origin/main` (`expected [] to deeply equal ['user-update']`) and passes with the fix. The other 11 tests in that suite still pass.
- Real Gateway and Control UI end to end: isolated Gateways (`env -i`, own state dir and port) with a real model. A parent spawns a visible child, the child calls `sessions_send` to the parent, and the parent's private turn calls `message(action=send)`.

issue.body:
Related: #193993, #193982

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a saved OpenClaw ID node keeps dialing the Gateway server key it learned at enrollment, so it cannot reconnect after the Gateway honestly rotates that key.

## User Impact

User impact: nodes refresh and verify the claw's current signed server authority and membership before every connection, follow an honest server-key rotation without rejoining, close a connection whose server key was replaced, and keep learned trust across restarts and refused rejoins. A node whose access was removed stops with a rejoin instruction, and the reason for any other refusal is printed once instead of a bare connection failure.

- A preview target saved without a Discovery origin no longer breaks `openclaw node` config loading. It still never connects: the owner removes the node on the Access page, then it rejoins with a new link and `--discovery-url`, keeping its verified trust.
- Reconnects now fail closed when Discovery is unreachable or serves stale evidence. A Discovery outage therefore interrupts node connections until it recovers. This is an intended tradeoff.
- Pairing assumes the invitation stays secret. The six-digit comparison does not protect against a stolen invitation combined with control of pairing delivery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Enrollment and reconnect share one node-signed Discovery client and descriptor verifier. Before each dial and periodic probe, the node verifies the binding, snapshot freshness and its own membership. The canonical SQLite writer saves the strongest binding, the membership order and the binding-retirement facts before any dial, without touching unrelated node settings. If that save fails, the node stops.

Rebased onto `main` after #193993. Its pre-mail re-enroll refusal, recovery-hint messages, `loadNodeTunnelKey` export and supervised foreground join are kept. Maintainer follow-up commits on top of Josh Avant's commit:

- Signed trust from a Discovery response is saved even when the response's unsigned relay URL is invalid; that response is still never dialed. Before this fix, a later attempt could accept older evidence that was still fresh.
- Preview targets without `discoveryUrl` load for an explicit-origin rejoin, but the runner refuses to dial them.
- Refusal reasons reach the node operator: once per distinct reason, built locally, with no Discovery response text.
- When Discovery refuses to serve a node's descriptor (403), for example after a removed node restarts, the host prints re-join guidance and keeps retrying without dialing. The refusal is unsigned, so it does not stop the host the way verified removal does.

## Evidence

- Regression tests, each red on the pre-fix code and green with the fix:
  - invalid relay URLs (`ftp:`, embedded credentials) keep binding 2 and snapshot 3, then refuse the older binding-1 evidence;
  - a preview SQLite row without `discoveryUrl` loads, refuses to dial, keeps stronger trust on a refused rejoin, and adopts the explicit origin on an admitted rejoin;
  - a refusal is reported once across repeated bridged requests;
  - an unsigned Discovery 403 prints re-join guidance and neither stops the host nor dials.
- Focused suites pass on the final head: enrollment, join, connection, transport, target, SQLite config, runner and protocol freshness (107 tests).
- The native node-host Gateway suite passes 6 of 7 with the real Linux iroh addon. The remaining case, `both streaming transfer routes use the same private bridge` (ECONNRESET), fails the same way on unmodified `origin/main` on the same host.
- Other checks: `pnpm tsgo:core`, changed-file oxlint and format, `git diff --check`, the mock-export ratchet and knip pass. The test-line ratchet against `origin/main` passes with an exact allocation (+776, slack 0). `deadcode:exports` reports only untouched exports in `src/daemon/launchd.ts` and `ui/.../dashboard-tools.tsx`, so that failure comes from `main`.
- An independent review found no P0 or P1 issues. Two findings were verified and fixed: refusal diagnostics (P2) and the preview-target recovery path, which conflicted with the re-enroll refusal (P3).
- At `92bbf99`, CI failed only `checks-node-changed-12`. Two `update-command-resume-completion.test.ts` cases failed because their Doctor fixture timed out (exit 124) under Bun. This PR does not touch that file, and it passes locally (11 of 11). At head `7863d1d`, all CI checks pass, including `checks-node-changed-12`, `Scan changed paths (precise)`, `check-lint-core-2` and `openclaw/ci-gate`.
- ClawSweeper's input scanner (TruffleHog `URI` detector) refused two synthetic `https://user:…@` test fixtures: one added here and one already on `main` in `openclaw-id-target.test.ts`. Both fixtures now build their userinfo at runtime. A local TruffleHog scan of all changed files at `58ac569` reports 0 findings. That head changes only those two tests and the line allocation.

### Live proof

The proof ran 7 of 7 steps green on build `92bbf99`, against staging OpenClaw ID and Discovery with a throwaway claw.

- **Gateway:** an isolated Gateway on the Mac Studio, with its own profile, state directory and port.
- **Owner:** real Chromium.
- **Node:** this PR's CLI on Linux, with `env -i` and isolated profiles.
- **Discovery:** the node reached staging Discovery through a local untrusted proxy. In pass mode the proxy forwards node-signed requests unchanged. It can also corrupt the unsigned `relay_url` or replay an earlier captured response.

| Step | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Join | Owner and node codes matched; the node connected over the tunnel with binding 1. |
| Honest rotation 1→2 while the node runs | The Gateway restarted on a new key (`iroh:3abd…` → `iroh:c952…`). The same node ID reconnected in about 7 s without rejoining. `system.which` ran over the new connection. The saved target is binding 2 with the new key, snapshot seq 3. |
| Restarted node, replayed binding 1 (still fresh) | Refused once: `Possible claw substitution: rollback`. No connection while the replay was served. The node connected once current evidence returned, without a restart. |
| (a) Rotation 2→3 served with relay `ftp://…` | Refused: `Discovery returned an invalid relay URL…`, and nothing was dialed. The saved target advanced to binding 3 with the new key and kept the previous relay. A replay of binding 2 was then refused (`rollback`), and the node connected on current evidence. |
| (b) Preview target without `discoveryUrl` | `node run` exits with the owner-removal and re-join guidance and makes no Discovery request. `node join --discovery-url` loads the profile, the owner approves, and the node connects. The saved target has the explicit origin and binding 3. |
| Verified removal | The owner removed the running node on Access. The host stopped with `OpenClaw ID node access was removed or is not admitted; re-join this node`. A restarted node never connected. |

Gaps:

- **No production rotation path.** `main` has no Gateway command that rotates the server key. Proof-only plumbing stopped the isolated Gateway, generated a new endpoint key, and signed `ServerBinding(seq+1)` for it with the claw root from the throwaway recovery kit. The unmodified Gateway then republished on start.
- **Retiring a still-live old connection was not shown live.** The old key went away with the restart, so this proof cannot separate retiring a still-live old connection from losing it. The transport tests cover that retirement.
- **The removed-restart guidance was fixed after this run.** On `92bbf99` the restarted node retried silently on Discovery's 403. On `7863d1d`, a rerun against the same removed node prints `Discovery does not list this node for the claw; retrying. If the owner removed this node, re-join it with a new link.` and does not dial.

Cleanup: the throwaway claw was retired from staging Discovery. The isolated Gateway was stopped, and its profile was backed up and removed. The local node profiles, proxy and secrets were removed, and the staging lock was released.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native OpenClaw ID nodes need a Swift/Kotlin transport with QUIC keep-alive and exact numeric application close codes for `openclaw/tunnel/1`.

## User Impact

No user-visible change yet. No app consumes this crate until Android #194194 and Apple #194201 land; default app builds are unchanged. This PR adds the standalone transport foundation, not an app cutover or a release.

**Remaining platform and release gates:** iOS builds successfully but has not been runtime-proven on a device or simulator. Device transport, mobile lifecycle, and final APK/AAB packaging remain consumer-lane work. License notices for UniFFI, `attohttpc`, and MPL-covered dependencies must be completed before shipping the apps; they are a release gate, not a gate for merging this source-only crate.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OpenClaw-owned adapter pins iroh 1.4.1 (matching the Node addon) and UniFFI 0.31.2. It exposes endpoint bind/connect, bidirectional streams, typed close information preserving every legal 62-bit QUIC application code, home-relay status, and explicit cancellation/shutdown. The existing Node addon is unchanged. Apps retain enrollment, destination verification, framing, protected key storage, and lifecycle ownership.

The native input seed is zeroized on success and failure; this does not promise erasure of Swift/Kotlin or UniFFI marshalling copies. The Minimal preset uses only the supplied relay, with no default discovery service. Android must install its Application context before binding. Swift cancellation must use native `CancelToken`/stream stop-reset/shutdown; Kotlin callers shield native result delivery with `NonCancellable` and use the same explicit cancellation signals to avoid abandoning lowered results.

`libc` stays pinned to 0.2.189 until follow-up **openclaw-85d** removes the incompatible iOS dependency path. The pin is guarded in CI and documented in `PACKAGING.md`; the locked dependencies are audited on changes and weekly. No dependency upgrade or pin removal is part of this merge.

## Evidence

Final candidate: **`d5003c1e09b565fd3b23f4e8dcfd991ac8ea3254`**. Its only change after `f1adbdd` corrects the README's obsolete no-upload claim to describe the short-lived Apple CI artifact; all code, bindings, lockfiles, tests, and workflows are byte-identical. Final-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42638547053), [native Linux/Android/Apple builds](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42638546821), and [dependency audit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42638546987) passed. Required CI/security gates were verified green before native merge submission.

Completed proof at code-identical head **`f1adbdd671ceb0219961d52d568d00ba7c688274`**:

- [Native CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42623477334) passed Linux, Android, and Apple. Linux runs Rust tests/lint, checks generated bindings, and builds the release library. Android builds all four ABIs with ELF LOAD alignment >=16 KiB. Apple builds all five Rust targets into the macOS/iOS-device/iOS-simulator XCFramework and typechecks the generated Swift.
- [Dependency audit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42623477771) passed, including the libc pin check and RustSec audit.
- Local Rust 1.99 validation passed: `cargo test --locked` (1 unit + 5 real loopback integration tests), `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, formatting, the pin check, deterministic Swift/Kotlin regeneration, and all 21 generated Kotlin ABI checksums against the rebuilt host library. The tests cover exact 2^62−1 application close codes, streams/FIN, input bounds, seed erasure, watcher shutdown, blocked read/accept/connect shutdown, and per-operation dial/stream cancellation while retaining endpoint/connection usability.
- Linux release library: 13,189,976 bytes; SHA-256 `cbda14805e7c8f583c7760a84228b84f590c2c48780654934c60846c11d03bb3`.
- [Apple CI artifact](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42623477334/artifacts/13678113168) is a short-lived workflow artifact, not a published package or app release.

Consumer-lane evidence is distinct from crate CI:
- Apple #194201 [Swift CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42624699734) passed at Apple head `ee25eeaea9129b4999b59c4dc7e535be760858a1`, based on this crate head `f1adbdd`. It builds matching bindings/macOS XCFramework and passes the native Swift → Rust loopback (1/1) and shared tests (25/25). This is macOS proof, not iOS runtime proof.
- Android #194194 passed [default-build/no-iroh validation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42623709966) and [opt-in build/tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42623719554) at Android head `d5f9459788221dc623e9b9f9e0ee778236f2ca61`, based on this crate head `f1adbdd`.
- The Android lane's JVM → generated Kotlin/JNA → Rust loopback (framing, FIN, 62-bit close code, cancelled/pre-cancelled dial) used the retained `.so` built at crate `92c2506`, whose ABI sources and generated bindings are unchanged at `f1adbdd`. This is prior-build evidence, not a freshly rebuilt exact-head JVM run or Android device proof.

Independent read-only Astra landing review covered the complete 25-file diff from merge-base `d88a384060d6d0f55920fc0092877c58d128cc3e` to `f1adbdd671ceb0219961d52d568d00ba7c688274`, including dependency ownership/cancellation and platform packaging contracts. issue.body:
Related: #193982 (node transport, merged), #194001 (Gateway node admission, merged), #194007 (Access node invites, merged), #195507 (one automatic node pairing per approved listing, merged; found by this PR's live proof)

## What Problem This Solves

Headless nodes need an owner-approved way to join an OpenClaw ID claw without a user account or a Gateway token.

## User Impact

Adds `openclaw node join <openclaw-node-link>` and sends the same link through `openclaw connect`. The node shows a six-digit code and its signed command list. The owner compares the code and approves on the Access page. After approval, the node checks that it was admitted, then connects in the foreground, or installs a user service with `--service`.

- **Discovery origin.** Set it with `--discovery-url` or reuse the one saved with the node's target; there is no production default. The origin is never derived from the claw hostname or relay URL.
- **Re-joining.** `node join` now refuses a node that is still admitted, and leaves the new invitation unused. To change a node's commands, the owner removes it on the Access page and sends a new link. Plain reconnects use `openclaw node run` or the installed service.
- **Supervision.** A foreground `node join` now runs under the packaged node supervisor, the same as `connect`. Supervisor restarts use `node run`, never the one-time link.
- **Labs preview limits.** Unix hosts and native-process workers only. Node is the qualified runtime; Bun streaming qualification is still pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

The node signs the command manifest it actually prepared, with its own local key, and Discovery only ever sees the redemption proof. Before the runner saves the target, the node checks the root, claw and hostname pins, the highest same-claw binding sequence it has seen, signed snapshot freshness, and its own listing. The first connection reuses that prepared runtime. The service is installed only after a successful first hello and a clean shutdown.

**ClawSweeper's re-enrollment finding (P2).** A membership snapshot lists node keys only; it says nothing about which invitation or description the owner approved. A node that is already admitted would therefore look approved before the owner had decided on the new invitation. The node now checks Discovery before mailing the redemption, and refuses if it is already listed. It doesn't wait on the new invitation, and it doesn't spend it.

**Accepted edge (named in code).** Suppose an earlier invitation for the same node key is still pending and the owner approves it later. That approval can also complete a newer join that is waiting. Binding completion to one specific invitation needs a signed per-invitation outcome, which doesn't exist yet and is tracked as openclaw-607; this PR adds no protocol statement. The Gateway pairs only the commands from the description the owner approved (`approveOpenClawIdNodePairing`), so this edge can't widen what the node may run. A Discovery that lies about pending state can, at most, cause the same mismatch; it can't grant access.

**Authority at admission and execution.** Gateway #194001 owns this. Admission resolves the tunnel peer against the Gateway's current authority, not Discovery's snapshot. `resolveGatewayConnectPolicyFailure` and request dispatch then re-check `isOpenClawIdTunnelPrincipalCurrent` before any work runs. A new real-Gateway test covers both cases. A node key the Gateway doesn't list (pending, or removed after the node fetched its descriptor) is refused before pairing. A live node session is closed with code 4001 on its next request once its listing is removed. Existing coverage includes `authority.nodes.test.ts`, where pending nodes don't resolve and removal closes connections, and the pairing suite's stale-principal case.

**Stored data.** This PR adds no new store, field or migration. Node config stays in SQLite `nodeHost.config` v1, as in 2026.11.2. The `openclaw-id` target shape already shipped in #193982. Existing Gateway-mode targets keep loading unchanged; only an explicit `node join` replaces the saved target. See Evidence for the upgrade check.

**Test lines.** The allocation is 542, exactly this PR's net test-line delta. Against current main the ratchet reports 32 lines of slack; that headroom was already on main and isn't allocated by this PR.

## Evidence

- **Re-enrollment regression.** `refuses re-enrollment while old membership still lists W, before spending the invite` is red against the previous enrollment source and green with the fix.
- **Focused suites.** 172 passed, 7 native-binding tests skipped, across enrollment, join, runner, connect/register CLI, node daemon, the Gateway node-pairing suite and the native node-host suite. The node launcher suite passed 15/15, including the new `["node","join"]` supervised-restart case.
- **Static checks.** `pnpm tsgo:core`, scoped oxlint and oxfmt, and `pnpm deadcode:exports` all passed with 0 entries. `loadNodeTunnelKey` is exported again because `openclaw-id-join.ts` uses it; #195338 had made it private. The mock-isolation ratchet passes; each orchestration mock in the join suite states why it is isolated.
- **Independent Astra review.** It found two P2s. The supervisor bypass is fixed. The pending-earlier-invitation edge is accepted as described above, pending openclaw-607. Neither finding bypasses Gateway enforcement.
- **Stored-data upgrade (isolated profiles, env cleared of live-Gateway variables).** 2026.10.10 configured a node host in plain Gateway mode against an isolated 2026.11.2 Gateway: it saved SQLite `nodeHost.config` v1 and paired. The PR head's `node run` with no flags then loaded that config and connected with the existing pairing (0 pending requests). The config bytes were unchanged (same hash). A failed `node join` (Discovery unreachable) left the config unchanged apart from creating the node's 0600 endpoint key, and `node run` connected again afterwards. Note: main is versioned 2026.11.1, so a 2026.11.2 → PR head run is a version downgrade and stops at the newer-config check; that is why the upgrade was seeded from 2026.10.10.
- **Exact-head CI on `7cf477a8e9e5`:** 73 passed, 52 skipped, 0 failed. Current head `eac8b7f06c2f`: CI is running.
- **Follow-up `eac8b7f` (ClawSweeper P3, after the live run):** failed descriptor or membership verification now names a recovery step. A stale membership snapshot asks the operator to have the claw owner check that the Gateway is online and connected to OpenClaw ID, then join with a new link; an invalid descriptor asks them to check `--discovery-url` with the owner. Only error strings and the stale-snapshot test assertion changed; enrollment logic didn't. The live proof below ran on `7cf477a`, and the enrollment, join and connect suites pass 46/46 at `eac8b7f`.
- **Rebase onto main (with #195507):** `git range-diff ac26a0d7f1f8..70d8109b8a56 origin/main..7cf477a8e9e5` shows all 4 commits unchanged (`=`).

### Live proof on the staging testnet (build `7cf477a`, this PR's head)

**Setup:**
- **Gateway:** an isolated Gateway on a Mac Studio, built from `7cf477a8e9e5` with its own profile, port and state, and linked as the throwaway staging claw `ocid517proof2-e61zr.crabd.xyz`. The Studio's own Gateway wasn't touched.
- **Owner:** used real Chromium against the real staging OpenClaw ID, Discovery, loader and relay. They signed in, enrolled with the recovery kit, and opened **Access** over the tunnel. This Gateway has no model configured, so the default landing goes to model setup; the harness opens the app with `?session=main`. Node admission doesn't depend on this.
- **Nodes:** ran this PR's shipped CLI on a Linux host, each in an isolated profile, with environment variables from the host's own Gateway cleared.

All 9 checks passed in one run:

| # | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Owner signs in and opens **Access**, then **Nodes**, over the tunnel | pass |
| 2 | Denied invite | Codes matched (`794-600`) and the owner selected **Deny node**. The invite reads `denied` and no node is listed. The waiting node never connected and, when cancelled, reported "no target was saved". |
| 3 | Approved invite | Codes matched (`865-003`) and the owner approved. The Gateway logged `admission allowed … path=relay` and then repeated admissions with `path=direct`. The node reported `connected … via OpenClaw ID (direct)`, and its device was auto-paired as `openclaw-id-node`. |
| 4 | A node command runs | `node.invoke system.which` over the tunnel returned `{"bins":{"sh":"/usr/bin/sh"}}` |
| 5 | Re-enrolling the admitted node with a fresh invite and more commands | Refused (exit 1) with "This node is already admitted … ask the owner to remove it on the Access page, then join with a new link". The fresh invite stays `open`, unused. |
| 6 | A pending node (code shown, not approved), given the admitted node's saved target | Never connected. For 90 seconds it got only `socket hang up` / 1006. The Gateway logged no admission for its key: it was refused at relay/tunnel admission, before any Gateway stream. |
| 7 | Owner removes a live node after it has retrieved its descriptor | The live session ended: the node exited 1 with "OpenClaw ID node access was removed or is not admitted; re-join this node". Restarting `node run` from the saved target never connected (`socket hang up`), and the Gateway logged no admission for that key between removal and the new approval. |
| 8 | Re-joining after removal with a new invite and more commands (`system.which,system.run`) | The node waited and connected only after the owner compared the code (`061-592`) and approved. The Gateway then auto-paired the same device (`approvedVia: openclaw-id-node`, 0 pending Devices approvals). `node.list` shows `system.run` and `system.which`. `system.which` worked, and `system.run echo` returned exit 0 with `stdout: "ocid517-ok"`. |
| 9 | `--service` | Approved (code `379-356`). The join installed the isolated user unit `openclaw-node-ocid517svc.service`, which became `active`. After `systemctl --user restart`, the journal shows a new `node host gateway connected … (direct)` and `node.list` shows the node connected again. |

**Path:** every node was admitted over the relay first and then moved to a direct path, according to both the node diagnostics and the Gateway's tunnel log.

**Before #195507:** an earlier run on build `70d8109`, against a claw since retired, passed steps 1–7. Step 8 then failed: after removal and a new approval, the Gateway answered `device pairing required` and left a non-repair pending node request. #195507 fixed that in the Gateway; step 8 above is the after.

**Cleanup:**
- The service unit is uninstalled, and the user unit list matches the list recorded before the run.
- The local node profiles and secrets are removed.
- The claw is retired in Discovery staging; queries show 0 claw, member and relay-key rows.
- The isolated Gateway is stopped. Its profile was backed up, then removed.
- The staging lock was taken for the run and released afterwards.

**Remaining limits:**
- The proof used Linux nodes with Node as the runtime. macOS, Windows and Bun weren't exercised (see the Labs preview limits above).
- Steps 6 and 7 show refusal at relay/tunnel admission. The Gateway's own refusal of unlisted and removed keys is covered by the real-Gateway test in this PR.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a session's reply fails mid-turn with "Cron occurrence source authority is no longer active" when another session's scheduled run sent it work with `sessions_send` and that run then ends.

## User Impact

A turn that another session hands off keeps running after the sender's scheduled run finishes, reschedules itself with `next_check`, deletes its one-shot job, or has its isolated run session cleaned up. Any of these still stops it:

- revoking the sender's role, access grant or profile;
- for device-token operators, revoking the sender's device;
- an explicit Stop.

A job's own turn still ends when the job is disabled or removed.

For trusted-proxy (person-identity) operators, authority is bound to the person. Revoking the person's role, grant or profile stops a handed-off turn. Removing their browser's device pairing does not. This is unchanged since #166553, and child receivers on `main` already behave this way. See Evidence.

## Why This Change Was Made

A turn admitted through `sessions_send` (and chat.send or Talk) inherits the sending run's operator authority. Since #176422 (`d74a4aeb7d62`), a scheduled continuation restores that authority bound to its single occurrence and to its exact session. #178693 moved only **child** targets onto the retained continuation authority. That authority keeps the person, role, grant and device-token checks but drops the occurrence binding. Any other receiver, such as the sender's parent or a peer, kept the occurrence-bound authority and failed as soon as the occurrence ended. This shipped in `v2026.10.10-beta.3`; the last stable release, `v2026.10.9`, is unaffected.

This change:

- makes every accepted turn retained through `retainGatewayOperatorRun` use the continuation authority, and removes the child-only `spawnedBy` plumbing;
- separates the claimed sender session's lifecycle from the continuation. Replacing or removing the sender's session (for example, cleanup of an isolated run's exact-run session) now ends only the sender's own run-bound authority. Previously it aborted the shared policy signal and also killed handed-off turns.

### Deliberate revocations (ruled on by @jalehman)

1. Sender device revoked: kept, for device-token operators. For trusted-proxy identities the source has no device binding (#166553), so the person-level checks below apply.
2. Profile or role change, or access grant ended: kept.
3. Explicit user Stop: kept.
4. A job's own turn when the job is disabled or removed: kept. The job's own run does not go through this path. Editing a running job's payload does not cancel its in-flight turn, on base or head.
5. Messages sent into a job's own `cron:<jobId>` session, which the next run takes over: unchanged for now.

### Known follow-up

Plugin subagent dispatch (`server-plugin-in-process-dispatch.ts`, `plugin_subagent`) still borrows its caller's authority without a retained continuation. It is out of scope here.

## Evidence

### Production incident

On a production Gateway (2026.11.1 `d4d6fe7`) at 2026-11-08 17:01:14 PST, a dashboard session's turn failed when the scheduled continuation of another session that had `sessions_send`-ed it work finished. The receiving session was the sender's parent, not a child:

```
session target preparation refused runId=9ff84731-… reason=source_authority_refused
… Cron occurrence source authority is no longer active
```

Earlier occurrences: 2026-11-07 07:47 and 08:08 PST, plus 2026-10-23, 10-24 and 11-06. None before 2026-10-23.

### Real-Gateway proof (isolated macOS host)

**Setup:**

- **Builds:** each build runs `openclaw.mjs gateway run` as its own process, with an isolated `HOME`, state dir, port and `env -i` environment. Builds: head `64c61302dffb`, merge-base `83f7614cc70d` and current `main` `a35b92ce7ea7`.
- **Real paths:** the cron scheduler, `automations`, `sessions_send`, `sessions_spawn` and agent runs are all real.
- **Scripted model:** only the model is scripted, using a deterministic OpenAI Responses server, so the interleaving is exact.
- **People:** two people sign in through trusted-proxy over TLS. Alice is an admin; Bob is the sender.
- **Job creation:** Bob's authenticated turn creates the job with the `automations` tool, like the incident.
- **Receiver hold:** the receiver is held mid-turn until the occurrence has finished.
- **Protected effect:** the receiver then sends with `sessions_send` into a third session. That effect needs the retained operator authority, and its observable result is the third session's turn reaching the model.
- **Grant case:** this uses a test-only `proof-grant` access-policy plugin loaded from a path through the shipped access-policy contract.

| Case | Base `83f7614` | Head `64c6130` |
|---|---|---|
| P1 one-shot `at` continuation; occurrence finishes and the job self-deletes | **refused** (`source_authority_refused`, "Cron occurrence source authority is no longer active") | **effect executes** |
| P2 recurring job; forced run finishes | refused | executes |
| P3 one-shot that reschedules itself with `next_check` | refused | executes |
| P4 `isolated` job; run session cleaned up | refused | executes |
| P5 child receiver (visible `sessions_spawn`) | executes | executes |
| F2 sender profile merged away after the occurrence ends | refused | **refused before the effect** |
| F3 sender role changed (`users.setRole`) | refused | **refused before the effect** |
| F4 sender's access grant ended | refused | **refused before the effect** |
| F5 explicit Stop (`chat.abort`) on the receiver | refused | **refused before the effect** |
| D1 device-token operator: device removed, peer receiver | refused | **refused before the effect** |
| D2 device-token operator: device removed, child receiver | refused | refused |
| D3 / D4 device-token operator positive controls (peer / child) | refused / executes | executes / executes |
| F1 trusted-proxy operator: device pairing removed, peer receiver | refused (occurrence binding) | executes: person-bound by design |
| F1b trusted-proxy operator: device pairing removed, child receiver | executes | executes (`main` `a35b92c`: executes) |
| O1 / O2 job's own turn; job disabled / removed while running | turn cancelled, no effect | turn cancelled, no effect |

**How the refusals happen:**

- **F2–F4:** the receiver's run is aborted within about 15 ms of the revocation, before the effect is reached, with "Restart recovery operator authority changed" (F4 also logs "proof grant ended").
- **F5:** aborted with "agent run aborted".
- **In every refused case:** no turn ever reaches the third session.

**F1 / F1b:** at the effect timestamp, Bob's client was already closed, and the pairing store shows neither a paired nor a pending row for his device. Trusted-proxy ingress attaches no device token (`connect-operator-access.ts`, "Shared/proxy identity can be tokenless"). The recovery snapshot therefore carries no device, which `#166553` pins with "does not adopt an incidental paired token for tokenless trusted-proxy ingress". Child receivers on base and on current `main` behave the same.

**Timing check:** I re-ran F1 and F1b with 1 s, 5 s and 15 s between the device removal and the effect. Both execute every time, and D1 is refused every time. So this is not a timing window; the device is never checked for a person-bound source.

**Traces (sanitized excerpts, source head `64c6130`; head `c53296a` only adds a test-lines allocation file).** Each run below is one built Gateway. Lines come from the harness timeline plus the Gateway log's authority lines; IDs are shortened, prompt-cache noise and JSON payloads are trimmed. "sink" is the third session the receiver's protected `sessions_send` targets; in every refused run the sink holds only its creation message. Included: P1 on base (refused) and head (executes), F3 role change on head (aborted ~16 ms after the revoke, before release), D1 device-token device removal on head (aborted before release), and F1 trusted-proxy pairing removal on head (executes; person-bound).

### Regression tests

In `operator-run-cancellation.test.ts`:

- Ending the sender's occurrence: fails on base, passes with the fix.
- Cleaning up the sender's session: fails at the first commit, passes with the second.
- Revoking the device still stops the turn. This is the same `it.each` case in `operator-run-cancellation.test.ts`, run as a device-token operator: the sender's source carries a paired device token (`pairedOperator()`), and the case calls `invalidateGatewayDeviceRevocation` after retention. It does not cover trusted-proxy identities, which carry no device binding (see Evidence).

### Checks

- `c53296a` adds `config/test-lines-allocations/194798-receiver-continuation-authority.txt` (56, the measured net test growth) for the `test-lines` ratchet; no source change.

- `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` pass; commit hooks ran.
- Related suites: 122 files and 1,522 tests pass.
- Independent review: found one P2, the sender-session cleanup gap. It is fixed in the second commit.

### Gaps

- The model is scripted. A live model can't hold a receiver mid-turn at an exact point. I did not do a live-model positive run, because it would mean copying real provider credentials onto the proof host.
- The harness is not committed: it is about 600 lines, over the test cost budget.

### ClawSweeper blockers

1. **Inspectable authority-chain trace of a real run, including the nearest forbidden case.** See P1 versus F2–F5 and D1 above. Each run records:
   - timestamps and run IDs;
   - the occurrence finishing and the job's state afterwards (removed, rescheduled or disabled);
   - the revocation;
   - the receiver's effect, executed or refused;
   - the third session's state.

   The nearest forbidden case to P1 is the same run plus one revocation after the occurrence has ended: F2 (profile), F3 (role), F4 (grant), D1 (device-token device) or F5 (Stop). Each is refused before the effect.
2. **Revocation after continuation retention must reject before the receiver's protected effect, at the effect boundary rather than through `assertCurrent`.** F2–F5 and D1 revoke through the real Gateway methods (`users.merge`, `users.setRole`, the grant policy, `chat.abort`, `device.pair.remove`) after retention. In each, the receiver's `sessions_send` never produces a turn in the target session.
3. **Merge risk: the broader lifetime must not carry revoked sender authority into a receiver's protected effect.** It doesn't, for every revocation the authority model defines: person, role, grant, device token and Stop. The one non-revocation, a trusted-proxy browser's device pairing, is the existing person-bound model from #166553. It already applies to child receivers on `main` (F1b), and the scope is stated above.
