issue.body:
Related: #193982 (node transport, merged), #194001 (Gateway node admission, merged), #194007 (Access node invites, merged), #195507 (one automatic node pairing per approved listing, merged; found by this PR's live proof)

## What Problem This Solves

Headless nodes need an owner-approved way to join an OpenClaw ID claw without a user account or a Gateway token.

## User Impact

Adds `openclaw node join <openclaw-node-link>` and sends the same link through `openclaw connect`. The node shows a six-digit code and its signed command list. The owner compares the code and approves on the Access page. After approval, the node checks that it was admitted, then connects in the foreground, or installs a user service with `--service`.

- **Discovery origin.** Set it with `--discovery-url` or reuse the one saved with the node's target; there is no production default. The origin is never derived from the claw hostname or relay URL.
- **Re-joining.** `node join` now refuses a node that is still admitted, and leaves the new invitation unused. To change a node's commands, the owner removes it on the Access page and sends a new link. Plain reconnects use `openclaw node run` or the installed service.
- **Supervision.** A foreground `node join` now runs under the packaged node supervisor, the same as `connect`. Supervisor restarts use `node run`, never the one-time link.
- **Labs preview limits.** Unix hosts and native-process workers only. Node is the qualified runtime; Bun streaming qualification is still pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

The node signs the command manifest it actually prepared, with its own local key, and Discovery only ever sees the redemption proof. Before the runner saves the target, the node checks the root, claw and hostname pins, the highest same-claw binding sequence it has seen, signed snapshot freshness, and its own listing. The first connection reuses that prepared runtime. The service is installed only after a successful first hello and a clean shutdown.

**ClawSweeper's re-enrollment finding (P2).** A membership snapshot lists node keys only; it says nothing about which invitation or description the owner approved. A node that is already admitted would therefore look approved before the owner had decided on the new invitation. The node now checks Discovery before mailing the redemption, and refuses if it is already listed. It doesn't wait on the new invitation, and it doesn't spend it.

**Accepted edge (named in code).** Suppose an earlier invitation for the same node key is still pending and the owner approves it later. That approval can also complete a newer join that is waiting. Binding completion to one specific invitation needs a signed per-invitation outcome, which doesn't exist yet and is tracked as openclaw-607; this PR adds no protocol statement. The Gateway pairs only the commands from the description the owner approved (`approveOpenClawIdNodePairing`), so this edge can't widen what the node may run. A Discovery that lies about pending state can, at most, cause the same mismatch; it can't grant access.

**Authority at admission and execution.** Gateway #194001 owns this. Admission resolves the tunnel peer against the Gateway's current authority, not Discovery's snapshot. `resolveGatewayConnectPolicyFailure` and request dispatch then re-check `isOpenClawIdTunnelPrincipalCurrent` before any work runs. A new real-Gateway test covers both cases. A node key the Gateway doesn't list (pending, or removed after the node fetched its descriptor) is refused before pairing. A live node session is closed with code 4001 on its next request once its listing is removed. Existing coverage includes `authority.nodes.test.ts`, where pending nodes don't resolve and removal closes connections, and the pairing suite's stale-principal case.

**Stored data.** This PR adds no new store, field or migration. Node config stays in SQLite `nodeHost.config` v1, as in 2026.11.2. The `openclaw-id` target shape already shipped in #193982. Existing Gateway-mode targets keep loading unchanged; only an explicit `node join` replaces the saved target. See Evidence for the upgrade check.

**Test lines.** The allocation is 542, exactly this PR's net test-line delta. Against current main the ratchet reports 32 lines of slack; that headroom was already on main and isn't allocated by this PR.

## Evidence

- **Re-enrollment regression.** `refuses re-enrollment while old membership still lists W, before spending the invite` is red against the previous enrollment source and green with the fix.
- **Focused suites.** 172 passed, 7 native-binding tests skipped, across enrollment, join, runner, connect/register CLI, node daemon, the Gateway node-pairing suite and the native node-host suite. The node launcher suite passed 15/15, including the new `["node","join"]` supervised-restart case.
- **Static checks.** `pnpm tsgo:core`, scoped oxlint and oxfmt, and `pnpm deadcode:exports` all passed with 0 entries. `loadNodeTunnelKey` is exported again because `openclaw-id-join.ts` uses it; #195338 had made it private. The mock-isolation ratchet passes; each orchestration mock in the join suite states why it is isolated.
- **Independent Astra review.** It found two P2s. The supervisor bypass is fixed. The pending-earlier-invitation edge is accepted as described above, pending openclaw-607. Neither finding bypasses Gateway enforcement.
- **Stored-data upgrade (isolated profiles, env cleared of live-Gateway variables).** 2026.10.10 configured a node host in plain Gateway mode against an isolated 2026.11.2 Gateway: it saved SQLite `nodeHost.config` v1 and paired. The PR head's `node run` with no flags then loaded that config and connected with the existing pairing (0 pending requests). The config bytes were unchanged (same hash). A failed `node join` (Discovery unreachable) left the config unchanged apart from creating the node's 0600 endpoint key, and `node run` connected again afterwards. Note: main is versioned 2026.11.1, so a 2026.11.2 → PR head run is a version downgrade and stops at the newer-config check; that is why the upgrade was seeded from 2026.10.10.
- **Exact-head CI on `7cf477a8e9e5`:** 73 passed, 52 skipped, 0 failed. Current head `eac8b7f06c2f`: CI is running.
- **Follow-up `eac8b7f` (ClawSweeper P3, after the live run):** failed descriptor or membership verification now names a recovery step. A stale membership snapshot asks the operator to have the claw owner check that the Gateway is online and connected to OpenClaw ID, then join with a new link; an invalid descriptor asks them to check `--discovery-url` with the owner. Only error strings and the stale-snapshot test assertion changed; enrollment logic didn't. The live proof below ran on `7cf477a`, and the enrollment, join and connect suites pass 46/46 at `eac8b7f`.
- **Rebase onto main (with #195507):** `git range-diff ac26a0d7f1f8..70d8109b8a56 origin/main..7cf477a8e9e5` shows all 4 commits unchanged (`=`).

### Live proof on the staging testnet (build `7cf477a`, this PR's head)

**Setup:**
- **Gateway:** an isolated Gateway on a Mac Studio, built from `7cf477a8e9e5` with its own profile, port and state, and linked as the throwaway staging claw `ocid517proof2-e61zr.crabd.xyz`. The Studio's own Gateway wasn't touched.
- **Owner:** used real Chromium against the real staging OpenClaw ID, Discovery, loader and relay. They signed in, enrolled with the recovery kit, and opened **Access** over the tunnel. This Gateway has no model configured, so the default landing goes to model setup; the harness opens the app with `?session=main`. Node admission doesn't depend on this.
- **Nodes:** ran this PR's shipped CLI on a Linux host, each in an isolated profile, with environment variables from the host's own Gateway cleared.

All 9 checks passed in one run:

| # | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Owner signs in and opens **Access**, then **Nodes**, over the tunnel | pass |
| 2 | Denied invite | Codes matched (`794-600`) and the owner selected **Deny node**. The invite reads `denied` and no node is listed. The waiting node never connected and, when cancelled, reported "no target was saved". |
| 3 | Approved invite | Codes matched (`865-003`) and the owner approved. The Gateway logged `admission allowed … path=relay` and then repeated admissions with `path=direct`. The node reported `connected … via OpenClaw ID (direct)`, and its device was auto-paired as `openclaw-id-node`. |
| 4 | A node command runs | `node.invoke system.which` over the tunnel returned `{"bins":{"sh":"/usr/bin/sh"}}` |
| 5 | Re-enrolling the admitted node with a fresh invite and more commands | Refused (exit 1) with "This node is already admitted … ask the owner to remove it on the Access page, then join with a new link". The fresh invite stays `open`, unused. |
| 6 | A pending node (code shown, not approved), given the admitted node's saved target | Never connected. For 90 seconds it got only `socket hang up` / 1006. The Gateway logged no admission for its key: it was refused at relay/tunnel admission, before any Gateway stream. |
| 7 | Owner removes a live node after it has retrieved its descriptor | The live session ended: the node exited 1 with "OpenClaw ID node access was removed or is not admitted; re-join this node". Restarting `node run` from the saved target never connected (`socket hang up`), and the Gateway logged no admission for that key between removal and the new approval. |
| 8 | Re-joining after removal with a new invite and more commands (`system.which,system.run`) | The node waited and connected only after the owner compared the code (`061-592`) and approved. The Gateway then auto-paired the same device (`approvedVia: openclaw-id-node`, 0 pending Devices approvals). `node.list` shows `system.run` and `system.which`. `system.which` worked, and `system.run echo` returned exit 0 with `stdout: "ocid517-ok"`. |
| 9 | `--service` | Approved (code `379-356`). The join installed the isolated user unit `openclaw-node-ocid517svc.service`, which became `active`. After `systemctl --user restart`, the journal shows a new `node host gateway connected … (direct)` and `node.list` shows the node connected again. |

**Path:** every node was admitted over the relay first and then moved to a direct path, according to both the node diagnostics and the Gateway's tunnel log.

**Before #195507:** an earlier run on build `70d8109`, against a claw since retired, passed steps 1–7. Step 8 then failed: after removal and a new approval, the Gateway answered `device pairing required` and left a non-repair pending node request. #195507 fixed that in the Gateway; step 8 above is the after.

**Cleanup:**
- The service unit is uninstalled, and the user unit list matches the list recorded before the run.
- The local node profiles and secrets are removed.
- The claw is retired in Discovery staging; queries show 0 claw, member and relay-key rows.
- The isolated Gateway is stopped. Its profile was backed up, then removed.
- The staging lock was taken for the run and released afterwards.

**Remaining limits:**
- The proof used Linux nodes with Node as the runtime. macOS, Windows and Bun weren't exercised (see the Labs preview limits above).
- Steps 6 and 7 show refusal at relay/tunnel admission. The Gateway's own refusal of unlisted and removed keys is covered by the real-Gateway test in this PR.

issue.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a session's reply fails mid-turn with "Cron occurrence source authority is no longer active" when another session's scheduled run sent it work with `sessions_send` and that run then ends.

## User Impact

A turn that another session hands off keeps running after the sender's scheduled run finishes, reschedules itself with `next_check`, deletes its one-shot job, or has its isolated run session cleaned up. Any of these still stops it:

- revoking the sender's role, access grant or profile;
- for device-token operators, revoking the sender's device;
- an explicit Stop.

A job's own turn still ends when the job is disabled or removed.

For trusted-proxy (person-identity) operators, authority is bound to the person. Revoking the person's role, grant or profile stops a handed-off turn. Removing their browser's device pairing does not. This is unchanged since #166553, and child receivers on `main` already behave this way. See Evidence.

## Why This Change Was Made

A turn admitted through `sessions_send` (and chat.send or Talk) inherits the sending run's operator authority. Since #176422 (`d74a4aeb7d62`), a scheduled continuation restores that authority bound to its single occurrence and to its exact session. #178693 moved only **child** targets onto the retained continuation authority. That authority keeps the person, role, grant and device-token checks but drops the occurrence binding. Any other receiver, such as the sender's parent or a peer, kept the occurrence-bound authority and failed as soon as the occurrence ended. This shipped in `v2026.10.10-beta.3`; the last stable release, `v2026.10.9`, is unaffected.

This change:

- makes every accepted turn retained through `retainGatewayOperatorRun` use the continuation authority, and removes the child-only `spawnedBy` plumbing;
- separates the claimed sender session's lifecycle from the continuation. Replacing or removing the sender's session (for example, cleanup of an isolated run's exact-run session) now ends only the sender's own run-bound authority. Previously it aborted the shared policy signal and also killed handed-off turns.

### Deliberate revocations (ruled on by @jalehman)

1. Sender device revoked: kept, for device-token operators. For trusted-proxy identities the source has no device binding (#166553), so the person-level checks below apply.
2. Profile or role change, or access grant ended: kept.
3. Explicit user Stop: kept.
4. A job's own turn when the job is disabled or removed: kept. The job's own run does not go through this path. Editing a running job's payload does not cancel its in-flight turn, on base or head.
5. Messages sent into a job's own `cron:<jobId>` session, which the next run takes over: unchanged for now.

### Known follow-up

Plugin subagent dispatch (`server-plugin-in-process-dispatch.ts`, `plugin_subagent`) still borrows its caller's authority without a retained continuation. It is out of scope here.

## Evidence

### Production incident

On a production Gateway (2026.11.1 `d4d6fe7`) at 2026-11-08 17:01:14 PST, a dashboard session's turn failed when the scheduled continuation of another session that had `sessions_send`-ed it work finished. The receiving session was the sender's parent, not a child:

```
session target preparation refused runId=9ff84731-… reason=source_authority_refused
… Cron occurrence source authority is no longer active
```

Earlier occurrences: 2026-11-07 07:47 and 08:08 PST, plus 2026-10-23, 10-24 and 11-06. None before 2026-10-23.

### Real-Gateway proof (isolated macOS host)

**Setup:**

- **Builds:** each build runs `openclaw.mjs gateway run` as its own process, with an isolated `HOME`, state dir, port and `env -i` environment. Builds: head `64c61302dffb`, merge-base `83f7614cc70d` and current `main` `a35b92ce7ea7`.
- **Real paths:** the cron scheduler, `automations`, `sessions_send`, `sessions_spawn` and agent runs are all real.
- **Scripted model:** only the model is scripted, using a deterministic OpenAI Responses server, so the interleaving is exact.
- **People:** two people sign in through trusted-proxy over TLS. Alice is an admin; Bob is the sender.
- **Job creation:** Bob's authenticated turn creates the job with the `automations` tool, like the incident.
- **Receiver hold:** the receiver is held mid-turn until the occurrence has finished.
- **Protected effect:** the receiver then sends with `sessions_send` into a third session. That effect needs the retained operator authority, and its observable result is the third session's turn reaching the model.
- **Grant case:** this uses a test-only `proof-grant` access-policy plugin loaded from a path through the shipped access-policy contract.

| Case | Base `83f7614` | Head `64c6130` |
|---|---|---|
| P1 one-shot `at` continuation; occurrence finishes and the job self-deletes | **refused** (`source_authority_refused`, "Cron occurrence source authority is no longer active") | **effect executes** |
| P2 recurring job; forced run finishes | refused | executes |
| P3 one-shot that reschedules itself with `next_check` | refused | executes |
| P4 `isolated` job; run session cleaned up | refused | executes |
| P5 child receiver (visible `sessions_spawn`) | executes | executes |
| F2 sender profile merged away after the occurrence ends | refused | **refused before the effect** |
| F3 sender role changed (`users.setRole`) | refused | **refused before the effect** |
| F4 sender's access grant ended | refused | **refused before the effect** |
| F5 explicit Stop (`chat.abort`) on the receiver | refused | **refused before the effect** |
| D1 device-token operator: device removed, peer receiver | refused | **refused before the effect** |
| D2 device-token operator: device removed, child receiver | refused | refused |
| D3 / D4 device-token operator positive controls (peer / child) | refused / executes | executes / executes |
| F1 trusted-proxy operator: device pairing removed, peer receiver | refused (occurrence binding) | executes: person-bound by design |
| F1b trusted-proxy operator: device pairing removed, child receiver | executes | executes (`main` `a35b92c`: executes) |
| O1 / O2 job's own turn; job disabled / removed while running | turn cancelled, no effect | turn cancelled, no effect |

**How the refusals happen:**

- **F2–F4:** the receiver's run is aborted within about 15 ms of the revocation, before the effect is reached, with "Restart recovery operator authority changed" (F4 also logs "proof grant ended").
- **F5:** aborted with "agent run aborted".
- **In every refused case:** no turn ever reaches the third session.

**F1 / F1b:** at the effect timestamp, Bob's client was already closed, and the pairing store shows neither a paired nor a pending row for his device. Trusted-proxy ingress attaches no device token (`connect-operator-access.ts`, "Shared/proxy identity can be tokenless"). The recovery snapshot therefore carries no device, which `#166553` pins with "does not adopt an incidental paired token for tokenless trusted-proxy ingress". Child receivers on base and on current `main` behave the same.

**Timing check:** I re-ran F1 and F1b with 1 s, 5 s and 15 s between the device removal and the effect. Both execute every time, and D1 is refused every time. So this is not a timing window; the device is never checked for a person-bound source.

**Traces (sanitized excerpts, source head `64c6130`; head `c53296a` only adds a test-lines allocation file).** Each run below is one built Gateway. Lines come from the harness timeline plus the Gateway log's authority lines; IDs are shortened, prompt-cache noise and JSON payloads are trimmed. "sink" is the third session the receiver's protected `sessions_send` targets; in every refused run the sink holds only its creation message. Included: P1 on base (refused) and head (executes), F3 role change on head (aborted ~16 ms after the revoke, before release), D1 device-token device removal on head (aborted before release), and F1 trusted-proxy pairing removal on head (executes; person-bound).

### Regression tests

In `operator-run-cancellation.test.ts`:

- Ending the sender's occurrence: fails on base, passes with the fix.
- Cleaning up the sender's session: fails at the first commit, passes with the second.
- Revoking the device still stops the turn. This is the same `it.each` case in `operator-run-cancellation.test.ts`, run as a device-token operator: the sender's source carries a paired device token (`pairedOperator()`), and the case calls `invalidateGatewayDeviceRevocation` after retention. It does not cover trusted-proxy identities, which carry no device binding (see Evidence).

### Checks

- `c53296a` adds `config/test-lines-allocations/194798-receiver-continuation-authority.txt` (56, the measured net test growth) for the `test-lines` ratchet; no source change.

- `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` pass; commit hooks ran.
- Related suites: 122 files and 1,522 tests pass.
- Independent review: found one P2, the sender-session cleanup gap. It is fixed in the second commit.

### Gaps

- The model is scripted. A live model can't hold a receiver mid-turn at an exact point. I did not do a live-model positive run, because it would mean copying real provider credentials onto the proof host.
- The harness is not committed: it is about 600 lines, over the test cost budget.

### ClawSweeper blockers

1. **Inspectable authority-chain trace of a real run, including the nearest forbidden case.** See P1 versus F2–F5 and D1 above. Each run records:
   - timestamps and run IDs;
   - the occurrence finishing and the job's state afterwards (removed, rescheduled or disabled);
   - the revocation;
   - the receiver's effect, executed or refused;
   - the third session's state.

   The nearest forbidden case to P1 is the same run plus one revocation after the occurrence has ended: F2 (profile), F3 (role), F4 (grant), D1 (device-token device) or F5 (Stop). Each is refused before the effect.
2. **Revocation after continuation retention must reject before the receiver's protected effect, at the effect boundary rather than through `assertCurrent`.** F2–F5 and D1 revoke through the real Gateway methods (`users.merge`, `users.setRole`, the grant policy, `chat.abort`, `device.pair.remove`) after retention. In each, the receiver's `sessions_send` never produces a turn in the target session.
3. **Merge risk: the broader lifetime must not carry revoked sender authority into a receiver's protected effect.** It doesn't, for every revocation the authority model defines: person, role, grant, device token and Stop. The one non-revocation, a trusted-proxy browser's device pairing, is the existing person-bound model from #166553. It already applies to child receivers on `main` (F1b), and the scope is stated above.

issue.body:
Related: #193982 (node transport, merged), #194001 (Gateway node admission, merged), #194007 (Access node invites, merged), #195507 (one automatic node pairing per approved listing, merged; found by this PR's live proof)

## What Problem This Solves

Headless nodes need an owner-approved way to join an OpenClaw ID claw without a user account or a Gateway token.

## User Impact

Adds `openclaw node join <openclaw-node-link>` and sends the same link through `openclaw connect`. The node shows a six-digit code and its signed command list. The owner compares the code and approves on the Access page. After approval, the node checks that it was admitted, then connects in the foreground, or installs a user service with `--service`.

- **Discovery origin.** Set it with `--discovery-url` or reuse the one saved with the node's target; there is no production default. The origin is never derived from the claw hostname or relay URL.
- **Re-joining.** `node join` now refuses a node that is still admitted, and leaves the new invitation unused. To change a node's commands, the owner removes it on the Access page and sends a new link. Plain reconnects use `openclaw node run` or the installed service.
- **Supervision.** A foreground `node join` now runs under the packaged node supervisor, the same as `connect`. Supervisor restarts use `node run`, never the one-time link.
- **Labs preview limits.** Unix hosts and native-process workers only. Node is the qualified runtime; Bun streaming qualification is still pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

The node signs the command manifest it actually prepared, with its own local key, and Discovery only ever sees the redemption proof. Before the runner saves the target, the node checks the root, claw and hostname pins, the highest same-claw binding sequence it has seen, signed snapshot freshness, and its own listing. The first connection reuses that prepared runtime. The service is installed only after a successful first hello and a clean shutdown.

**ClawSweeper's re-enrollment finding (P2).** A membership snapshot lists node keys only; it says nothing about which invitation or description the owner approved. A node that is already admitted would therefore look approved before the owner had decided on the new invitation. The node now checks Discovery before mailing the redemption, and refuses if it is already listed. It doesn't wait on the new invitation, and it doesn't spend it.

**Accepted edge (named in code).** Suppose an earlier invitation for the same node key is still pending and the owner approves it later. That approval can also complete a newer join that is waiting. Binding completion to one specific invitation needs a signed per-invitation outcome, which doesn't exist yet and is tracked as openclaw-607; this PR adds no protocol statement. The Gateway pairs only the commands from the description the owner approved (`approveOpenClawIdNodePairing`), so this edge can't widen what the node may run. A Discovery that lies about pending state can, at most, cause the same mismatch; it can't grant access.

**Authority at admission and execution.** Gateway #194001 owns this. Admission resolves the tunnel peer against the Gateway's current authority, not Discovery's snapshot. `resolveGatewayConnectPolicyFailure` and request dispatch then re-check `isOpenClawIdTunnelPrincipalCurrent` before any work runs. A new real-Gateway test covers both cases. A node key the Gateway doesn't list (pending, or removed after the node fetched its descriptor) is refused before pairing. A live node session is closed with code 4001 on its next request once its listing is removed. Existing coverage includes `authority.nodes.test.ts`, where pending nodes don't resolve and removal closes connections, and the pairing suite's stale-principal case.

**Stored data.** This PR adds no new store, field or migration. Node config stays in SQLite `nodeHost.config` v1, as in 2026.11.2. The `openclaw-id` target shape already shipped in #193982. Existing Gateway-mode targets keep loading unchanged; only an explicit `node join` replaces the saved target. See Evidence for the upgrade check.

**Test lines.** The allocation is 542, exactly this PR's net test-line delta. Against current main the ratchet reports 32 lines of slack; that headroom was already on main and isn't allocated by this PR.

## Evidence

- **Re-enrollment regression.** `refuses re-enrollment while old membership still lists W, before spending the invite` is red against the previous enrollment source and green with the fix.
- **Focused suites.** 172 passed, 7 native-binding tests skipped, across enrollment, join, runner, connect/register CLI, node daemon, the Gateway node-pairing suite and the native node-host suite. The node launcher suite passed 15/15, including the new `["node","join"]` supervised-restart case.
- **Static checks.** `pnpm tsgo:core`, scoped oxlint and oxfmt, and `pnpm deadcode:exports` all passed with 0 entries. `loadNodeTunnelKey` is exported again because `openclaw-id-join.ts` uses it; #195338 had made it private. The mock-isolation ratchet passes; each orchestration mock in the join suite states why it is isolated.
- **Independent Astra review.** It found two P2s. The supervisor bypass is fixed. The pending-earlier-invitation edge is accepted as described above, pending openclaw-607. Neither finding bypasses Gateway enforcement.
- **Stored-data upgrade (isolated profiles, env cleared of live-Gateway variables).** 2026.10.10 configured a node host in plain Gateway mode against an isolated 2026.11.2 Gateway: it saved SQLite `nodeHost.config` v1 and paired. The PR head's `node run` with no flags then loaded that config and connected with the existing pairing (0 pending requests). The config bytes were unchanged (same hash). A failed `node join` (Discovery unreachable) left the config unchanged apart from creating the node's 0600 endpoint key, and `node run` connected again afterwards. Note: main is versioned 2026.11.1, so a 2026.11.2 → PR head run is a version downgrade and stops at the newer-config check; that is why the upgrade was seeded from 2026.10.10.
- **Exact-head CI on `7cf477a8e9e5`:** 73 passed, 52 skipped, 0 failed. Current head `eac8b7f06c2f`: CI is running.
- **Follow-up `eac8b7f` (ClawSweeper P3, after the live run):** failed descriptor or membership verification now names a recovery step. A stale membership snapshot asks the operator to have the claw owner check that the Gateway is online and connected to OpenClaw ID, then join with a new link; an invalid descriptor asks them to check `--discovery-url` with the owner. Only error strings and the stale-snapshot test assertion changed; enrollment logic didn't. The live proof below ran on `7cf477a`, and the enrollment, join and connect suites pass 46/46 at `eac8b7f`.
- **Rebase onto main (with #195507):** `git range-diff ac26a0d7f1f8..70d8109b8a56 origin/main..7cf477a8e9e5` shows all 4 commits unchanged (`=`).

### Live proof on the staging testnet (build `7cf477a`, this PR's head)

**Setup:**
- **Gateway:** an isolated Gateway on a Mac Studio, built from `7cf477a8e9e5` with its own profile, port and state, and linked as the throwaway staging claw `ocid517proof2-e61zr.crabd.xyz`. The Studio's own Gateway wasn't touched.
- **Owner:** used real Chromium against the real staging OpenClaw ID, Discovery, loader and relay. They signed in, enrolled with the recovery kit, and opened **Access** over the tunnel. This Gateway has no model configured, so the default landing goes to model setup; the harness opens the app with `?session=main`. Node admission doesn't depend on this.
- **Nodes:** ran this PR's shipped CLI on a Linux host, each in an isolated profile, with environment variables from the host's own Gateway cleared.

All 9 checks passed in one run:

| # | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Owner signs in and opens **Access**, then **Nodes**, over the tunnel | pass |
| 2 | Denied invite | Codes matched (`794-600`) and the owner selected **Deny node**. The invite reads `denied` and no node is listed. The waiting node never connected and, when cancelled, reported "no target was saved". |
| 3 | Approved invite | Codes matched (`865-003`) and the owner approved. The Gateway logged `admission allowed … path=relay` and then repeated admissions with `path=direct`. The node reported `connected … via OpenClaw ID (direct)`, and its device was auto-paired as `openclaw-id-node`. |
| 4 | A node command runs | `node.invoke system.which` over the tunnel returned `{"bins":{"sh":"/usr/bin/sh"}}` |

Headless nodes need an owner-approved way to join an OpenClaw ID claw without a user account or a Gateway token.

## User Impact

The owner compares the code and approves on the Access page. After approval, the node checks that it was admitted, then connects in the foreground, or installs a user service with `--service`.

- **Discovery origin.** Set it with `--discovery-url` or reuse the one saved with the node's target; there is no production default. The origin is never derived from the claw hostname or relay URL.
- **Re-joining.** `node join` now refuses a node that is still admitted, and leaves the new invitation unused. To change a node's commands, the owner removes it on the Access page and sends a new link. Plain reconnects use `openclaw node run` or the installed service.

- **Labs preview limits.** Unix hosts and native-process workers only. Node is the qualified runtime; Bun streaming qualification is still pending.

The node signs the command manifest it actually prepared, with its own local key, and Discovery only ever sees the redemption proof. Before the runner saves the target, the node checks the root, claw and hostname pins, the highest same-claw binding sequence it has seen, signed snapshot freshness, and its own listing. The first connection reuses that prepared runtime. The service is installed only after a successful first hello and a clean shutdown.

**ClawSweeper's re-enrollment finding (P2).** A membership snapshot lists node keys only; it says nothing about which invitation or description the owner approved. issue.body:
Related: #193993 (`openclaw node join`), #194001 (Gateway node admission and pairing)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an OpenClaw ID node that the owner removed on the Access page and then approved again with a new invitation still needs a second manual approval under **Devices** before it can connect.

## User Impact

When an owner approves a node again with a new invitation after removing it, the node pairs automatically on its next connection, the same as on its first approval. The behavior everywhere else stays the same:

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| First owner approval, first connection | pairs automatically | pairs automatically |
| A second device using the same node key and approval | manual | manual |
| Pairing removed only under **Devices** while the node is still approved | manual | manual |
| Node removed on **Access**, then approved again with a new invitation | **manual (bug)** | pairs automatically, once |
| First connection paired manually, then that pairing removed | manual | manual |

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway records that a node key has used its one automatic pairing. That record was keyed by the node key alone and deliberately survives removal, so a second owner approval of the same key could never pair automatically. The record is now keyed by the listing the owner signed: the claw, its root key, and the sequence number the node was listed at. These are the same provenance fields already stored on the node token and used to remove its pairings.

The protocol gives a node a fresh listing sequence only when the owner approves it again after it was removed. Approving a node that is still listed keeps its sequence. So a new automatic pairing always needs a new owner approval on Access.

**Security:**
- A new automatic pairing needs a new owner approval: the owner compares the six-digit code and explicitly approves.
- The commands and capabilities granted are unchanged. Only the subset the owner reviewed in that approval qualifies.
- A pairing removed under **Devices** never returns on the same listing.
- A manual approval over the tunnel still uses up that listing's automatic pairing, in the same transaction that issues its token.

**Upgrade:** there is no migration. Old records keyed by the node key alone are simply not read. They exist only on main and development builds: #194001 merged at 09:17 PST on 2026-11-08, after 2026.11.2 was published at 01:48 PST, and 2026.11.2's `dist` does not contain `devicePairing.openclawIdNode`. Accepted edge case for development builds only: after upgrading, a still-approved node listing can pair automatically once more without a new owner approval. That includes a device whose **Devices** pairing was removed by hand, or a second device on that listing if it connects before the existing device's next token issuance.

## Evidence

- **Red on main, green with the fix**, in the real-Gateway node-pairing suite (`server.auth.openclaw-id-node-pairing.test.ts`, real SQLite pairing broker):
  - New test: after removal and a new approval, the node pairs automatically once. Under that listing, a second device and a **Devices**-only removal both stay manual. On main it fails with `expected false to be true` at the re-pair.
  - Extended test: a manual pairing uses up its listing's automatic pairing, and a newly approved listing then pairs automatically. On main it fails at the re-pair.
- **Focused suites:** 17/17 passed across `authority.nodes`, the node-pairing suite, `node-principal` and the node pairing lifecycle tests.
- **Independent Astra review:** no P0–P2 findings. One P3 docs wording finding (re-approving a still-listed key keeps its listing) is fixed. It also confirmed the development-build upgrade consequence named above.
- **Static checks:** `pnpm tsgo:core`, scoped oxlint and oxfmt, `git diff --check`, the mock-exports ratchet and `pnpm deadcode:exports` (0 entries) all pass. The test-line ratchet passes against `origin/main` with an allocation of exactly 34, this PR's net test lines. The 32 lines of reported slack were already free on main.
- **Before, live staging (2026-11-08):** in #193993's live run on the staging testnet, a node was removed on Access, approved again with a new invitation and admitted over the tunnel. The Gateway then answered `device pairing required` and left a non-repair pending node request. The after evidence comes from the same live flow on a build that includes this fix and will be added here.

## What Problem This Solves

Owners need a browser flow to invite, verify, approve, and remove computers connecting through OpenClaw ID.

## User Impact

The Access page adds owner-device-only node management: create a ten-minute single-use join command, compare all six verification digits, review the node's full declared command/capability surface, then explicitly approve or deny it. Removing a node explains that it disconnects and loses its pairing. Existing pairing-only removal stays distinct from OpenClaw ID access removal.

**Stack dependency:** Gateway #194001 and protocol #193980 are merged; this PR now targets main; shipping also requires the node-host CLI in #193993. This UI-only branch does not independently provide `openclaw node join`. The CLI flags were checked against that sibling's implementation. Landing is authorized in node-stack order; no release is requested.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser signs through the existing owner-device key and keeps the secret-bearing join link inside the originating dialog. The Gateway receives only the signed capability and proof key; its configured Discovery origin and version supply command metadata. No Discovery origin means setup guidance, not a fabricated default or a copyable command. A dismissed dialog cannot be reopened by late creation completion.

The existing Access refresh/write owner and host modal shell remain authoritative. Pending approval never auto-approves; self-reported identity is labeled, sensitive commands are highlighted, and the signed request is checked against fresh membership state before submission. Nodes show the Gateway's last-seen value rather than inventing an online signal.

## Evidence

### Current restack validation (November 8)

Head: `5a4672ddd1dc61ef3dc238ebfc3e45e5582d41c5`. Base: main `21c02885fb1a51903d4c6f7f9b3893895b2c2f31`, including Gateway merge `c1b75daf79463773375988651395787efa3374ff`. - **`pnpm tsgo:core` passed.**

Related: #193980 (protocol merged into main), #193993 (enrollment follow-up), #192345 (tunnel server)

## What Problem This Solves

Headless nodes need to reach a claw through OpenClaw ID without LAN reachability, Tailscale, SSH, or a Gateway bearer token.

## User Impact

Labs transport preview: a saved OpenClaw ID target can run or reinstall a Unix node host using its locally generated iroh key. Main and worker WebSockets, desktop/portal attachment streams, bundle downloads, and workspace transfers share the same private tunnel. Existing ws/wss targets are unchanged. Enrollment remains the separate #193993 follow-up.

This preview supports Unix hosts and native-process workers, not Windows or container-isolated workers. Node is the qualified runtime. Bun streaming, relayed operation, and live node-principal enrollment are not qualified by this PR. Native prebuilt packages must be rebuilt for the added optional `keepAliveMs` API through the existing platform packaging flow; no binaries are committed or published here.

## Why This Change Was Made

The node verifies the saved ServerBinding against its claw/root/sequence pin and dials only its K_srv over `openclaw/tunnel/1`. IP transports remain enabled; the relay is a routing hint. The local key stays in a 0600 private node-state file, not config, logs, or worker descriptors. One owner-only Unix bridge (0600 socket in a fresh 0700 directory) shares that identity without distributing its secret or opening a TCP listener.

The connection owner supplies keep-alives, silent-connection probes, relay-denial backoff, and terminal membership-removal handling. Diagnostics show the logical claw target and observed route, not private socket paths. Service installation preserves the saved target and does not inherit unrelated Cloudflare/Gateway credentials. Optional Discovery routing is persisted independently, never inferred from the claw hostname or relay.

Review repairs keep desktop/portal attachment paths on that same bridge and drain queued WebSocket data before graceful close + FIN; abnormal closure still resets immediately. This fixes a reproduced finite-response truncation rather than adding another connection or buffering owner. Existing binding, framing, client, key-storage, and config owners are reused; enrollment and Gateway authorization remain separate stack stages.

## What Problem This Solves

Headless nodes need to reach a claw through OpenClaw ID without an account, a shared Gateway token, or Tailscale, while remaining separate from owner and member identities.

## User Impact

Labs-enabled claws can admit owner-approved node keys over the tunnel. The owner compares a six-digit code and reviews the node's signed, self-reported command/capability description. First pairing approves only that surface, once per key; removing the pairing keeps later requests manual. Removing or revoking the key disconnects it and retires its node-role pairing and surface without deleting unrelated roles.

This is the Gateway portion of the coordinated stack. The node-host, Discovery, and Control UI pieces are separate. It adds no Gateway-local invitation signing and has not been exercised against a live relay deployment.

## Why This Change Was Made

Node principals accept only node-role/node-mode connections, with no operator scopes, operator HTTP access, or plugin cookies. Worker WebSocket and transfer routes keep their own credentials. Existing authority serialization owns invitations and membership; the pairing worker atomically records the one-time receipt, provenance, and reviewed surface. Startup reconciliation also cleans orphaned grants when Labs is off, without deleting still-current listings.

The owner view exposes pending descriptions/codes and admitted nodes through existing authority/People APIs. Documentation marks the flow as Labs. Invite operations and owner projections live in sibling modules rather than growing the authority/service lifecycle modules beyond their limits; no new database schema or parallel authority owner is introduced.

## Evidence

Related: #192352 ## What Problem This Solves Headless nodes need an accountless, owner-approved identity and bootstrap contract before they can reach a claw through the OpenClaw ID relay and tunnel. ## User Impact This PR defines the protocol layer only; it does not yet enable node connectivity in the running product. Nodes get a separate W-only key class, never owner or member privileges. All changes revise the unshipped v1-draft in place. **Stack dependency:** this now targets `main`. Gateway, Discovery and node-host consumers follow in the implementation stack. A minimal existing Gateway consumer repair refuses accountless member-redemption mail with `audience_mismatch` through the normal settlement/acknowledgment path; valid member handling is unchanged. Test fixtures initialize the new empty draft state and preserve their concrete human-sender types. Persisted-state initialization and snapshot re-signing are included at the startup migration boundary. Full node dispatch and runtime connectivity remain in the following stack. ## Why This Change Was Made - Owner-signed `NodeInviteCap` plus a proof key registers directly at the Gateway. W-signed `NodeRedemption` proves the invite and becomes pending, admitting nothing. - Owner/R-signed `add_node` and `remove_node`, denial and peer revocation use the existing membership authority. Nodes have listing seqs, limits, inactivity clocks and pairing-cleanup events; snapshots carry `node_peer_keys`. - W-signed bearerless Discovery requests can only mail a node redemption before admission; verified admitted nodes can read the descriptor and snapshot. Relay admission includes the new snapshot list. - Strict fragment-only join links contain only the invite and claw pin/routing fields. `--discovery-url` (or deployment configuration) supplies the separate Discovery origin; clients never infer it from the hostname/relay and never weaken pin verification. The simplification pass reused owner verification, sequences, invite proof-key derivation, retention, strict schema combinators and signature transport. Node-specific lifetime enforcement leaves member policy unchanged. This remains a protocol stage: Gateway/UI/runtime enforcement follows in the stack. The owner-reviewed flow now includes a shared six-digit `nodeVerificationCode` bound to the claw, invite, W and signed `NodeDescription`. The terminal and dialog show the same code; the owner compares it and explicitly clicks Approve. Opening the dialog never approves automatically. The signed description declares display name, platform, commands and caps under strict size/count limits; it is retained with pending and approved nodes, but is not standalone authority. First-connect command/capability auto-approval is bounded to subsets of what the owner approved; additions use normal capability approval. Node invite creators default to 10 minutes; registration enforces a strict one-hour maximum. ## Evidence - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`: independent physical worktree install passed; donor checkout unchanged. - `pnpm test packages/openclaw-id-protocol --maxWorkers=1`: **169 tests / 25 files passed** after the owner-approval UX additions (4.03s Vitest, 7.38s wrapper). - Targeted strict tsgo of the protocol public barrel and affected protocol tests, plus canonical `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed. - `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json packages/openclaw-id-protocol/src`: passed, 67 files. - Package-config boundary lint also passed (66 files) after successful declaration emission; the original Gateway consumer type error is resolved. - Package format check, docs MDX check, changed-source line-cap ratchet and staged whitespace check: passed. - Test-line allocation: 565 = original 436 + exactly 40 mailbox regression lines + exactly 89 net description/code/lifetime test lines. Two fixture initialization lines use existing slack; the shared scalar is unchanged. The allocation protects forgery/class-separation and bootstrap boundaries, not test-volume growth for its own sake. - Existing claw-store and member-profile persistence tests: 8 tests / 2 files passed (89.99s Vitest including 67.5s one-time worker preparation; 96.21s wrapper). - Mailbox reader: 6 tests passed; new regression failed before the guard and passed after it. Existing callback/acknowledgment tests remain green. Final run: 86.19s Vitest including 80.55s one-time worker preparation, 94.02s wrapper; regression itself 7ms. CI timing is not yet available. - Deterministic v1-draft JSON regenerated from the vector builder; fixtures test byte-for-byte agreement. - Independent read-only review found one P2 (Discovery origin absent from link bootstrap). Verified and resolved through the explicit configured-origin/default-and-override contract, preserving the requested link fields. No other verified P0–P2 findings in the original review. A follow-up review of the small consumer repair completed but its result was unavailable; publication proceeds with coordinator approval on the original review and passing affected checks. Fresh independent read-only review of the UX delta found no verified P0–P2 findings and independently reproduced code vector `168017`. Canonical production types and strict package types (including tests), lint, format, MDX, line caps, test allocation and whitespace checks passed. Protocol boundary coverage includes forged/wrong-key and mailbox approval refusal, pending-only redemption, owner capability/sequence checks, node/human key separation in both directions, limits, denial, removal events, revocation replay, inactivity, strict links and W-signed request path binding. Deployed Gateway/Discovery enforcement and real tunnel traffic remain named integration gates for the following stack, not claims made by these tests. Stack conflict repair: rebased onto `90a2c765e10799dce65c5cffc2539b878a46f71a`, preserving both the base’s signed `protocols` and this change’s `node_peer_keys` snapshot fields. Regenerated deterministic vectors; protocol suite, canonical production typecheck, test-line ratchet and whitespace checks passed again. The range-diff contains only the combined snapshot schema context and regenerated signatures. issue.body:
Related: Linear OCF-495

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an already-approved OpenClaw ID browser must ask the owner for approval again after signing out and signing back in, even when it requests the same access.

## User Impact

User impact: returning browsers reconnect with their previously approved access. New roles, broader scopes, or a different device key still require approval. Approval prompts describe the role or scopes being requested.

OpenClaw ID Control UI browsers are managed through Access and the account menu's Your devices, rather than device removal or token revocation. Devices UI and CLI identify these browsers; `devices clear` preserves them. Nodes, native apps, ordinary browsers, and pairings with OpenClaw ID disabled keep normal device management.

## Why This Change Was Made

Sign-out revokes Gateway credentials but intentionally retains device approval and membership. The pairing planner now restores the same approved role only on the OpenClaw ID lane, bounded by live membership, connection limits and the device's approved scopes. Revoked credentials no longer widen a narrower replacement. The existing approval and credential owners retain their live-authority checks.

The existing tunnel-token binding also identifies Access-managed browsers, including tokenless browser lanes. Sign-out retains that binding; membership removal and device deletion clean it up. Accepted availability tradeoff: a custom same-origin proxy sharing one browser key between ordinary and OpenClaw ID ingress binds that key's token to its OpenClaw ID peer. This does not add authority.

## Evidence

Local test command wall times: Gateway/CLI 185 s (includes cold worker compilation), UI 8 s, supplemental HTTP/ingress 117 s, node-pairing 140 s. Exact-head CI completed; the failing UI shard ran for 694 s. The added tunnel suite completed in 31 s (19 tests); Devices and lifecycle suites passed 48 tests in the combined run, and the binding suite passed 7 tests. An earlier supplemental invocation passed its assertions but was invalidated by concurrent formatting; the reported 117 s run kept source unchanged and completed successfully.

- Rebased onto main `604aacb6cdf4df3ecf6fb5b7bf690dd58d6804c5`. The repair is still needed: main's planner excludes the revoked-token `role-upgrade` case. Two textual conflicts preserved main's CLI unknown-ID handling and keyed/accessor UI warning rows alongside this PR's changes.
- Updated the two current-main binding-owner test fixtures to implement the new cleanup contract. No restoration or membership behavior was changed by conflict resolution.
- Focused Gateway/CLI tests: 108 passed across tunnel restoration, trusted-proxy exclusion, device management, binding ownership, remote sign-out and CLI suites. UI tests: 57 passed across login feedback and device inventory. Supplemental HTTP/remote-ingress tests: 15 passed; current-main node-pairing/listing regressions: 7 passed. Core, UI and Gateway-server test typechecks passed. Type-aware lint passed for touched core/UI files and the added fixture repairs.
- [Prior isolated staging live proof at `c1c539d`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194354#issuecomment-6715102894): real Chromium owner/member sign-out and sign-in over staging ID/Discovery/relay without an approval prompt; removed-member sign-in refused with no replacement token. The throwaway claw and isolated Gateway were retired afterwards. This remains historical proof of the unchanged restoration logic, **not a final-head live run**. Later Access-management changes are covered by production-path Gateway and UI tests, not that staging run. The new tokenless cases use a real isolated Gateway and WebSocket RPC with synthetic ingress attribution and membership owners, not live external ID/Discovery/relay services.
- Test budget: 442 added test/support lines with a matching PR-owned allocation. The review repair adds a stalled-cleanup ordering assertion and two production-boundary tokenless membership cases while removing the helper-only tokenless test. The shared ceiling is unchanged.
- Exact-head review at `b6c78b319a0a` identified a real P1: device removal awaited binding cleanup before revoking connected clients. The cleanup is now inside the existing teardown protection, after synchronous client invalidation. The deferred-cleanup regression failed on `b6c78b319a0a` (zero invalidation calls while cleanup was pending) and passes with the repair; caller-retirement and worker-cleanup-failure lifecycle tests remain green.
- Tokenless production-boundary proof: with configured operator roles, a member receives no device token, appears as Access-managed, completes an allowed `health` RPC, and is refused an admin RPC. Removing its peer or reassigning that peer to another account then closes the connection before another `health` RPC can run. The initial fixture expected generic configured-role scopes; source inspection confirmed the tunnel's built-in operator policy takes precedence. The corrected test asserts that exact policy and passes both cases.
- Fresh independent Astra review covered the complete rebased diff and supplemental repairs, then separately reviewed the removal-ordering and tokenless proof delta. No remaining verified P0–P2 findings. [Exact-head hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194354#issuecomment-6698222852) at `09a3f91d12d1` found no remaining defects and accepted the proof.

Captured from the production Control UI build with a mocked Gateway connect rejection (`role-upgrade`, request `7f6e33d0…`), on main `936f38793bab` and on this branch.


### Final CI qualification

[CI run 42785043378, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42785043378) completed for `09a3f91d12d1aa81a29193c6504e5a36121a4660`. Core/changed-node tests, UI unit tests, production/test typechecks, lint, security and baseline ratchets passed. CI remains red for two independently verified inherited failures; landing uses the native inherited-failure route, not a claim that CI passed:

- [check-docs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42785043378/job/129724783224): `pnpm format:check` fails on `scripts/lib/full-release-child-reuse.mjs`, `test/scripts/full-release-receipt-recovery.test.ts`, `test/scripts/plugin-npm-cli-process.test.ts`, and `test/scripts/plugin-npm-cli-recovery.test-support.mjs`. All four blobs and formatter configuration are identical between tested merge `f1b22eb5491d` and its main parent `7f7c1a70699a`. Checking extracted main-parent bytes with the same oxfmt 0.74.0 reproduces exactly these four failures. All actual docs-content checks passed.
- [checks-ui-e2e (4/7)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42785043378/job/129724784043): the mobile/tablet/desktop thinking-argument completion cases expect `/think ultra` after Tab but receive `/think `. [Scheduled main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42782788359/job/129717133294) fails the same three cases with the same assertion at `chat-thinking-arguments.e2e.test.ts:148` (assigned to shard 5 there). The failing test, test harness, and chat-components subtree are unchanged by this PR.

The aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` failure follows those two jobs. No CI rerun or unrelated source repair was used to obtain green results.

### Live proof on the staging testnet (build `c1c539d`, this PR's head)

An isolated Gateway on a Mac Studio, with its own profile, port and state, was built from `c1c539d` and linked as a throwaway staging claw (`ocf495proof-e61zr.crabd.xyz`). Real Chromium browsers used the real staging OpenClaw ID, Discovery, loader and relay. All 13 checks passed in one run:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Owner browser signs in, enrolls with the recovery kit and reaches the Control UI over the tunnel | pass; paired as `operator`, `approvedVia: trusted-proxy`, six scopes |
| Owner chooses **Sign out of OpenClaw ID** from the account menu (issuer sign-out confirmed) | pass |
| Gateway after sign-out | operator token revoked, device row still approved |
| Owner chooses **Sign in again** on the same browser | pass; reconnected with **no device-approval prompt and no pending request**; token re-issued with the same six scopes; approved scopes unchanged |
| Owner invites the demo member as operator; member joins; owner approves | pass |
| Member signs out, then signs in again on the same browser | pass; reconnected with no prompt; token re-issued within the member's approved scopes |
| Owner removes the member while the member is signed out | pass |
| Removed member chooses **Sign in again** on the same browser and completes the OpenClaw ID login | refused with "This claw isn't in your account"; the device's token stays revoked and its `rotatedAtMs` is unchanged (**no new token**); no pending pairing request |

Afterwards the throwaway claw was retired in Discovery staging (no claw, relay-key or live-hostname rows remain), and the isolated Gateway was stopped. Its profile was backed up and then removed.

| Owner signed out | Owner back in, no prompt | Member back in, no prompt | Removed member refused |
|---|---|---|---|
| ![owner signed out](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7b365a1a-7422-491c-b7a2-03d24847115d) | ![owner reconnected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5aead449-3ee8-41aa-b7d4-3c8a674b3ca2) | ![member reconnected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/826262fc-26eb-43a5-a9bc-13336ffc904f) | ![removed member refused](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b1f5626-5e83-4900-abb4-f2157469f717) |

Unrelated observation, not caused by this PR: one earlier run hit a 28 s Gateway main-thread stall (`task=unattributed`) during a member join. The tunnel child missed its health pings and was killed and restarted, so the owner page sat reconnecting and that run failed. The stall did not recur in the final run, and it will be tracked separately.
